The Praise belongs to Allah

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verses 1–5:

﴿Al-hamd﴾: It is the description of the praised one with perfection, out of love and exaltation. This is praise (hamd): that you describe the praised one with perfection, out of love and exaltation. By our saying "out of love and exaltation" we exclude mere praise (madh), because praise does not necessarily entail love and exaltation. A person may praise someone who is not worth a fils, but in hope of some benefit or to ward off some harm. As for hamd, it is a description of perfection together with love and exaltation.

﴿Al-hamdu lillah﴾: This is a proper name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, specific to Him; it is not used to praise anyone else. It is a name for the Sacred Essence, blessed and exalted is He.

﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitab﴾: The sentence ﴿Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi anzal﴾ — is it a report, in which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to inform His servants that He is praiseworthy; or is it an instruction and guidance that we should praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for this; or both?

Both. It is a report from Allah about Himself, and it is also a guidance for us that we should praise Him, the Mighty and Majestic, for this.

﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitaba wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾: ﴿ʿAbdihi﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ). He is described with servitude (ʿubudiyyah) because he is the most devoted of mankind to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, exalted is He, described him with servitude in the state of the revelation of the Book to him, in the state of defending it, and in the state of the Night Journey (isra') with him. He, majestic and exalted, said in the state of the revelation of the Qur'an to him: ﴿He sent down to His servant the Book﴾; and in the state of defending it: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ [al-Baqarah 23]; meaning Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace; and in the state of the Night Journey with him, in His saying: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [al-Isra' 1]; meaning, at the most noble station of the Prophet (ﷺ), Allah described him as His servant. And how excellent a description it is for a person to be a servant of Allah, to the point that the lover said:

Do not call me except by "O slave of her" — for it is the most noble of my names.

And His saying: ﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitab﴾ refers to the Qur'an. It was called "al-Kitab" because it is written (yuktab), or because it is a gathering (jami'), since the root ka-ta-ba carries the meaning of "gathering"; hence it is said "al-katibah," meaning a group of horses. The Qur'an is suitable for both meanings: it is written, and it is also a comprehensive gathering; al-Kitab.

﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾: ﴿Lahu﴾ means, for this Qur'an, ﴿ʿiwajan﴾ (crookedness). Rather, it is upright; hence He said: ﴿Qayyiman﴾ (straight), and ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (ḥal) from His saying ﴿al-kitab﴾, meaning in the state of it being ﴿qayyiman﴾.

If someone says: Why did you not make it an adjective (ṣifah), since ﴿al-kitab﴾ is in the accusative and ﴿qayyiman﴾ is in the accusative?

The answer: ﴿Qayyiman﴾ is indefinite (nakirah), and ﴿al-kitab﴾ is definite (maʿrifah), and a definite noun cannot be described by an indefinite one. The meaning of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is that it is upright to the utmost degree of uprightness. Here He mentioned the negation of defect first, then the affirmation of perfection second. An example of the negation of defect?

* Student: ﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitaba wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾. The perfection is ﴿qayyiman﴾. Likewise, one should clear a place of harm and then establish perfection; hence it is said: clearing (takhliyah) comes before adorning (tahliyah). That is, before you adorn a thing, clear the place of whatever contradicts adornment, and then adorn it.

In His saying: ﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan qayyiman﴾ there is a point of caution: it is obligatory to pause at His saying ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾, because if you continued, there would be a contradiction in the speech: ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan qayyiman﴾ — how? Is crookedness upright? No. Therefore, pause: ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾, then ﴿qayyiman﴾ and so on.

What is the wisdom in the revelation of the Qur'an?

Allah explained it in His saying: ﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf 2]. The pronoun in ﴿li-yundhira﴾ may refer back to ﴿ʿabdihi﴾, and it may refer to ﴿al-kitab﴾; both are correct. The Book was sent down to the Messenger so that he might warn by it, and the Book itself warns people.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾: that is, from the side of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And ba's (punishment) means torment, as He said: ﴿And the patient in adversity and hardship and at the time of battle﴾ [al-Baqarah 177], and as in His saying: ﴿Then Our punishment came to them by night﴾ [al-A'raf 4]; meaning, a torment.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers﴾: We find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, omitted the object in ﴿li-yundhira﴾ and mentioned the object in ﴿yubashshira﴾. How then do we account for the omitted object of ﴿li-yundhira﴾?

We supply it in correspondence with ﴿yubashshira﴾, and this is one of the benefits of the science of tafsir: that a thing is known by mention of its counterpart. So, He gives good news to the believers and warns the disbelievers; and the object was omitted because what follows indicates it.

We have mentioned that the Qur'an may be explained by some of its words through others, by mentioning their context. Among this is His saying: ﴿So go forth in groups or go forth all together﴾ [al-Nisa' 71]; ﴿thubat﴾ means dispersed. What is the evidence? Then He said: ﴿or go forth all together﴾.

﴿Wa yubashshira al-mu'minina alladhina yaʿmalun al-salihat﴾: With faith there must be righteous deeds; faith alone is not sufficient, rather righteous deeds must accompany it. Hence it was said to some of the early generations (salaf): Is not the key to Paradise "There is no god but Allah"? That is, whoever brings it enters? He said: Yes, but does a key open without teeth?

The answer: No; so there must be deeds.

﴿Wa yubashshira al-mu'minina alladhina yaʿmalun al-salihat﴾. First, we ask: who are the believers?

The believers are those who believe in what must be believed in. The Messenger (ﷺ) explained what must be believed in to Jibril when he asked him about faith, and he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, both its good and its evil."

﴿Alladhina yaʿmalun al-salihat﴾: that is, they do righteous deeds. And when is a deed righteous? It cannot be righteous unless it includes two things. The first: sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second: following (mutabaʿah) the Law of Allah. Sincerity to Allah means that a person does not intend by his deed anything other than the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Hereafter. Following means that he does not depart from the Law of Allah, whether what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought or others. It is known that all laws before the mission of the Messenger are abrogated.

The opposite of sincerity is shirk, and the opposite of following is innovation (bid'ah). Therefore, innovation, however much it increases in the heart of its doer, and whatever wickedness it contains, and whatever softening of the heart it may bring, (...).

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes; because it is not conformity to the thing. Hence we say: every innovation, however much its innovator considers it good, is not accepted; rather it is misguidance, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said.

Whoever performs a deed in accordance with the Law outwardly, but there is showing-off (riya') in the heart, this is not accepted. Why?

Because of the lack of sincerity.

Therefore, two things are necessary: sincerity to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); otherwise it is not righteous. With what does He give them good news?

He said: ﴿That they will have a good reward, remaining therein forever﴾ [al-Kahf 2, 3]. ﴿Ajran﴾ means reward (thawab). Allah called the reward of deeds "ajr" because they are in exchange for work. This is from His justice, the Mighty and Majestic, that He calls the reward He bestows upon one who obeys His command "ajr," so that a person may be reassured of this reward, since it is well known that a wage (ajr) is deserved when the hired worker performs his work; He called it ajr so that the doer may be assured that he will be rewarded for it.

And His saying: ﴿Hasanan (good)﴾: another verse has mentioned something higher than this description, namely His saying: ﴿For those who did good is the best (husna) and more﴾ [Yunus 26].

And in another verse, similar to this verse: ﴿Is the reward of good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman 60]. So shall we take what implies equality or what implies the more complete?

What implies the more complete. So we say: ﴿hasanan﴾ means it is the best thing; and there is no doubt that the reward of Paradise is not matched by any other reward.

And the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Remaining therein forever﴾ means remaining in it.

﴿Abadan (forever)﴾: until when? Until there is no end: no sickness, no death, no hunger, no thirst, no heat, no cold; everything is perfect in every respect. Know that among the creed of the People of the Sunnah and the Community is that Paradise now exists and is everlasting, and that Hell now exists and is everlasting; this is the creed of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, and this is in the Qur'an. The verses of eternity regarding the companions of the right are numerous, and regarding the companions of the left, eternity is mentioned in three verses. The first? In Surat al-Nisa'.

* Student: The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged — Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa' 168, 169].

* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged — Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾. And the second verse?

* Student: In Surat al-Jinn.

* The Shaykh: No, before al-Jinn.

* Student: In Surat al-Ahzab, in the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever﴾.

* The Shaykh: In His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Ahzab 64, 65]. The third verse?

* Student: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23].

* The Shaykh: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾. And since these three verses, which are the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are an indication of eternity, it should not be said otherwise; for the poet says:

Not every dispute is considered, except a dispute that has some share of insight.

And this one has no share of it. How can the Creator, the All-Knowing, say: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, then say: there is no eternity? This is strange, among the strangest things!!

Therefore ﴿Makithina fihi abadan﴾ is evidence of what? Of the eternity of Hell. So pay attention to the principle in the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community: that Paradise and Hell are created by Allah, for Allah mentioned of Paradise ﴿prepared﴾ and mentioned of Hell ﴿prepared﴾.

Second: that they are both everlasting; neither of them perishes, nor do those in them (...).

﴿And warn those who say: "Allah has taken a son"﴾ [al-Kahf 4, 5]: this is an elaboration of what was left vague in the previous verse: ﴿And to warn those who say: Allah has taken a son﴾, such as the Christians, who said: Jesus is the son of Allah; the Jews, who said: Ezra is the son of Allah; and the polytheists, who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah; (...) males and females; and Ezra was not a prophet, but a righteous man, and the Messiah was a prophet.

Allah said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾ [al-Kahf 5]. ﴿Lahum bihi﴾: concerning what, the son or the saying? The saying. ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾: of this saying, or they have no knowledge of it, i.e., of the son. ﴿No knowledge﴾; so it is established for them: ignorance.

﴿Nor for their fathers﴾ who said things like their saying; they have no knowledge of it; there are only illusions which they took to be realities, otherwise they have no knowledge.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the phrase ﴿kabura kalimatan﴾ may cause difficulty for a student of knowledge, (...). It is said: "kabura kalimatun" (a word is great); but the answer to this is that ﴿kalimatan﴾ is a specifier (tamyiz), and the subject is omitted, and the estimate is: their statement was great as a word that comes out of their mouths, i.e., it was magnified, because it is great, God forbid, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam 90–92], meaning it is utterly impossible that He should have a son.

If someone says: Does not Allah say: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 81]?

The answer: Yes, but conditioning does not indicate the occurrence of the conditioned. ﴿If﴾: can it happen? No; we understand from other verses that it cannot be. This is like His saying to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Book﴾ [Yunus 94].

Can the Messenger doubt? No; but on the supposition of a matter that does not occur. This is like His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]; it is impossible that there be in them gods other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus it becomes clear, my brothers, that the existence of the condition does not indicate the possibility of the conditioned; rather it may be utterly impossible.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, and their fathers... grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾. Can we benefit from His saying ﴿out of their mouths﴾ that these people say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and that they do not truly believe that Allah has a son? For no intelligent person could say that Allah has a son; and how could Allah have a son, when this son of humans, you see him like us: he eats, drinks, wears clothes, and is afflicted with hunger, thirst, heat and cold?! How could he be a son?!

This is impossible; hence He said: ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾. The ﴿in﴾ here means "what" (ma).

Among the signs of the negating ﴿in﴾ is that it is followed by ﴿illa﴾: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23]; ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾; ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾ [al-An'am 7]; that is, these people say nothing but a lie. A lie is a report that contradicts reality, and truth is a report that corresponds to reality.

If someone says: "So-and-so arrived today," and he did not arrive?

* Student: It is a lie.

* The Shaykh: This is a lie, whether he knew or did not know, even if he did not know that he came. It is not as some people say: that a lie is only what is deliberate, i.e., what contradicts reality deliberately. No; even if it is not deliberate. The proof of this is the story of Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, when her husband died while she was pregnant; she gave birth a few nights after his death, then she removed the mourning garments and wore beautiful clothes, wishing to be proposed to. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak entered upon her and said to her: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." For she gave birth after her husband's death by forty nights or less or more, as was mentioned; how much of the mourning period remains?

Four months and ten days. He said: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." She put on mourning garments, then came to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and informed him of the matter. He said to her: "Abu al-Sanabil has lied." Although the man did not intend it; he thought she should observe the longer of the two waiting periods: if she remained pregnant after four months, she would remain in mourning, and if she gave birth after four months, she would remain in mourning, observing the longer of the two periods. This is undoubtedly a mere opinion, were it not for the Sunnah, it would have been the intended meaning; but the Sunnah has established that the waiting period of a pregnant woman is by giving birth, even if it is less than four months and ten days.

The evidence from the hadith: the Prophet (ﷺ) described the statement of Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak as "lying," although he did not intend it. ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾.

﴿Abadan (forever)﴾: until when? Until there is no end: no sickness, no death, no hunger, no thirst, no heat, no cold; everything is perfect in every respect. Know that among the creed of the People of the Sunnah and the Community is that Paradise now exists and is everlasting, and that Hell now exists and is everlasting; this is the creed of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, and this is in the Qur'an. The verses of eternity regarding the companions of the right are numerous, and regarding the companions of the left, eternity is mentioned in three verses. The first? In Surat al-Nisa'.

* Student: The saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged — Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Nisa' 168, 169].

* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged — Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path, except the path of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾. And the second verse?

* Student: In Surat al-Jinn.

* The Shaykh: No, before al-Jinn.

* Student: In Surat al-Ahzab, in the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever﴾.

* The Shaykh: In His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blaze, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Ahzab 64, 65]. The third verse?

* Student: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ [al-Jinn 23].

* The Shaykh: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾. And since these three verses, which are the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are an indication of eternity, it should not be said otherwise; for the poet says:

Not every dispute is considered, except a dispute that has some share of insight.

And this one has no share of it. How can the Creator, the All-Knowing, say: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, then say: there is no eternity? This is strange, among the strangest things!!

Therefore ﴿Makithina fihi abadan﴾ is evidence of what? Of the eternity of Hell. So pay attention to the principle in the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community: that Paradise and Hell are created by Allah, for Allah mentioned of Paradise ﴿prepared﴾ and mentioned of Hell ﴿prepared﴾.

Second: that they are both everlasting; neither of them perishes, nor do those in them (...).

﴿And warn those who say: "Allah has taken a son"﴾ [al-Kahf 4, 5]: this is an elaboration of what was left vague in the previous verse: ﴿And to warn those who say: Allah has taken a son﴾, such as the Christians, who said: Jesus is the son of Allah; the Jews, who said: Ezra is the son of Allah; and the polytheists, who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah; (...) males and females; and Ezra was not a prophet, but a righteous man, and the Messiah was a prophet.

Allah said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾ [al-Kahf 5]. ﴿Lahum bihi﴾: concerning what, the son or the saying? The saying. ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾: of this saying, or they have no knowledge of it, i.e., of the son. ﴿No knowledge﴾; so it is established for them: ignorance.

﴿Nor for their fathers﴾ who said things like their saying; they have no knowledge of it; there are only illusions which they took to be realities, otherwise they have no knowledge.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the phrase ﴿kabura kalimatan﴾ may cause difficulty for a student of knowledge, (...). It is said: "kabura kalimatun" (a word is great); but the answer to this is that ﴿kalimatan﴾ is a specifier (tamyiz), and the subject is omitted, and the estimate is: their statement was great as a word that comes out of their mouths, i.e., it was magnified, because it is great, God forbid, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam 90–92], meaning it is utterly impossible that He should have a son.

If someone says: Does not Allah say: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 81]?

The answer: Yes, but conditioning does not indicate the occurrence of the conditioned. ﴿If﴾: can it happen? No; we understand from other verses that it cannot be. This is like His saying to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Book﴾ [Yunus 94].

Can the Messenger doubt? No; but on the supposition of a matter that does not occur. This is like His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]; it is impossible that there be in them gods other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus it becomes clear, my brothers, that the existence of the condition does not indicate the possibility of the conditioned; rather it may be utterly impossible.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, and their fathers... grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾. Can we benefit from His saying ﴿out of their mouths﴾ that these people say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and that they do not truly believe that Allah has a son? For no intelligent person could say that Allah has a son; and how could Allah have a son, when this son of humans, you see him like us: he eats, drinks, wears clothes, and is afflicted with hunger, thirst, heat and cold?! How could he be a son?!

This is impossible; hence He said: ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾. The ﴿in﴾ here means "what" (ma).

Among the signs of the negating ﴿in﴾ is that it is followed by ﴿illa﴾: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23]; ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾; ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾ [al-An'am 7]; that is, these people say nothing but a lie. A lie is a report that contradicts reality, and truth is a report that corresponds to reality.

If someone says: "So-and-so arrived today," and he did not arrive?

* Student: It is a lie.

* The Shaykh: This is a lie, whether he knew or did not know, even if he did not know that he came. It is not as some people say: that a lie is only what is deliberate, i.e., what contradicts reality deliberately. No; even if it is not deliberate. The proof of this is the story of Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, when her husband died while she was pregnant; she gave birth a few nights after his death, then she removed the mourning garments and wore beautiful clothes, wishing to be proposed to. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak entered upon her and said to her: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." For she gave birth after her husband's death by forty nights or less or more, as was mentioned; how much of the mourning period remains?

Four months and ten days. He said: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." She put on mourning garments, then came to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and informed him of the matter. He said to her: "Abu al-Sanabil has lied." Although the man did not intend it; he thought she should observe the longer of the two waiting periods: if she remained pregnant after four months, she would remain in mourning, and if she gave birth after four months, she would remain in mourning, observing the longer of the two periods. This is undoubtedly a mere opinion, were it not for the Sunnah, it would have been the intended meaning; but the Sunnah has established that the waiting period of a pregnant woman is by giving birth, even if it is less than four months and ten days.

The evidence from the hadith: the Prophet (ﷺ) described the statement of Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak as "lying," although he did not intend it. ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾.

The Praise belongs to Allah

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verses 1–5:

﴿Al-hamd﴾: It is the description of the praised one with perfection, out of love and exaltation. This is praise (hamd): that you describe the praised one with perfection, out of love and exaltation. By our saying "out of love and exaltation" we exclude mere praise (madh), because praise does not necessarily entail love and exaltation. A person may praise someone who is not worth a fils, but in hope of some benefit or to ward off some harm. As for hamd, it is a description of perfection together with love and exaltation.

﴿Al-hamdu lillah﴾: This is a proper name of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, specific to Him; it is not used to praise anyone else. It is a name for the Sacred Essence, blessed and exalted is He.

﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitab﴾: The sentence ﴿Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi anzal﴾ — is it a report, in which Allah, glorified and exalted is He, wishes to inform His servants that He is praiseworthy; or is it an instruction and guidance that we should praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for this; or both?

Both. It is a report from Allah about Himself, and it is also a guidance for us that we should praise Him, the Mighty and Majestic, for this.

﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitaba wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾: ﴿ʿAbdihi﴾ means Muhammad (ﷺ). He is described with servitude (ʿubudiyyah) because he is the most devoted of mankind to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah, exalted is He, described him with servitude in the state of the revelation of the Book to him, in the state of defending it, and in the state of the Night Journey (isra') with him. He, majestic and exalted, said in the state of the revelation of the Qur'an to him: ﴿He sent down to His servant the Book﴾; and in the state of defending it: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ [al-Baqarah 23]; meaning Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace; and in the state of the Night Journey with him, in His saying: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [al-Isra' 1]; meaning, at the most noble station of the Prophet (ﷺ), Allah described him as His servant. And how excellent a description it is for a person to be a servant of Allah, to the point that the lover said:

Do not call me except by "O slave of her" — for it is the most noble of my names.

And His saying: ﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitab﴾ refers to the Qur'an. It was called "al-Kitab" because it is written (yuktab), or because it is a gathering (jami'), since the root ka-ta-ba carries the meaning of "gathering"; hence it is said "al-katibah," meaning a group of horses. The Qur'an is suitable for both meanings: it is written, and it is also a comprehensive gathering; al-Kitab.

﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾: ﴿Lahu﴾ means, for this Qur'an, ﴿ʿiwajan﴾ (crookedness). Rather, it is upright; hence He said: ﴿Qayyiman﴾ (straight), and ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (ḥal) from His saying ﴿al-kitab﴾, meaning in the state of it being ﴿qayyiman﴾.

If someone says: Why did you not make it an adjective (ṣifah), since ﴿al-kitab﴾ is in the accusative and ﴿qayyiman﴾ is in the accusative?

The answer: ﴿Qayyiman﴾ is indefinite (nakirah), and ﴿al-kitab﴾ is definite (maʿrifah), and a definite noun cannot be described by an indefinite one. The meaning of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is that it is upright to the utmost degree of uprightness. Here He mentioned the negation of defect first, then the affirmation of perfection second. An example of the negation of defect?

* Student: ﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitaba wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾. The perfection is ﴿qayyiman﴾. Likewise, one should clear a place of harm and then establish perfection; hence it is said: clearing (takhliyah) comes before adorning (tahliyah). That is, before you adorn a thing, clear the place of whatever contradicts adornment, and then adorn it.

In His saying: ﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan qayyiman﴾ there is a point of caution: it is obligatory to pause at His saying ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾, because if you continued, there would be a contradiction in the speech: ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan qayyiman﴾ — how? Is crookedness upright? No. Therefore, pause: ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾, then ﴿qayyiman﴾ and so on.

Allah explained it in His saying: ﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf 2]. The pronoun in ﴿li-yundhira﴾ may refer back to ﴿ʿabdihi﴾, and it may refer to ﴿al-kitab﴾; both are correct. The Book was sent down to the Messenger so that he might warn by it, and the Book itself warns people.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾: that is, from the side of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And ba's (punishment) means torment, as He said: ﴿And the patient in adversity and hardship and at the time of battle﴾ [al-Baqarah 177], and as in His saying: ﴿Then Our punishment came to them by night﴾ [al-A'raf 4]; meaning, a torment.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers﴾: We find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, omitted the object in ﴿li-yundhira﴾ and mentioned the object in ﴿yubashshira﴾. How then do we account for the omitted object of ﴿li-yundhira﴾?

We supply it in correspondence with ﴿yubashshira﴾, and this is one of the benefits of the science of tafsir: that a thing is known by mention of its counterpart. So, He gives good news to the believers and warns the disbelievers; and the object was omitted because what follows indicates it.

We have mentioned that the Qur'an may be explained by some of its words through others, by mentioning their context. Among this is His saying: ﴿So go forth in groups or go forth all together﴾ [al-Nisa' 71]; ﴿thubat﴾ means dispersed. What is the evidence? Then He said: ﴿or go forth all together﴾.

Hence it was said to some of the early generations (salaf): Is not the key to Paradise "There is no god but Allah"? That is, whoever brings it enters? He said: Yes, but does a key open without teeth?

The answer: No; so there must be deeds.

The believers are those who believe in what must be believed in. The Messenger (ﷺ) explained what must be believed in to Jibril when he asked him about faith, and he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, and the decree, both its good and its evil."

﴿Alladhina yaʿmalun al-salihat﴾: that is, they do righteous deeds. And when is a deed righteous? It cannot be righteous unless it includes two things. The first: sincerity (ikhlas) to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

The second: following (mutabaʿah) the Law of Allah. Sincerity to Allah means that a person does not intend by his deed anything other than the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Hereafter. Following means that he does not depart from the Law of Allah, whether what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought or others. It is known that all laws before the mission of the Messenger are abrogated.

The opposite of sincerity is shirk, and the opposite of following is innovation (bid'ah). Therefore, innovation, however much it increases in the heart of its doer, and whatever wickedness it contains, and whatever softening of the heart it may bring, (...).

* Student: (...).

Whoever performs a deed in accordance with the Law outwardly, but there is showing-off (riya') in the heart, this is not accepted. Why?

Because of the lack of sincerity.

He, majestic and exalted, said in the state of the revelation of the Qur'an to him: ﴿He sent down to His servant the Book﴾; and in the state of defending it: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant﴾ [al-Baqarah 23]; meaning Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace; and in the state of the Night Journey with him, in His saying: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram﴾ [al-Isra' 1]; meaning, at the most noble station of the Prophet (ﷺ), Allah described him as His servant. And how excellent a description it is for a person to be a servant of Allah, to the point that the lover said:

Do not call me except by "O slave of her" — for it is the most noble of my names.

And His saying: ﴿Alladhi anzala ʿala ʿabdihi al-kitab﴾ refers to the Qur'an. It was called "al-Kitab" because it is written (yuktab), or because it is a gathering (jami'), since the root ka-ta-ba carries the meaning of "gathering"; hence it is said "al-katibah," meaning a group of horses. The Qur'an is suitable for both meanings: it is written, and it is also a comprehensive gathering; al-Kitab.

﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾: ﴿Lahu﴾ means, for this Qur'an, ﴿ʿiwajan﴾ (crookedness). Rather, it is upright; hence He said: ﴿Qayyiman﴾ (straight), and ﴿qayyiman﴾ is a circumstantial accusative (ḥal) from His saying ﴿al-kitab﴾, meaning in the state of it being ﴿qayyiman﴾.

If someone says: Why did you not make it an adjective (ṣifah), since ﴿al-kitab﴾ is in the accusative and ﴿qayyiman﴾ is in the accusative?

The answer: ﴿Qayyiman﴾ is indefinite (nakirah), and ﴿al-kitab﴾ is definite (maʿrifah), and a definite noun cannot be described by an indefinite one. The meaning of ﴿qayyiman﴾ is that it is upright to the utmost degree of uprightness. Here He mentioned the negation of defect first, then the affirmation of perfection second. An example of the negation of defect?

* The Shaykh: ﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾. The perfection is ﴿qayyiman﴾. Likewise, one should clear a place of harm and then establish perfection; hence it is said: clearing (takhliyah) comes before adorning (tahliyah). That is, before you adorn a thing, clear the place of whatever contradicts adornment, and then adorn it.

In His saying: ﴿Wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan qayyiman﴾ there is a point of caution: it is obligatory to pause at His saying ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾, because if you continued, there would be a contradiction in the speech: ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan qayyiman﴾ — how? Is crookedness upright? No. Therefore, pause: ﴿wa lam yajʿal lahu ʿiwajan﴾, then ﴿qayyiman﴾ and so on.

What is the wisdom in the revelation of the Qur'an?

Allah explained it in His saying: ﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf 2]. The pronoun in ﴿li-yundhira﴾ may refer back to ﴿ʿabdihi﴾, and it may refer to ﴿al-kitab﴾; both are correct. The Book was sent down to the Messenger so that he might warn by it, and the Book itself warns people.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him﴾: that is, from the side of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And ba's (punishment) means torment, as He said: ﴿And the patient in adversity and hardship and at the time of battle﴾ [al-Baqarah 177], and as in His saying: ﴿Then Our punishment came to them by night﴾ [al-A'raf 4]; meaning, a torment.

﴿To warn of a severe punishment from Him and to give good news to the believers﴾: We find that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, omitted the object in ﴿li-yundhira﴾ and mentioned the object in ﴿yubashshira﴾. How then do we account for the omitted object of ﴿li-yundhira﴾?

We supply it in correspondence with ﴿yubashshira﴾, and this is one of the benefits of the science of tafsir: that a thing is known by mention of its counterpart. So, He gives good news to the believers and warns the disbelievers; and the object was omitted because what follows indicates it.

We have mentioned that the Qur'an may be explained by some of its words through others, by mentioning their context. Among this is His saying: ﴿So go forth in groups or go forth all together﴾ [al-Nisa' 71]; ﴿thubat﴾ means dispersed. What is the evidence? Then He said: ﴿or go forth all together﴾.

﴿Wa yubashshira al-mu'minina alladhina yaʿmalun al-salihat﴾: With faith there must be righteous deeds; faith alone is not sufficient, rather righteous deeds must accompany it. Hence it was said to some of the early generations (salaf): Is not the key to Paradise "There is no god but Allah"? That is, whoever brings it enters? He said: Yes, but does a key open without teeth?

The answer: No; so there must be deeds.

The second: following (mutabaʿah) the Law of Allah. Sincerity to Allah means that a person does not intend by his deed anything other than the Face of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the Hereafter. Following means that he does not depart from the Law of Allah, whether what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought or others. It is known that all laws before the mission of the Messenger are abrogated.

Because of the lack of sincerity.

Not every dispute is considered, except a dispute that has some share of insight.

﴿Nor for their fathers﴾ who said things like their saying; they have no knowledge of it; there are only illusions which they took to be realities, otherwise they have no knowledge.

And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam 90–92], meaning it is utterly impossible that He should have a son.

If someone says: Does not Allah say: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 81]?

The answer: Yes, but conditioning does not indicate the occurrence of the conditioned. ﴿If﴾: can it happen? No; we understand from other verses that it cannot be. This is like His saying to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Book﴾ [Yunus 94].

Can the Messenger doubt? No; but on the supposition of a matter that does not occur. This is like His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]; it is impossible that there be in them gods other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus it becomes clear, my brothers, that the existence of the condition does not indicate the possibility of the conditioned; rather it may be utterly impossible.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, and their fathers... grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾. Can we benefit from His saying ﴿out of their mouths﴾ that these people say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and that they do not truly believe that Allah has a son? For no intelligent person could say that Allah has a son; and how could Allah have a son, when this son of humans, you see him like us: he eats, drinks, wears clothes, and is afflicted with hunger, thirst, heat and cold?! How could he be a son?!

This is impossible; hence He said: ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾. The ﴿in﴾ here means "what" (ma).

Among the signs of the negating ﴿in﴾ is that it is followed by ﴿illa﴾: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23]; ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾; ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾ [al-An'am 7]; that is, these people say nothing but a lie. A lie is a report that contradicts reality, and truth is a report that corresponds to reality.

If someone says: "So-and-so arrived today," and he did not arrive?

* Student: It is a lie.

* The Shaykh: This is a lie, whether he knew or did not know, even if he did not know that he came. It is not as some people say: that a lie is only what is deliberate, i.e., what contradicts reality deliberately. No; even if it is not deliberate. The proof of this is the story of Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, when her husband died while she was pregnant; she gave birth a few nights after his death, then she removed the mourning garments and wore beautiful clothes, wishing to be proposed to. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak entered upon her and said to her: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." For she gave birth after her husband's death by forty nights or less or more, as was mentioned; how much of the mourning period remains?

Four months and ten days. He said: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." She put on mourning garments, then came to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and informed him of the matter. He said to her: "Abu al-Sanabil has lied." Although the man did not intend it; he thought she should observe the longer of the two waiting periods: if she remained pregnant after four months, she would remain in mourning, and if she gave birth after four months, she would remain in mourning, observing the longer of the two periods. This is undoubtedly a mere opinion, were it not for the Sunnah, it would have been the intended meaning; but the Sunnah has established that the waiting period of a pregnant woman is by giving birth, even if it is less than four months and ten days.

The evidence from the hadith: the Prophet (ﷺ) described the statement of Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak as "lying," although he did not intend it. ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾.

* The Shaykh: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger – indeed, for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever﴾. And since these three verses, which are the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are an indication of eternity, it should not be said otherwise; for the poet says:

Not every dispute is considered, except a dispute that has some share of insight.

And this one has no share of it. How can the Creator, the All-Knowing, say: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, then say: there is no eternity? This is strange, among the strangest things!!

Therefore ﴿Makithina fihi abadan﴾ is evidence of what? Of the eternity of Hell. So pay attention to the principle in the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah and the Community: that Paradise and Hell are created by Allah, for Allah mentioned of Paradise ﴿prepared﴾ and mentioned of Hell ﴿prepared﴾.

Second: that they are both everlasting; neither of them perishes, nor do those in them (...).

﴿And warn those who say: "Allah has taken a son"﴾ [al-Kahf 4, 5]: this is an elaboration of what was left vague in the previous verse: ﴿And to warn those who say: Allah has taken a son﴾, such as the Christians, who said: Jesus is the son of Allah; the Jews, who said: Ezra is the son of Allah; and the polytheists, who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah; (...) males and females; and Ezra was not a prophet, but a righteous man, and the Messiah was a prophet.

Allah said: ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾ [al-Kahf 5]. ﴿Lahum bihi﴾: concerning what, the son or the saying? The saying. ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾: of this saying, or they have no knowledge of it, i.e., of the son. ﴿No knowledge﴾; so it is established for them: ignorance.

﴿Nor for their fathers﴾ who said things like their saying; they have no knowledge of it; there are only illusions which they took to be realities, otherwise they have no knowledge.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers. Grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾: the phrase ﴿kabura kalimatan﴾ may cause difficulty for a student of knowledge, (...). It is said: "kabura kalimatun" (a word is great); but the answer to this is that ﴿kalimatan﴾ is a specifier (tamyiz), and the subject is omitted, and the estimate is: their statement was great as a word that comes out of their mouths, i.e., it was magnified, because it is great, God forbid, as the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿The heavens are almost torn apart from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son﴾ [Maryam 90–92], meaning it is utterly impossible that He should have a son.

If someone says: Does not Allah say: ﴿Say: If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [al-Zukhruf 81]?

The answer: Yes, but conditioning does not indicate the occurrence of the conditioned. ﴿If﴾: can it happen? No; we understand from other verses that it cannot be. This is like His saying to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who read the Book﴾ [Yunus 94].

Can the Messenger doubt? No; but on the supposition of a matter that does not occur. This is like His saying: ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya' 22]; it is impossible that there be in them gods other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Thus it becomes clear, my brothers, that the existence of the condition does not indicate the possibility of the conditioned; rather it may be utterly impossible.

﴿They have no knowledge of it, and their fathers... grave is the word that comes out of their mouths﴾. Can we benefit from His saying ﴿out of their mouths﴾ that these people say with their tongues what is not in their hearts, and that they do not truly believe that Allah has a son? For no intelligent person could say that Allah has a son; and how could Allah have a son, when this son of humans, you see him like us: he eats, drinks, wears clothes, and is afflicted with hunger, thirst, heat and cold?! How could he be a son?!

This is impossible; hence He said: ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾. The ﴿in﴾ here means "what" (ma).

Among the signs of the negating ﴿in﴾ is that it is followed by ﴿illa﴾: ﴿You are only a warner﴾ [Fatir 23]; ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾; ﴿This is nothing but evident magic﴾ [al-An'am 7]; that is, these people say nothing but a lie. A lie is a report that contradicts reality, and truth is a report that corresponds to reality.

If someone says: "So-and-so arrived today," and he did not arrive?

* Student: It is a lie.

* The Shaykh: This is a lie, whether he knew or did not know, even if he did not know that he came. It is not as some people say: that a lie is only what is deliberate, i.e., what contradicts reality deliberately. No; even if it is not deliberate. The proof of this is the story of Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah, may Allah be pleased with her, when her husband died while she was pregnant; she gave birth a few nights after his death, then she removed the mourning garments and wore beautiful clothes, wishing to be proposed to. Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak entered upon her and said to her: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." For she gave birth after her husband's death by forty nights or less or more, as was mentioned; how much of the mourning period remains?

Four months and ten days. He said: "You will not marry until four months and ten days have passed over you." She put on mourning garments, then came to the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, and informed him of the matter. He said to her: "Abu al-Sanabil has lied." Although the man did not intend it; he thought she should observe the longer of the two waiting periods: if she remained pregnant after four months, she would remain in mourning, and if she gave birth after four months, she would remain in mourning, observing the longer of the two periods. This is undoubtedly a mere opinion, were it not for the Sunnah, it would have been the intended meaning; but the Sunnah has established that the waiting period of a pregnant woman is by giving birth, even if it is less than four months and ten days.

The evidence from the hadith: the Prophet (ﷺ) described the statement of Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak as "lying," although he did not intend it. ﴿They say nothing but a lie﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 6:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then perhaps you would destroy yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message.﴾ [al-Kahf 6]. ﴿Then perhaps﴾: the address is to the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him.

﴿Destroy yourself﴾ means ruin yourself. This applies to the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him: when they did not respond to him, he would grieve intensely and his chest would be constricted, to the point that he nearly perished. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, consoled him and made clear to him that he bears no responsibility for this. He said: ﴿Then perhaps you would destroy yourself﴾. ﴿Destroy﴾ means ruin.

﴿Over them﴾ means following their traces, in hope that they would return if they turned away.

﴿If they do not believe in this message﴾: the one referred to is the Quran.

﴿With grief﴾ (asafan) is an object of purpose (maf'ul min ajlihi), and the word governing it is ﴿destroy﴾ (bakhi').

The meaning: perhaps you would destroy yourself out of grief if they do not believe in it, although the Messenger, may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him, bears no responsibility for their traces. What is the Messenger's duty? His duty is delivery (al-balagh). ﴿Your duty is only to deliver the message﴾ [Al 'Imran 20]. He delivers, and the reckoning is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Likewise, his heirs among the scholars after him: their duty is delivery, while guidance is in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So do not grieve over them: ﴿and do not be in distress over what they plot﴾.

It is well known that a person certainly grieves when people do not accept the truth, but the situation when people do not accept the truth is of two kinds: one kind grieves because it was not accepted (for himself), and another kind grieves because the truth was not accepted. Which of these is praiseworthy?

The second, because the first, when he calls, calls for himself, whereas the second, when he calls, calls to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Call to the way of your Lord﴾ [al-Nahl 125].

But if a person says: I grieve when my words are not accepted, because they are true; and for this reason, if the truth becomes clear to me contrary to my view, I adopt it. Is he praiseworthy or not?

He is praiseworthy, but he is not like the other, who has no concern except accepting the truth, whether it comes from himself or from someone else. This is more complete in manners, O brothers.

﴿Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it﴾ [al-Kahf 7]. When you look in the Quran, you will find that Allah, the Exalted, puts the law (shar') before creation: ﴿The Most Merciful (1) taught the Quran (2) created man﴾ [al-Rahman 1-3]. Reflect on the verses in this sense and you will find that Allah begins with the laws before mentioning creation and what relates to it, because created things were subjected only to fulfill obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat 56], and He said: ﴿It is He who created for you all that is on the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah 29]. So the important thing is carrying out obedience to Allah. Reflect on this subtle point until it becomes clear to you that the creation of the world and its existence is only through carrying out the law of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 7–8:

He says: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾. ﴿Made (ja'ala)﴾ means "transformed/rendered" (bi-ma'na sayyara). The verb ja'ala comes with the meaning of "created" (khalaqa) and also with the meaning of "rendered" (sayyara). If it takes one object, it means "created," such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And He made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am 1], where ja'ala means khalaqa. If it takes two objects, it means "rendered" (sayyara), such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ [az-Zukhruf 3], meaning: We rendered it in the language of the Arabs. I only drew attention to this because the Jahmiyyah say that ja'ala means "created" in all contexts, and they say the meaning of ﴿Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an﴾ is "We created it." But we say: (...) ja'ala, if it takes one object, it means "created," and if two objects, it means "rendered."

He said: ﴿Indeed, We have made what is upon the earth an adornment for it﴾. Here, does "ja'ala" mean "created" or "rendered"?

It means "rendered." The first object is ﴿what﴾, and the second object is ﴿an adornment for it﴾. ﴿What is upon the earth﴾ — God made it an adornment for the earth. This is related to the fact that people are attached to something: do they attach themselves to this adornment, or do they attach themselves to the Creator? People divide into two categories: some are attached to the adornment, and some are attached to the Creator. Listen to the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, explaining this: ﴿So he was of those who went astray (175). And had We willed, We could have raised him thereby﴾ [al-A'raf 175–176] — to where? To high ranks.

﴿But he inclined toward the earth﴾ — he leaned toward it and became content with it ﴿and followed his desire. So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾. May Allah protect us and you.

So He made for them the adornment to test people, and whether this adornment is among what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created and brought into being, or among what man has made, such as lofty, ornamented palaces, it is an adornment; yet the latter is man's handiwork. The earth with its mountains, rivers and plants is also an adornment from Allah, Exalted is He. When Allah sends down water upon it, it stirs, swells, and brings forth every lovely pair that delights the one who looks upon it. This is an adornment from Allah, Exalted is He.

﴿That He may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾. ﴿That He may test them﴾ means: that We may test them.

﴿Which of them is best in deed﴾. The pronoun refers to the creation. Here He said ﴿best in deed﴾ and did not say "most in deed," because what counts is the best, not the most. On this basis, if a person prays four rak'ahs with weak certainty, and another prays two rak'ahs with strong certainty and following of the Sunnah, which is better?

The second is better and more excellent, because what counts is the excellence and perfection of the deed, in sincerity and following of the Sunnah.

In some acts of worship, lightening is preferable, such as the two rak'ahs of Fajr for example. If a person says: "I love to prolong, I love to recite in the bowing, in the prostration, in the standing, and in the sitting," and another says: "I love to lighten," which is better?

The second is better. Therefore, when we see a common person prolonging the two rak'ahs of Fajr, we should ask: are these two rak'ahs the Fajr sunnah or the greeting of the mosque?

If they are the greeting of the mosque, then his matter is his own. If they are the two rak'ahs of Fajr, we say: No, it is better to lighten them.

Regarding fasting, the Prophet ﷺ permitted his Ummah to continue (wisal) until dawn, meaning not to break the fast except after suhur, and he encouraged them to break the fast without waiting for sunset. Two men fasted: one whose fast extended to suhur, and the second who broke his fast as soon as the sun set. Which is better?

The second, without doubt. The first, although it is not forbidden, is permissible but not prescribed (mashru'). It is permissible, but be mindful of this.

﴿Which of them is best in deed﴾. Therefore you find the Prophet ﷺ encouraging the following of funerals in worship, yet funerals would pass by him and he would not follow them; he encouraged us to fast one day and break the next, yet he himself did not do this, he did not fast one day and break the next. Rather, at times he prolonged the fast until it was said that he never broke it. And the reverse. All of this indicates what was most pleasing to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and most beneficial for his heart.

﴿That He may test them as to which of them is best in deed﴾. ﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust﴾ [al-Kahf 8]. The condition of the earth with its palaces, trees and plants: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will turn it into bare dust, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast"﴾ [Ta-Ha 105], meaning a mighty blast. For this reason it came indefinite; that is, a mighty blasting. He will make it ﴿a level plain﴾ [Ta-Ha 106], ﴿in which you will not see crookedness or unevenness﴾ [Ta-Ha 107]. Let every one beware. Glory be to Allah.

So this earth, my brother, do not let your heart be attached to it; it is passing, it will become as if it had never flourished yesterday, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿as if it had not flourished yesterday﴾ [Yunus 24].

﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust﴾. Reflect now on ﴿And indeed, We will﴾: in it there are two emphatics, "inna" and the "lam," and then it came as a nominal sentence indicating continuous power.

﴿And indeed, We will make what is upon it into barren dust﴾. When the Resurrection comes, where are the palaces? No palaces, no mountains, no trees. The earth will be like one smooth stone, with nothing in it: no plants, no buildings, no trees, nor anything else.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 9:**

﴿Or do you think﴾ [Al-Kahf: 9] (*am*) here is *munqati'ah* (disjunctive, introducing a new topic), so it means (*bal*, "rather").

And ﴿you thought﴾ means (*zanantu*, "I supposed").

﴿that the companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder﴾ [Al-Kahf: 9]. Here He used *am* as a disjunctive particle, which carries the sense of a question, in order to draw the soul to listen to the story, because it is truly a wonder. This story is a wonder!

﴿the companions of the Cave﴾: *al-Kahf* is the cave in the mountain.

And ﴿al-Raqim﴾ means (*al-marqum*), i.e., "the inscribed," because their story was written on this cave from beginning to end.

﴿were among Our signs a wonder﴾ [Al-Kahf: 9]. ﴿Were﴾ means that the companions of the Cave and the Inscription were among the signs of Allah. Are they cosmic signs or legislative ones? They are among Allah's cosmic signs.

﴿a wonder﴾ means an object of amazement and astonishment, because these were seven with a dog. They disliked the polytheism that the people of their town were upon, and they set out heading towards Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wishing to save themselves from what their townspeople were upon.

﴿They were seven, and the eighth was their dog﴾ [Al-Kahf: 22]. So they took refuge in this cave, and by good fortune for them, this cave had an entrance that faced neither east nor west. Glory be to Allah, the Mighty! For if it had faced east, the sun would have consumed them at its rising, and if it faced west, it would have consumed them at its setting. But it faces between east and west, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And you would see the sun, when it rose, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it set, passing them on the left while they were in a spacious area within it﴾ [Al-Kahf: 17], and this will come, Allah willing.

Ibn 'Uthaymin said, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding the verse: "The Most High said: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾. Here the story begins. Accordingly, ﴿when﴾ (idh) is connected to an omitted element whose estimated meaning is: 'Remember when the youths took refuge.' The disbelievers of Quraysh had asked the Prophet ﷺ about their story, and he, peace and blessings be upon him, had not read any book, so he would not know it. [Allah says]: ﴿And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾ [al-'Ankabut 48]. So he promised them, and Allah fulfilled the promise to him.

He said: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave.﴾ The fata (youth) is the young man full of strength and resolve.

* A student: Are Paradise and Hellfire existing now?

* The Shaykh: The Messenger ﷺ said: "He saw 'Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i dragging his intestines in the Fire, and he saw in the Fire the woman who was punished because of a cat she had imprisoned, and he saw in the Fire the owner of the hooked staff." Do you know the mihjan? With a nun: a staff with a heated head. The owner of the hooked staff was a man who, when pilgrims passed by him in Makkah, would snatch their goods with this hooked staff; if the owner of the goods was not attentive he would walk off, and if he noticed he would pass by. This is ... of people, and he was like that, so the Messenger ﷺ informed that he is punished in the Fire of Hell. ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing – We will make him taste a painful punishment﴾ [al-Hajj 25].

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: If he is not qualified to be emulated, such as a student of knowledge who is also a worshipper of Allah, there is no harm in it. But if he is not one who (...) acts... it is not valid; or others say he is a learned man, but he does not have strength in worship.

Allah the Most High says: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾, meaning the cave in the mountain.

﴿Took refuge﴾ means they sought shelter in it. From what? From their people, fleeing from them out of fear that they would suffer what those people had suffered. ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾. And ﴿the youths﴾, as we said, is the plural of (fata), and the fata is the strong young man.

﴿So they said: Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy and prepare for us from our affair right guidance﴾ [al-Kahf 10]. They took refuge with Allah.

﴿Grant us﴾ means give us.

﴿From Yourself﴾ means from Your presence.

﴿Mercy﴾ means that You show mercy to us through it. This is like the Prophet ﷺ's words to Abu Bakr, with the supplication he had taught him: "O Allah, I have wronged myself greatly, and none forgives sins except You, so forgive me with a forgiveness from You."

He says: ﴿And prepare for us﴾: "prepare" means "make for us." Preparing something means readying it so that it is ready and devoted to acting upon it.

﴿Prepare for us﴾ means: make easy for us from our affair right guidance. Rushd (right guidance) is the opposite of ghayy (error); meaning: make our situation conform to what is correct.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 11:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We struck upon their ears in the cave﴾ [al-Kahf 11]. ﴿So We struck upon their ears﴾ means: We put them into a deep sleep. You know that sleep is of two kinds: light sleep, which does not prevent hearing, and for this reason (...) when sleep first comes upon you, you hear those around you; but when you sleep a deep sleep (...). For this reason He said: ﴿So We struck upon their ears﴾, meaning: such that they could not hear.

﴿in the cave, for years counted⦆ means: a counted number. Its explanation will come in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾ [al-Kahf 25].

﴿Then We raised them up⦆ and that was by waking them from sleep. Allah called waking from sleep "raising" (ba'th), because sleep is a form of death (wafah). Allah the Exalted said: ﴿It is He who takes you back to Himself at night, and knows what you have committed by day; then He raises you up therein﴾ [al-An'am 60], meaning: by day. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾ [al-Zumar 42], He takes them in their sleep.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 12:

In this regard, [Allah] said: ﴿Then We awakened them﴾, meaning, We roused them, ﴿that We might know which of the two parties was most precise in calculating the period they had stayed﴾, ﴿that We might know﴾. There may be a difficulty here: does Allah not know that?

* Student: No.

* Shaykh: But know that such an expression is meant to convey two things.

The first thing: the knowledge of seeing, manifestation and witnessing, i.e., "so that We may see." It is well known that knowledge of what will happen is not like knowledge of what has happened, is it not so?

* Student: Indeed.

* Shaykh: Yes, it is so, because Allah's knowledge of a thing before it occurs is knowledge that it will occur, but after it occurs it is knowledge that it has occurred.

The second matter: the knowledge that entails reckoning (hisab) is what is meant in the verse. How do we know, [in the sense of] a knowledge that entails recompense? Like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will surely test you until We know those who strive among you and the patient﴾ [Muhammad 31]. He knows this before He tests us; He has known who is obedient and who is disobedient. But this does not entail either reward or recompense. So the meaning becomes: "that We may know" in the sense of manifestation and witnessing, and the knowledge of manifestation and witnessing is not like the knowledge of what will be.

The second: knowledge that entails reckoning. As for the certainty of the occurrence of the known thing with respect to Allah, there is no difference between what He knew would occur and what He knew had occurred; all are the same. As for us, it is true that we know what will occur through the report of the Truthful one, but our knowledge of that is not like our knowledge of it when we witness it with our own eyes. For this reason the authentic hadith says: «The report is not like seeing with one's own eyes» (ليس الخبر كالمعاينة).

﴿that We might know which of the two parties was most precise in calculating the period they had stayed﴾ [al-Kahf 12]. ﴿al-hizbayn (the two parties)﴾ means the two groups.

﴿aḥṣā (most precise)﴾ means more exact in reckoning; it is not a past-tense verb, but an elative noun (ism tafḍil).

﴿ayyu al-hizbayni aḥṣā (which of the two parties was most precise)﴾ means most accurate.

﴿limā labithū amadā (the period they had stayed)﴾ means the duration they had remained; for they disputed among themselves about their matter, saying: ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Kahf 19]. Then people after them also differed: how long did they stay? ﴿that We might know which of the two parties was most precise in calculating the period they had stayed﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 13:**

﴿We relate to you their story with truth.﴾ [al-Kahf: 13] Indeed, the Speaker is excellent in truthfulness, knowledge, eloquence, and clarity, because the speech of Allah, blessed and exalted, includes knowledge, truthfulness, eloquence, and good intention. These are four qualities. His speech, mighty and majestic, is based on knowledge. His speech is also based on truthfulness. His speech is at the utmost level of eloquence. His intention in this speech is the best intention; through what He says, He wants to guide His servants.

So, ﴿We relate﴾: the stories told by Allah, mighty and majestic, are the most beautiful and the best of stories, because they proceed from knowledge. The second quality is truthfulness. The third is that they are expressed in the most eloquent, clearest, and most explicit words. Nothing is clearer than the speech of Allah, except for one whom Allah has caused to deviate in his heart and who says: ﴿This is nothing but the myths of the ancients.﴾

The fourth is intention. Allah, mighty and majestic, did not intend by what He relates to us that we should go astray, nor by what He has decreed upon us that we should go astray. Rather, He intended that we be guided and that we take lessons.

As for His saying ﴿We relate﴾: if someone asks, "Is 'We' referring to one or to a group?"

The answer: It refers to a group. Is that correct?

Student: No.

Shaykh: It refers to one, but there is no doubt that He, may He be exalted, is among the greatest of the great. In the Arabic style, when a single speaker refers to himself with a plural form, it signifies glorification. It is well known that no one is greater than Allah, mighty and majestic. For this reason, when kings or leaders wish to issue decrees, what do they say? "We, so-and-so and so-and-so, command such-and-such." Therefore, all plural pronouns attributed to Allah, mighty and majestic, are intended to express glorification.

﴿We relate to you their story with truth﴾: that is, We relate to you and tell you about it.

﴿Their story﴾: that is, their news.

﴿With truth﴾: that is, with truthfulness that corresponds to reality.

﴿Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord﴾: ﴿youths﴾ means young men, but they had strength of resolve and strength of faith.

﴿And We increased them in guidance﴾: Allah, mighty and majestic, increased them in guidance, because Allah, exalted, increases in guidance those who seek guidance. Whenever you act upon knowledge, Allah increases you in guidance; that is, Allah increases you in knowledge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 14:

﴿And We strengthened their hearts﴾ [Al-Kahf: 14]. That is: We made them firm, and We gave them a bond (ribat) of steadfastness; because all their people were opposed to them, and opposing one's people requires firmness, especially since they were young men, and a young man may be influenced by his father, who says to him: "Disbelieve!" But Allah bound their hearts and made them firm. O Allah, make us firm, O Lord of the worlds.

﴿And We strengthened their hearts﴾ means: We made them firm and strengthened them.

﴿When they stood up﴾ means: among their people, teaching monotheism (tawhid).

﴿And said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾ and they did not care for anyone. They were like the magicians of Pharaoh. What did they say? ﴿They said: We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us and over Him who created us. So decide whatever you are going to decide﴾. Decide what you want.

﴿You decide only regarding this worldly life﴾ [Ta-Ha: 72]. The world is entirely passing and ending, whether your life in it is long or short, and every person must face one of two things: either old age or death, and the end of old age is death. For this reason the poet says:

"There is no pleasure in life as long as its delights are clouded
By remembrance of death and old age."

Whenever a person remembers that he will die, whether his life is long or short, life is not pleasant for him. But it is one of Allah's blessings, Mighty and Majestic, that people forget this matter. Yet among those who forget it, some forget it by occupying themselves with obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and some forget it by occupying themselves with the world, and there is a difference between the two.
* * *
The saying of the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿When the youths took refuge in the cave﴾. What is meant by "youths" (fityah) here? That is, what is the meaning of fityah?
* A student: It is the young man complete in his strength and resolve.

* The Shaykh: Yes, well done.

His saying: ﴿So We sealed their ears﴾, and He did not say "We put them to sleep," as an indication of the depth of their sleep, and that they could not hear anything. A person whose sleep is light hears, and whenever someone makes a sound he hears it; but these did not hear.

His saying: ﴿We raised them up﴾. What is derived from it?

* A student: That sleep is called death (wafah).

* The Shaykh: That sleep is death. Is there anything in the Qur'an that indicates this explicitly?

* A student: Yes, the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is He who takes you back to Himself at night, and knows what you have committed by day; then He raises you up therein﴾ [Al-An'am: 60].

* The Shaykh: Well done, may Allah bless you.

His saying: ﴿That We might know which of the two parties was better at reckoning the period they had remained﴾. Is it not the case that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, knew that before it occurred?

* A student: Allah is capable of knowledge..

* The Shaykh: The answer is yes, or no?

* A student: He is knowing.

* The Shaykh: He is knowing. Then how did He say ﴿That We might know﴾, when it is well known that the lam here indicates purpose (ta'lil)?

* A student: (...) It is said: knowledge of manifestation and observation, or that it is knowledge that results in recompense.

* The Shaykh: That is, knowledge upon which recompense is based. But in other verses this second explanation may not hold. ﴿Which of the two parties﴾: what are they?

* A student: The two parties are these youths, or those who came upon them.

* The Shaykh: Either the youths or their people who came upon them; but the youths are closer, because Allah will say later: ﴿A speaker among them said: How long have you remained? They said: We have remained a day or part of a day. They said: Your Lord knows best how long you have remained﴾ [Al-Kahf: 19]. I think we have arrived at His saying: ﴿And We strengthened their hearts﴾.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾. ﴿We strengthened their hearts﴾ means: We made them firm and strengthened them, as if something had been bound upon them.

﴿When they stood up﴾ means: when they stood, that is, among their peoples, disassociating themselves from what those peoples were upon.

﴿Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, and not the lord of so-and-so and so-and-so. Rather, He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth; He, glorified and exalted, is the Owner, the Creator, and the Governor of the heavens and the earth. For the Lord, which is one of the names of Allah, means the Creator, the Owner, the Governor; the Lord of the heavens and the earth. The seven heavens and the earth likewise are seven, as the texts have established, and there is no need to mention them, since they are known, praise be to Allah.

﴿We will never call upon any god besides Him; for then we would have uttered an enormity﴾. ﴿We will never call upon﴾ is a calling of request, and not a calling of worship. ﴿Any god﴾ other than Him. So they affirmed lordship (rububiyyah) and affirmed divinity (uluhiyyah).

As for lordship, they said: ﴿Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾; and as for divinity, they said: ﴿We will never call upon any god besides Him﴾, that is, other than Him, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿For then we would have uttered an enormity﴾. ﴿For then we would have uttered﴾: this sentence is emphasized by three emphases: the lam, qad, and the oath indicated by the lam. And His saying ﴿then﴾ means: if we called upon a god other than Him.

﴿We would have uttered an enormity﴾, that is, a saying that deviates and goes far into disbelief. And they spoke truly: if they had called upon a god other than Allah, they would have said this deviating saying that goes far into disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 15:

﴿These our people have taken gods besides Him.﴾ [Al-Kahf 18:15] They point to their viewpoint in isolating themselves from their people.

They said: ﴿These our people have taken﴾, i.e., have made (ṣayyarū).

﴿gods﴾ [ālihah], besides Him, gods they worshipped besides Allah.

﴿Why do they not bring for them a clear authority?﴾ Here, ﴿Why not﴾ [lawlā] means (hallā, "why did they not"). Lawlā has several meanings in the Arabic language, and this is not the place to mention them, but here it means (hallā), just like His saying: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ [An-Nur 24:13], i.e., why did they not bring.

﴿Bring for them﴾ means for these gods; that is, for their being gods and for their being worshipped. So two things are demanded of them: that they establish that these are gods, and that they establish that worshipping them is right. Both matters are impossible.

﴿Why do they not bring for them a clear authority?﴾ And His saying ﴿a clear authority﴾ [sultān bayyin]. Sultān is everything through which a person has power (sulṭah); anything that has power through it is a sultān. It may mean proof, as in: ﴿You have no authority for this﴾ [Yunus 10:68]. It may mean strength and dominance, as in His saying: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾ [An-Nahl 16:100], meaning Satan. And it may mean argument and evidence, as here, and as we mentioned a moment ago.

﴿A clear authority﴾ means a manifest argument by which they would have power. Is the answer possible or not?

It is not possible. For this reason they said: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ The fa' is for consequence, and (man) is an interrogative meaning negation; that is, no one is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah. Know that when the interrogative is given the meaning of negation, it gains an added benefit: it carries the sense of challenge, because bare negation does not indicate challenge. If you say, "Zayd did not stand," there is no challenge in it. But when you say: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ it is a challenge, as if you were saying: tell me, or produce for me anyone more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah.

His saying ﴿more unjust﴾ means: more severe in injustice than one who fabricates a lie against Allah by attributing a partner to Him and other things. Anyone who fabricates a lie against Allah, no one is more unjust than him. If you lied about a person, that would be injustice; if you lied about someone higher than him, that would be a greater injustice than the first. So when you fabricate a lie against Allah, there is no injustice above it. For this reason He said: ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾

If someone says: We find that Allah says ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ and He says ﴿And who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them?﴾ [Al-Baqarah 2:114], and "more unjust" [aẓlam] appears in two places, and aẓlam indicates the superlative, so how is this reconciled?

We say: the reconciliation is that it is a superlative within the very meaning in which it occurs. For example, ﴿Who is more unjust than one who prevents the mosques of Allah﴾ means: no one is more unjust in preventing than one who prevents the mosques of Allah from having His name mentioned in them. And in the other, the lie: which is more unjust, the lie against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?

The superlative here is relative to the meaning for which the verse is brought, not an absolute superlative, because if it were absolute, there would be a kind of contradiction.
