So do not seek the truth by any path other than the path of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for the truth is from Allah.

﴿So whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾. The imperative in His words ﴿and whoever wills, let him disbelieve﴾ is for threat, not for permission, and not for obligation. Rather, it is for threat, just as a person threatens another by saying: "Do such-and-such," or "If you are truthful, then do such-and-such." This is supported by His words: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire, its enclosure will surround them﴾, meaning: whoever disbelieves, the Fire has been prepared for him.

His words ﴿for the wrongdoers﴾ refer to the disbelievers, and the evidence for this is His words ﴿let him disbelieve﴾.

If someone asks: Is disbelief called wrongdoing? The answer: Yes, as the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 254]. And no one is more wrongdoing than the one who sets up a partner with Allah, while He is the One who created him, sustained him and provided for him.

﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire, its enclosure will surround them﴾. ﴿Surround them﴾ means: the Fire surrounds them. ﴿Its enclosure﴾ means what is around it; that is, the Fire has encompassed them, and we seek refuge in Allah, so they cannot escape from it to the right or to the left. ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces; wretched is the drink﴾. That is, the people of the Fire, may Allah protect me and you from it, when they become severely thirsty, and that is due to eating the Zaqqum or otherwise, are given relief with this water, water like molten brass. You say: "like the sediment of olive oil"; that is, its dregs or the like, which is a repulsive sight that souls do not accept, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And he is given to drink of festering water, which he gulps down but scarcely can swallow﴾, i.e., like pus, ﴿which he gulps but can hardly swallow﴾ [Ibrahim 17].

﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces﴾. I seek refuge in Allah: when it is brought near them, it roasts them and their faces fall off, because they are scorched, and we seek refuge in Allah, from the intense heat of this water. When it reaches their intestines, it cuts them apart, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And they are given to drink boiling water, which cuts their intestines to pieces﴾ [Muhammad 15]. How great is the pain and suffering of those whose intestines are cut from within; yet despite that, they are cut and restored like skins: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins﴾ [An-Nisa 56]. Allahu akbar, glory be to the One who is capable of everything! In an instant this process is continuous: whenever they are roasted, they are replaced; whenever the intestines are cut, they are quickly reconnected.

The Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿They will be relieved with water like molten brass, which scalds the faces﴾. ﴿Wretched is the drink﴾: this is a disparagement of this drink, and ﴿wretched﴾ is a past-tense verb used to express blame: wretched is the drink, their drink, we seek refuge in Allah. ﴿And wretched is the resting place﴾; that is, how evil is their resting place and what they lean upon. The murtafaq is what a person reclines upon of a dwelling; it may be good or it may be bad. In Paradise: ﴿How good a resting place﴾; in the Fire: ﴿How evil a resting place﴾.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of anyone who does good work.﴾ [Al-Kahf 30] This is from the style of the Qur'an: whenever Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions the people of the Fire, He mentions the people of Paradise. This is part of the meaning of His saying: ﴿oft-repeated (mathani)﴾ [Az-Zumar 23], meaning that meanings, states and attributes are repeated within it, so that a person combines fear and hope in his journey to his Lord. The discussion of His saying ﴿those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ has already preceded.

﴿Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of anyone who does good work.﴾ What one would expect is that He say: "Indeed, We do not allow their reward to be lost." But He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿the reward of anyone who does good work﴾, to explain the cause of the reward of these people, which is that they did good work. ﴿Is the reward for good [anything] but good?﴾ [Ar-Rahman 60]. This is in terms of meaning. As for the verbal aspect, it is that the verse-endings (ru'us al-ayat) are harmonious and matching; for if He had said "Indeed, We do not allow their reward to be lost," the verse-endings would have differed.

﴿Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of anyone who does good work.﴾ And how is good work achieved? It is by two things. The first: sincerity (al-ikhlas) to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The second: following (al-mutaba'a) the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

And there is no concealing what this noble verse contains of exhortation to doing good work.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 31:

﴿Those, for them are Gardens of Eden﴾ [al-Kahf: 31]. The one referred to by ﴿those who believed and did righteous deeds﴾: ﴿for them are Gardens of Eden﴾. And "al-Jannat" (the gardens) is the plural of "jannah" (garden), which is the abode that Allah the Exalted has prepared for His friends; in it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. And "al-'Adn" (Eden) means "residence" (al-iqamah); that is, gardens of residence, ﴿they will not desire any transfer from them﴾ [al-Kahf: 108], meaning they will not desire any change away from them.

Among the completeness of bliss is that each one of them does not see that anyone is more blessed than he. Among the completeness of misery for the people of the Fire is that each one of them does not see anyone who is more severely punished than he. But these do not see that anyone is more blessed than they, because if they saw that, their bliss would be disturbed, since they would imagine that theirs was less.

The statement of the Exalted and Majestic: ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾. What is the meaning of this construction, ﴿And they remained in their cave three hundred years and added nine﴾?

* Student: Refuting those who claim..

* Shaykh: I mean, why was the verse not: "And they remained in their cave three hundred years and nine years"?

* Student: To refute the Jews, because they claimed that this number is found in the Torah: the number three hundred and nine.

* Shaykh: Wrong.

* Student: Because they said: this is the difference between the solar and lunar calendars, Shaykh (...).

* Shaykh: No, that is also a mistake.

* Student: We said: the two meanings are one, or the two styles are one, but from the saying of Allah..

* Shaykh: That is, "three hundred years and nine years" means "three hundred years and added nine."

* Student: But Allah the Exalted said that — and Allah knows best — to match the endings of the verses.

* Shaykh: The endings of the verses, ﴿and added nine﴾, good.

Some scholars hold that His saying ﴿three hundred years﴾ is reckoned by solar years, and ﴿and added nine﴾ is reckoned by Gregorian years. What do you say?

* Student: We said: this statement is not correct, because the number of months with Allah is by the lunar year.

* Shaykh: Yes, because the number that is considered in reckoning time is the lunar months. What is your evidence?

* Student: ﴿Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve in the Book of Allah, the day He created the heavens and the earth; of them four are sacred﴾ [al-Tawbah: 36].

* Shaykh: Good.

* Student: ﴿They ask you about the crescents﴾ [al-Baqarah: 189].

* Shaykh: ﴿They ask you about the crescents. Say, they are measures of time for the people and for the Hajj﴾. Good. A third verse?

* Student: The saying of Allah Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is He who made the sun a shining light and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the reckoning﴾ [Yunus: 5].

* Shaykh: Well done, may Allah bless you, excellent.

His saying: ﴿Say, Allah is most knowing of how long they remained﴾. Some exegetes have used this clause as evidence that His saying ﴿and they remained﴾ is the speech of the People of the Book; i.e., they said: "and they remained." What is your response?

* Student: The answer is that we say: this is the speech of Allah Mighty and Majestic..

* Shaykh: That His saying ﴿and they remained﴾ is the speech of Allah. Then how did He say: ﴿Say, Allah is most knowing of how long they remained﴾?

* Student: (...) Allah Mighty and Majestic.

* Shaykh: To emphasize what? The previous sentence stated that they remained three hundred years and added nine, then He said: ﴿Say, Allah is most knowing of how long they remained﴾, and He, glorified and exalted, has already informed us that they remained three hundred years and added nine.

His saying: ﴿and He does not share His command with anyone﴾. Which of the two commands is meant: the cosmic (kawni) or the legislative (shar'i)?

* Student: The cosmic and the legislative.

* Shaykh: The two commands are intended. As for the cosmic, no one can change the command of Allah; as for the legislative, one may contravene the command of Allah, but he is not authorized to do so. So the negation is a negation of its legitimacy. Good, may Allah bless you.

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Lord﴾. Does it have two meanings?

* Student: ﴿And recite what has been revealed to you from the Book of your Lord﴾, meaning..

* Shaykh: Recitation as reading.

* Student: Recitation of verbal reading, and recitation of meaningful reading (following).

* Shaykh: Yes, that is: following. ﴿Recite﴾ means: recite it verbally, and also follow it; because the follower is said to "talā" (follow) someone, meaning he followed him.

His saying: ﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them﴾. What is its meaning?

* Student: That is: do not look at others.

* Shaykh: Do not look at others. Is this prohibition restricted?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: By what?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: By His saying: ﴿desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾. May Allah bless you.

What do we benefit from His saying: ﴿and do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance﴾?

* Student: A person should be present of heart..

* Shaykh: At the remembrance of Allah. It indicates that presence of heart is necessary when remembering Allah Mighty and Majestic. Are people now afflicted with this heedlessness?

* Student: Many.

* Shaykh: Many, well done. Especially when a person is in prayer, for Satan dominates him to make his heart heedless of the remembrance of the prayer in which he is engaged.

Does the verse ﴿And whoever wills, let him disbelieve; indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers﴾ indicate that disbelief is wrongdoing?

* Student: His saying, glorified and exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose enclosure surrounds them﴾ indicates it.

* Shaykh: After His saying ﴿let him disbelieve﴾. Do you have a verse indicating that the disbeliever is a wrongdoer?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: What is it?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾..

* Shaykh: ﴿And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾. May Allah bless you.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. What is the benefit of His saying: ﴿whose enclosure surrounds them﴾? This is an addition; why did He not suffice with saying "it surrounds them"?

* Shaykh: Yes, its meaning: that the Fire has a enclosure (surādiq), which is what surrounds it, encompassing these people, and this is more emphatic than merely encompassing them, because this enclosure surrounds both the Fire and the people of the Fire.

* Student: When Allah Mighty and Majestic mentions a statement or something and then remains silent about it, it is as if it is approval. Among such is His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿They will say, "They were three, the fourth of them was their dog,"﴾ and in His saying: ﴿Those who prevailed over their affair said, "We will surely take over them a place of worship,"﴾ it is known that this is prohibited, and yet Allah remained silent about it, and did not..?

* Shaykh: No, He did not remain silent; it came in the Sunnah that it is reprehensible (munkar). It may be said that in their law it was not prohibited. Did not the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, inform us, saying: "You will surely follow the ways of those before you"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3456), and Muslim (2669/6) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id.]]? He informed of it and did not forbid it, but the prohibition of it came in other texts.

* Student: The saying of Allah ﴿Make them see and hear﴾ — to what does it refer?

* Shaykh: ﴿Make them see﴾: we told you, this is an expression of wonder; that is: how clear His sight is and how acute His hearing!

* Student: ﴿We have made his heart heedless of Our remembrance﴾, what is meant by ﴿Our remembrance﴾?

* Shaykh: ﴿Our remembrance﴾ has two interpretations: ﴿of Our remembrance﴾ meaning of His remembering us, or ﴿of Our remembrance﴾ meaning of the reminder We sent down, which is the Qur'an, as Allah Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9].

* Student: (...)?

* Shaykh: No, we said the verse includes both this and that; it includes both matters.

* Student: (...) of His remembrance?

* Shaykh: Of us; that is, he mentions with his tongue but his heart is heedless, and this is the condition of many people today.

* Student: Your Eminence, in the previous lesson, when the people found them, the people of the People of the Cave, when they found them, did they find them after..? Because they disputed about them and built over them a mosque on their graves; that is, their rulers commanded them to build a mosque over their graves. Does that mean they found them after they had died?

* Shaykh: Yes, after they had died.

* Student: May Allah be good to you. In His saying: ﴿Indeed, if they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you or return you to their religion﴾, can it be taken from it that compulsion is not an excuse?

* Shaykh: It is not apparent, because these people may be mentioning a description of reality: that this or that will happen.

Allah Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Those, for them are Gardens of Eden; beneath them rivers flow﴾. (Al-anhar, "the rivers") is the plural of (nahr, "river"), and they are of four kinds, which Allah the Exalted mentioned in Surah Muhammad, ﷺ, He said: ﴿The likeness of Paradise which the righteous have been promised: in it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to drinkers, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. Here He said ﴿beneath them﴾, and in another verse He says ﴿beneath them﴾ [beneath it], and the meaning is one; for if the rivers flow beneath their trees and palaces, then they flow beneath them without doubt.

﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾. ﴿They will be adorned therein﴾ means: in these gardens. ﴿with bracelets﴾: some said that (min, "from") here is extra, based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver﴾ [al-Insan: 21], so "min" is extra. But this view is weak, because "min" is not added in affirmative sentences, as Ibn Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Alfiyyah:

"It is added in a negation or what resembles it, governing an indefinite noun, like (mā li-bāghin min mafar)."

And when this view is invalidated, then "min" is either explanatory (bayaniyyah), because bracelets are made of what? Of silver, of iron, of gold, of emerald? We do not know, so "min" is what? Explanatory. ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets﴾ [al-Kahf: 31]: it is either partitive (tab'id), meaning they will be adorned with some bracelets, because many great bracelets are distributed among them, so "min" is partitive, meaning some bracelets; that is, each of them is adorned with some of these bracelets, and then there is no difficulty.
﴿of gold﴾: this "min" is explanatory, explaining that the bracelets are of gold. But do not think that the gold in Paradise is like the gold of this world, differing greatly. Allah, blessed and exalted, said in a hadith qudsi: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived," [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3244), and Muslim (2824/2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]] and if it were like the gold of this world, the eye would have seen it, ﴿of gold﴾.

﴿They will wear green garments of fine silk﴾: sundus is what is thin of brocade and silk. ﴿They will wear green garments﴾, and He specified them as green because green is the most restful color for the eye; there is beauty in it, and it gives rest to the eye of the beholder. And ﴿of fine silk﴾.

His saying: ﴿and brocade﴾: this is what is thick of brocade; so sundus is thin brocade and istabraq is thick brocade.

﴿Reclining therein on thrones﴾: ﴿reclining﴾ is a state of the statement ﴿Those, for them are Gardens of Eden﴾; that is, while they are reclining therein. Reclining indicates ease of the soul and tranquility.

﴿on thrones﴾: plural of arīkah, and the arīkah is a kind of cushion on which one reclines. It was said that the arīkah is a small tent covered with beautiful cloth, resembling what they call a kiosk; that is, each of them reclines on this, so it is a small canopied chamber in which there are couches on which they recline.

﴿How excellent the reward, and how good a resting place!﴾: this is an expression of praise, praising this Garden and the bliss in it. There is praise for this Garden in two respects: that it is an excellent reward and that it is a good resting place. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of Paradise on that Day will have a better abode and a finer place of rest﴾ [al-Furqan: 24].

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And present to them the parable of two men﴾ [al-Kahf 18:32]. ﴿Present﴾ means: make and set forth. ﴿To them﴾ means: to the disbelievers, from Quraysh and others. ﴿A parable﴾ is the object of (idrib). This parable is explained by His words: ﴿two men﴾. On this basis, ﴿two men﴾ is an appositive (ʿatf bayan), serving as an explanation of the parable. ﴿We granted one of them﴾; that is, one of the two men, ﴿two gardens of grapevines, and We surrounded them with palm trees, and We placed between them cultivated crops﴾. Most of what is in the two gardens is grapevines, the borders of the two gardens are palm trees, and what is between them is crops. Thus there is in them fruit and sustenance from grain and the fruit of the date palm.

Ibn 'Uthaymin, Commentary on the Noble Qur'an, on Surah al-Kahf, verse 33:

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And We made between them a field of crops (32). Both gardens yielded their produce﴾ [al-Kahf 33]. He did not say "they both yielded their produce" because in (kilta) it is permissible to observe either the wording or the meaning. Both have been combined here, meaning the observance of both wording and meaning, in the verse of the poet:

Both of them, when the racing between them grew intense, have stopped, and both their nostrils are swollen.

It refers to two horses that raced. He says "kilaahumaa" (both of them), meaning both horses. "When the racing between them grew intense" means the competition. "Have stopped" means they halted. "Both their nostrils are swollen" means they are puffed up, because with the intensity of running the horses' nostrils swell. The evidence is "kilaahumaa ... qad aqla'aa" (both of them ... have stopped), where he did not say "qad aqla'a" (has stopped). And "wa kilaa anfayhimaa raabin" (both their nostrils are swollen), where he did not say "raabiyaan" (swollen, dual). So the line observes both meaning and wording. Here, in ﴿Yielded its produce﴾, what kind of consideration is it?

Student: The wording.

Shaykh: The wording. ﴿Yielded its produce﴾, meaning its fruit. ﴿And did not wrong anything from it﴾, meaning it did not diminish. ﴿And We caused a river to gush forth between them﴾: there was a river running between the two gardens. If you imagine the scene, you will picture a magnificent sight: two gardens containing every element of sustenance, grapes and what? And palm trees and crops. Then between them this flowing river.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 18, verse 34:

﴿And We caused a river to gush forth amidst them﴾ [al-Kahf: 33, 34], ﴿and he had fruit﴾. ﴿He had﴾ means one of the two men. ﴿He had fruit﴾ means he had produce beyond what these two gardens yielded. ﴿So he said to his companion while he was conversing with him﴾, in speech, the two of them trading words. ﴿I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾. He boasted over him in two things. First: abundance of wealth. Second: the might of his clan and tribe. This is why he said ﴿mightier in men﴾. So he boasted over him with wealth and lineage.

﴿I am greater than you in wealth and mightier in men﴾. Does he say this out of boasting or out of recounting the blessings of God?

* Students: Boasting.

* The Shaykh: He says it out of boasting, as shown by the punishment that befell him, and God knows best.

* * *

Also, to match the rhyme endings of the verses (ra'us al-ayat, the rhyming endings of verses).

His saying: ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold﴾. Al-asawir (bracelets) is the plural of siwar, or as-wira, and "asawira" is the plural of siwar. Yes.

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: And what is the siwar?

* The student: What a woman wears (...).

* The Shaykh: No. Does that mean that bracelets are worn in Paradise only by women?

* The student: It is what a person wears on his hand.

* The Shaykh: Yes, what one adorns oneself with on the hand.

In fact, God the Mighty and Majestic mentioned for them bracelets of gold, silver and pearls, meaning three kinds. When they are all combined on a person's forearm, they are among the most complete in appearance and delight.

His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And set forth for them a parable﴾. Is this the subject of today's lesson?

* A student: ﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself﴾.

* The Shaykh: Yes. The saying of God, exalted be He: ﴿And set forth for them a parable: two men﴾. Is this parable real or hypothetical? That is, did this actually happen, or is it a thing God set forth as a parable? I think we did not address this, but now we will. Some scholars said it is a hypothetical parable (mathal taqdiri), like His saying, blessed and exalted: ﴿And Allah sets forth an example: two men, one of whom is dumb﴾ [al-Nahl: 76], and His saying: ﴿Allah sets forth an example: a man belonging to associates in dispute﴾ [al-Zumar: 29], and similar to these. So it is a hypothetical parable and not a real event. However, the context, with its exchange of argument and response, indicates that it is a real, actual parable. ﴿Two men﴾: one of them whom God blessed in this world, and the other who did not have the like of it. With what did the owner of the two gardens boast?

* A student: With wealth and authority.

* The Shaykh: With wealth and what?

* The student: With wealth and authority.

* The Shaykh: With wealth and the second, what?

* The student: Honor.

* Another student: The tribe, Shaykh. He is from a tribe...

* The Shaykh: Meaning, with wealth and kinsmen.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And he entered his garden﴾ [Al-Kahf 35], meaning one of the two men. ﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself﴾. His saying ﴿entered his garden﴾, although He had said ﴿We had made for one of them two gardens﴾, may mean the genus (i.e., gardens in general), or it may mean one of the two gardens, the greater of the two being the one he entered. ﴿While he was wronging himself﴾ is a circumstantial clause (jumlah ḥāliyyah), meaning: and the state he was in was that he was wronging himself. And how did he wrong himself? He wronged himself by disbelief, as will become clear.

﴿He said, "I do not think that this will ever perish"﴾, meaning: I do not think that it will ever pass away or cease to exist. He was impressed by it, by its strength, the beauty of its appearance and other things, to the point that he forgot that the whole world passes away and that it does not remain for anyone. ﴿He said, "I do not think that this will ever perish"﴾ out of his admiration for it.

Then he added to that: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾ [al-Kahf 36]. He denied the Resurrection, God forbid, because if his garden is not going to perish, then he says: "Moreover, I will not perish either, and there is neither death nor resurrection." ﴿I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾, and what is meant by the Hour is the Hour of Resurrection.

﴿And even if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a final destination﴾. ﴿Even if I am returned﴾ means on the assumption that the Hour should occur and I am returned to God. ﴿I will surely find better than this as a final destination﴾, that is, a place of return. It is as though he is saying: since God has bestowed His favour upon him in this world, He must bestow it upon him in the Hereafter as well. This is faulty analogy, because bestowing blessings in this world does not necessarily mean that a person will be blessed in the Hereafter, nor does a person's not being blessed in this world mean he will not be blessed in the Hereafter. There is no necessary connection between this and that. Rather, the disbelievers are given ease in this world, and their good things are hastened to them in their worldly life, but in the Hereafter they will be punished.

So ﴿even if I am returned to my Lord﴾ presents no difficulty. Some people say: how can this be, when he has denied the Resurrection? The answer is: it is by way of supposition, meaning, "If I am returned, I will find something better than this." This is like the saying of the Blessed and Exalted in Surat Fussilat: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless. And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I will have the best with Him."﴾ [Fussilat 49-50]. This is similar to this, for they analogised the matter of the Hereafter with the matter of this world: ﴿I will surely find better than this as a final destination﴾.

He said to him, while he was arguing with him (﴿قَالَ لَهُ صَاحِبُهُ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ﴾), that is, debating with him in speech. ﴿Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you as a man?﴾ He reminded him of his origin. The hamza here is for denial (lil-inkar).

﴿Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust⁠—﴾ As for His saying ﴿created you from dust﴾, it is because Adam, the father of mankind, was created from dust. As for ﴿from a sperm-drop﴾, it is because the children of Adam are created from a sperm-drop. The meaning is as if he is saying: He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you as a man, is capable of what? Of the resurrection (al-ba'th) which you deny.

﴿Then fashioned you﴾ means: made you proportionate (adalaka) and made you a man. This interrogative is undoubtedly for denial. Can we also take it to express wonder (lil-ta'ajjub)? It can be for both denial and wonder, meaning: how can you disbelieve in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then fashioned you as a man? Yes. And it is derived from this that one who denies the resurrection is a disbeliever, and there is no doubt about this, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Those who disbelieved claim that they will never be resurrected﴾ [al-Taghabun 7].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 38:

﴿But as for me, He is Allah, my Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 38]. The origin of ﴿lakinna﴾ is "lakin ana" (but I). The hamzah of "ana" was dropped for ease of pronunciation, and the first of the two consecutive nuns (the sukun nun of "lakin") was assimilated into the second, open nun, so it became ﴿lakinna﴾. The question is whether it is read with the alif both in continuous recitation (wasl) and when pausing (waqf), or with the alif only when pausing.

On this there are two readings. Some scholars said: you read it with the alif, ﴿lakinna huwa Allahu rabbi﴾, both in continuous recitation and when pausing. Others said: if you pause and say ﴿lakinna﴾, you pause there, and then it has the alif; but if you run the words together (idraj), it is without the alif, so you say ﴿lakinna huwa Allahu rabbi﴾. Thus both are valid recitations.

﴿lakinna huwa Allahu rabbi﴾: ﴿huwa Allahu rabbi﴾ is like the words of the Most High: ﴿Huwa Allahu ahad﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1]. On this basis, (huwa) is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-sha'n), meaning: the matter is that Allah, the Most High, is my Lord, and I do not associate anyone with my Lord. This is like the words of the son of Adam to his brother Qabil: ﴿Innama yataqabbalu Allahu mina al-muttaqin﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 27], meaning: you disbelieved, but as for me, I take pride in my faith and believe in Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

The Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 39:

﴿And why, when you entered your garden, did you not say, "What Allah wills [is so]; there is no power except in Allah"?﴾ [al-Kahf: 39] Meaning: why did you not say, ﴿when you entered your garden﴾, that is, at the time of your entering it, ﴿"What Allah wills [is so]; there is no power except in Allah"﴾, so that you would leave the matter entrusted to whom? To Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And His saying ﴿What Allah wills﴾ has two possible readings:

The first: that ﴿mā﴾ is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul), the predicate of an omitted subject, its implied meaning being: "This is what Allah willed."

The second: that ﴿mā﴾ is a conditional particle (sharṭiyyah), ﴿shāʾa Allāh﴾ is the conditional verb, and its response (jawāb) is omitted, the implied meaning being: "Whatever Allah wills, it comes to be."

﴿There is no power except in Allah﴾: meaning, the entrusting of power to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for He alone possesses absolute power, all of it. Meaning: this garden did not come into being by your own power, nor by your own will, but by the will and power of Allah. When a person is pleased with something of his wealth, he should say, "What Allah wills [is so]; there is no power except in Allah," so that the matter is entrusted to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and not to his own strength and power. It has been reported in a narration (athar) that whoever says this about something of his wealth that pleases him, he will not see in it anything disliked.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children (39). Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ [al-Kahf: 39–40]. ﴿In⁠﴾ here is a conditional particle (ḥarf sharṭ), and its verb (taraniy, "you see me") is the conditional verb; the nūn is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāyah), and the yāʾ is omitted for lightness; the original is "in tarāni." ﴿anā⁠﴾ ("I") is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position (lā maḥalla lahu min al-iʿrāb).

﴿less than you in wealth and children (39). Perhaps my Lord will give me⁠﴾: meaning, if you belittle me for being less than you in wealth and less than you in children, and I am not like you in the might of numbers (ʿizzat al-nafar), ...

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 40:

﴿Then it may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾ to the end of the verse. The clause ﴿Then it may be that my Lord﴾ is the answer of the condition. Regarding his saying ﴿Then it may be that my Lord﴾, is "ʿasā" here for hope (tarajji) or for expectation (tawaqquʿ)? There are two possibilities.

The first possibility: it is for hope, and that this man prayed that Allah would give him something better than his garden, and that He would send upon his garden a calamity (ḥusbān) from the sky, because he (the rich man) had belittled him and humiliated him, so he prayed against him with the same kind of wrong that he had done to him. There is no blame upon a person for praying against his oppressor with the same thing that he wronged him with.

The second aspect: he prayed against him so that this boastful man would come to know his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and would abandon admiration for wealth. This is in his own interest. So it is as if he prayed that Allah would give him what would make him superior to him, something better than his garden, and that He would destroy this garden until this one who boasted of his garden and the might of his people would know that the matter belongs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. So it is as if he prayed against him with what would harm him, for a benefit that is what? It is greater: that a person should know himself and return to his Lord is better for him than that he should boast of his wealth and take pride in it. This is if we take ʿasā to be for hope.

It may also be that ʿasā is for expectation and not for hope. The meaning is: if you see this, then it is expected that Allah, the Exalted, will remove from me what you reproached me with, and will remove from you what you boast of. Whatever the case, the matter has happened, either as a response to his supplication or as the fulfilment of his expectation.

﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children (39). Then it may be that my Lord will give me something better than your garden, and send upon it﴾, upon what? Upon his garden ﴿a calamity from the sky, so that it becomes a barren ground, slippery (ṣaʿīdan zalaqan)﴾. The meaning of ḥusbān here is what destroys it, such as thunderbolts, or another punishment.

As for his saying ﴿from the sky﴾, the sky is specified because what comes from the earth may be repelled, for if we suppose that torrents of rain and sweeping floods came, they could be repelled, and burning fires that advance and burn what is before them could be repelled, but from the sky it is difficult.

﴿So it becomes a barren ground, slippery﴾: ﴿ṣaʿīdan﴾ means that there is no vegetation in it, and ﴿zalaqan﴾ means that water has flooded it until it became slippery.

﴿Or its water will become sunken, so that you cannot seek it﴾ [al-Kahf: 41]. This is the opposite of slippery, meaning that no water remains in it. So he supplicated for something that would remove this garden, either by water that floods it until it becomes what?

* Student: Crushed stubble (...).

* Shaykh: No, ﴿a bare, slippery ground﴾. And either by water sinking away with no irrigation in it, as His saying: ﴿Or its water will become sunken, so you cannot seek it﴾. Both are destruction and devastation. Floods destroy the produce, and the water sinking so deep into the bottom of the earth that we cannot seek it also destroys the produce.

﴿Or its water will become sunken, so you cannot﴾: ﴿ghawran﴾ (غَوْرًا) means "sunken" (ghā'ir, غائر). It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) used in the sense of an ism al-fā'il (active participle). ﴿So you cannot seek it﴾ (﴿فَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَبًا﴾). So what happened after this expectation, or after this supplication?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 42:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And his fruit was encompassed (by ruin)﴾ [al-Kahf 18:42]. Encompassed by the ruin of whose fruit? The owner of the two gardens, so the two gardens were destroyed. ﴿So he began to turn his palms over (in regret) over what he had spent upon it, while it lay fallen on its trellises, and he said﴾, and so on to the end of the verse. He began to turn his palms over out of remorse. You know that when a person regrets, he turns his palms over: "What happened? What was it that was?" ﴿Over what he had spent upon it﴾, and this indicates that he had spent a great deal on it. ﴿While it lay fallen﴾, we seek refuge in Allah, ﴿on its trellises﴾. "Fallen" (khawiyah) means withered and collapsed. ﴿On its trellises﴾: the plural of 'arsh, or 'arish, which is that which is placed so that the branches of grapevines and other plants can spread over it. ﴿While it lay fallen on its trellises, and he said: "Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord."﴾

But he repents only after the time has passed: ﴿"Oh, I wish I had not associated anyone with my Lord."﴾ However, regret after the time has passed does not benefit. What benefits is the one who hears the story: whoever hears the story will benefit from it. As for the one upon whom it has befallen, it will not benefit him, because the time has already passed.

"Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And he had no company to help him against Allah, nor was he able to defend himself﴾ [al-Kahf 18:43]. Allahu Akbar! The one who used to boast of it said: ﴿I have more wealth than you and greater strength in men﴾. But it did not benefit him; his wealth did not protect him from the punishment of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and he could not defend himself by his own means. Thus he lost what he used to boast of, because he—and we seek refuge in Allah—disbelieved and argued with the believer, and was punished with this punishment."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿There, protection belongs to Allah, the True.﴾ [Al-Kahf 18:44]. ﴿هُنَالِكَ الْوَلَايَةُ﴾ has two readings (qira'at, recited variants): ﴿الوِلَايَةُ﴾ (al-wilāyah) and ﴿الْوَلَايَةُ﴾ (al-walāyah). ﴿الْوَلَايَةُ﴾ (al-walāyah) means support and help, as in His saying: ﴿You have no share in their support at all﴾ [Al-Anfal 8:72]. ﴿الوِلَايَةُ﴾ (al-wilāyah) means dominion and authority. So on the Day of Resurrection, there is no support and no dominion except for whom? For Allah, the True, glorified and exalted. And when there is no victory and no authority except for Allah, then everything other than Him is of no benefit to its devotee at all.

﴿هُنَالِكَ الْوَلايَةُ لِلَّهِ الْحَقِّ هُوَ خَيْرٌ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ عُقْبًا﴾ ﴿There, protection belongs to Allah, the True. He is best in reward and best in outcome.﴾ The pronoun ﴿هُوَ﴾ (huwa, "He") refers to Allah. ﴿خَيْرٌ ثَوَابًا﴾ (khayrun thawāban, "best in reward") is greater than anyone else's. If someone rewards an act, the reward of others is only equal to the deed, and if they increase it, they increase it only slightly. As for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, He multiplies the reward of a deed tenfold, up to seven hundredfold, and up to many multiples. Likewise, He is ﴿خَيْرٌ عُقْبًا﴾ (khayrun ʿuqbā, "best in outcome"), may He be exalted, because whoever's outcome is the victory and guardianship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, there is no doubt that this is better than everything else. All the outcomes that a person obtains at the hands of human beings will vanish, but the outcome that is with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does not vanish.

The example ends here. There are many lessons and benefits in it, but it is among the conditions of this lesson that we do not mention them.

Ibn 'Uthaymin says: "﴿And strike for them﴾ [al-Kahf 45], another example. ﴿And strike for them﴾ means: set forth for them a parable, ﴿the likeness of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky﴾, namely rain, ﴿and the vegetation of the earth mingles with it﴾. 'Mingles with it' means that the gardens become interwoven with varieties of plants in their flowers, leaves and trees, as you see in springtime, how the earth becomes, glory be to God, as if it were a most beautiful embroidered cloth, ﴿the vegetation of the earth mingles with it﴾ of every kind and every species.

﴿Then it becomes dry stubble, which the winds scatter﴾. '(It becomes)' means this varied, intermingled vegetation ﴿becomes dry stubble, which the winds scatter﴾; withered, ﴿which the winds scatter﴾: carry away. This is the likeness of the life of this world. Now, the world flourishes for a person and displays its beauty to him, and then suddenly it dies down. By what? By his death or by losing the world. This is unavoidable: either a person dies or he loses the world.

This is a likeness that matches perfectly, and this kind of parable God Almighty has struck in several surahs of the Noble Qur'an, so that we will not be deceived by the world nor cling to it. What is strange is that we are deceived by it and cling to it, even though its troubles, worries and griefs are far more numerous than its pleasures and comforts. The poet who said:

*One day is against us and one day is for us,
and one day we are made to suffer and one day we are made to rejoice,*

does not, as it appears to us, intend an equation; rather, the meaning is that there is no joy without some harm accompanying it, and no harm without some joy accompanying it, but its pure moments are far fewer than its troubles. Even those who are pampered by it are not at ease with it, as the other poet said:

*There is no sweetness to life as long as its pleasures are clouded
by remembering death and old age.*

﴿Then it becomes dry stubble, which the winds scatter, and God is over all things Omnipotent﴾. God Almighty is over all things Omnipotent. No one is able to annihilate it, and whatever is annihilated, who is able to...?
* Student: To bring it into existence.

* Shaykh: To bring it into existence. And between bringing into existence and annihilation there is nothing but the word "Be", ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82]."

Then, the Mighty and Majestic said, contrasting what remains with what does not remain: ﴿Wealth and children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾ [al-Kahf 46]. Wealth, of whatever kind, whether goods, cash, human beings or livestock. ﴿And children are the adornment of the worldly life﴾, and nothing benefits a person in the Hereafter except what he has sent ahead of himself.

He mentioned sons without daughters because it was the custom that they took pride only in what? Only in sons. In the Jahiliyyah, daughters were humiliated, held in the utmost contempt, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When one of them is given the good news of a female, his face becomes darkened, and he is filled with suppressed rage﴾ [al-Nahl 58]. That is, his face became dark and his heart filled with rage. ﴿And he hides himself from the people﴾ [al-Nahl 58-59], meaning he hides himself from them, ﴿because of the evil of that which he has been given good news of﴾ [al-Nahl 59]. Then he deliberates within himself: ﴿Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust?﴾ [al-Nahl 59]. There remains a third option, that he keeps her in honour, but this was not possible in their view. There was only one of two choices: either he keeps her in humiliation and disgrace, or he buries her in the dust alive. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they decide﴾ [al-Nahl 59].

﴿The adornment of the worldly life﴾: a person beautifies himself with them, he is adorned by having children. Imagine yourself as one who hosts guests, that is, you are hospitable, and you have five or ten young men who receive the guests. You will find that this is the utmost of joy and comfort. This is adornment, is it not? Likewise, imagine yourself riding a horse, with these young men surrounding you from the right and the left, and from behind and in front. You will find it a great adornment. But there is something better than that. He said: ﴿And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord in reward and better in hope﴾.

﴿The enduring good deeds﴾ are the righteous deeds of speech and action, including: Glory be to Allah, Praise be to Allah, There is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, There is no power nor strength except with Allah, and including charity, and other things. These are the enduring good deeds.

﴿Better with your Lord in reward and better in hope﴾. There is no doubt that the matter is as our Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, said: better in reward, that is, in recompense and reward. ﴿And better in hope﴾, that is, in what a person hopes for, because these enduring good deeds, as Allah described them, are enduring. As for the worldly life, what is it?

* Students: Perishable.

* The Shaykh: Perishable and transient.

Then the Most High said: ﴿And the day We set the mountains in motion﴾ [al-Kahf 18:47]. Mention the day We set [the mountains] in motion. On this reading, ﴿the day﴾ (yawm) is an adverbial complement whose governing verb is omitted; the sense is: "Mention the day We set the mountains in motion."

﴿And you will see the earth laid bare, and We will gather them﴾ and so on to the end of the verse. That is, [the meaning is]: mention to them, to the people, this state and this great scene, the day We set the mountains in motion. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has explained in another verse that He sets them in motion so that they become a mirage, and become like carded wool. This is because Allah, the Most High, will crush the earth, and the mountains will become a heap of sand, scattered, and then they will be dispersed through the air. This is the meaning of their being set in motion.

Among the verses that point to this is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in Surah an-Naml: ﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they pass like the passing of clouds — the handiwork of Allah, who perfected everything﴾ [an-Naml 27:88]. Some people said: this verse [refers to] the rotation of the earth, meaning that you see the mountains and suppose them to be fixed, but they are moving. This is an error and speaking about Allah without knowledge, because the context of the verse is when? The Day of Resurrection, as Allah the Most High said: ﴿And the day the Trumpet is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills; and all will come to Him in humility. (87) And you see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they pass like the passing of clouds — the handiwork of Allah, who perfected everything. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what you do. (88) Whoever comes with a good deed will have better than it﴾ [an-Naml 27:87–89]. The verse clearly refers to the Day of Resurrection.

As for the claim of this man who says that on the Day of Resurrection matters are realities, and here He says ﴿you see the mountains, thinking them﴾, there is no thinking in the Hereafter — this is also an error; for if Allah has affirmed this, we must believe in it. Moreover, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing. (1) On the day you see it, every nursing mother will be distracted from that which she nursed﴾ and ﴿And you will see the people as drunkards, but they are not drunkards﴾ [al-Hajj 22:1–2]. So if we say that the convulsion of the Hour is its occurrence, Allah has affirmed that a seer will see people and think them drunk, when they are not drunk.

In any case, this is a rule we should understand: it is obligatory for us to take the verses according to their apparent meaning, and to recognize that context determines the meaning. How many a sentence, within a context of other sentences, would have a meaning if it were in a different context, but in this context it has the meaning appropriate to the context. ﴿And the day We set the mountains in motion, and you see the earth laid bare﴾ — apparent: the earth; because it will be one flat expanse, and it is not now laid bare, since it is spherical, most of it now not visible to us, is it not so?

Moreover, what is visible to us is also largely hidden in the mountains which we do not see. But on the Day of Resurrection there will be no mountains and no sphericity; the earth will be stretched out like a leather hide, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿When the sky splits open (1), and it hears and obeys its Lord, and it is right to do so (2), and when the earth is stretched out﴾ [al-Inshiqaq 84:1–3]. ﴿When the earth is stretched out﴾ means it is not stretched now; now it is spherical, but on the Day of Resurrection it will be stretched. Glory be to Allah the Great.

﴿And you see the earth laid bare, and We will gather them﴾ means: We will assemble them, i.e., all the people. Indeed, even the wild beasts will be gathered, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And when the wild beasts are gathered﴾ [at-Takwir 81:5]. Indeed, besides the wild beasts, [others] too, as the Most High said in Surah al-An'am: ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ [al-An'am 6:38]. When He mentioned all the creatures, He said: ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ It is better that I recite the whole verse: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book anything. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾. Everything will be gathered. Therefore the Mighty and Majestic says here: ﴿and We will gather them﴾, meaning all of mankind; and in other verses [it says] that the wild beasts will be gathered, and that all creatures will be gathered.

﴿And We gathered them, and We left out none of them﴾. Allah is greatest! ﴿Leave out﴾ means abandon. ﴿None of them﴾: all people are gathered. If one dies on land, he is gathered; at sea, he is gathered; in whatever place, he must be gathered on the Day of Resurrection and brought together.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 48:

﴿وَعُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا﴾ [al-Kahf: 48] ﴿عُرِضُوا﴾ from al-'arid (the one who presents)?

* Student: God.

* Shaykh: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is also possible that the angels bring them by the knowledge of Allah and present them to Him. ﴿عَلَى رَبِّكَ﴾ means Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

﴿صَفًّا﴾ means: in the state of being in rows (ṣaffan), that is, ranks. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, will call them to account. "As for the believer, he will be alone with Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and He will make him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'You did such-and-such, and you did such-and-such.' He will acknowledge them, and the Most Generous of the generous will say to him: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you.'"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2768/52) from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar.]] O Allah, to You be praise. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives them on the Day of Resurrection, so He does not take him to account for them, and in this world He conceals them. This is the reality. Now, how many sins do you have in secret? Many, whether they are actions of the outward limbs or actions of the hearts. They are concealed. Bad opinion exists, envy exists, the wish for harm to a Muslim (not every Muslim) exists, and it is concealed from you. Other actions of the limbs exist too, but Allah, exalted is He, conceals them over the servant. We hope, God willing, that the One who concealed them for us in this world will forgive them for us in the Hereafter. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forgives them, saying: "I forgive them for you today."

Then He said: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾. Allahu akbar! The sentence is emphasized with three emphatics: the lam, qad, and the implied oath, meaning: "By Allah, you have truly come to Us."

﴿كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾: you have no wealth, no garments, nor anything else. Indeed, we may say: ﴿كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾; rather, whatever was lost from you will be returned to you, as in the authentic hadith that they "will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised" (ghurlan),[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6527) and Muslim (2859/56) from the hadith of 'A'isha, in similar wording.]] the plural of aghral, which is one who has not been circumcised. Glory be to Allah! The foreskin that was removed in this world by circumcision returns on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا﴾. Look: they are presented before Allah in rows, and it is said: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾, and it is said: ﴿بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا﴾. This "bal" is a transitional turn (idrab intiqal), and they are being reproached: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا﴾, so there is no escape for you; ﴿كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ﴾, so you have no wealth or family with you; ﴿بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ﴾ in the world ﴿أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا﴾. And is this supposition shown to be false or true? It is shown to be false, so it is baseless.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 49:

Then the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾ [Al-Kahf 49]. ﴿Wuddia﴾ means it will be distributed among the people, so one will take his book in his right hand and another will take his book in his left.

﴿So you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it﴾: You will see them, O man, the criminals, meaning the disbelievers, ﴿fearful of what is in it﴾, meaning afraid, because they know their deeds. This resembles the saying of Allah the Exalted about the Jews who said: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days﴾ [Al-Baqarah 80]. So they were challenged, and it was said to them: If the Hereafter is yours, then wish for death. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah 7]. Because they know that when they die they will be punished, and whoever knows that when he dies he will be punished will never wish for death. So these are fearful of what is in their book, because they know that it contains disgraceful acts and great evil deeds.

﴿Fearful of what is in it, and they will say﴾ when they face it: ﴿Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?﴾ ﴿Ya wailatana﴾: ﴿Ya﴾ is a particle of calling. ﴿Wailatana﴾: how is "wailah" called upon? And "wailah" means destruction; how is it called upon?

The answer: Either we make ﴿Ya﴾ merely a particle of alerting, since calling includes both supplication and alerting; or we say they treated their woe as if it were a rational being being called, and the implied meaning is: "O our woe, come!" But the first meaning is closer, because it needs no implied element, and because it is more eloquent.

* * *
Allah the Blessed and Exalted said about the story of the two men who conversed: ﴿And he entered his garden while he was wronging himself﴾. The clause in His saying ﴿while he was wronging himself﴾ is what?
* Student: A circumstantial clause (ḥāliyah).

* Shaykh: A circumstantial clause. Why is he a wrongdoer?

* Student: Because he was not thankful for the blessings of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and he denied the Resurrection; the verses that come after it explain that he denied the Resurrection, and...

* Shaykh: So ﴿wronging himself﴾ is by disbelief in Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Why did he say: ﴿I do not think this will ever perish﴾? What moved him to it?

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, no, ﴿I do not think this will ever perish﴾.

* Student: He saw in it the strength (...).

* Shaykh: Yes.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: The sight, meaning admiration. The summary is that he was impressed by it until he said: ﴿I do not think this will ever perish﴾. Good. With what did he disbelieve: with his saying ﴿I do not think this will ever perish﴾, or with his saying ﴿I do not think the Hour will be established﴾?

* Student: With his saying: ﴿I do not think the Hour will be established﴾.

* Shaykh: With his saying: ﴿I do not think the Hour will be established﴾.

How do we reconcile his saying ﴿I do not think the Hour will be established﴾ with his saying ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely find better than this as a destination﴾?

* Student: By his own analogy, a corrupt analogy. He supposed that if the Resurrection occurred, he would be given in the Hereafter what Allah gave him of blessings in this world, and this is a corrupt analogy.

* Shaykh: Yes, that is, on the supposition that I am returned, I will find better than it as a destination.

Is there a verse similar in meaning but general?

* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat 50].

* Shaykh: What precedes it?

* Student: ﴿And when We let man taste mercy from Us, he rejoices in it﴾ [Ash-Shura 48].

* Shaykh: Yes, at the end of Fussilat.

* Student: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is hopeless and despairing (49). And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say: This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will be established. And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward]﴾ [Fussilat 49-50].

* Shaykh: May Allah bless you. His brother who was conversing with him said to him: ﴿If you see me as less than you in wealth and children (39), then perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden﴾. What is the occasion?

* Student: Because he boasted over him that he had more wealth and more powerful people, so it is possible that he said: If you boast over me with that while I am less than you in wealth and children, then it is possible that he invoked against him that Allah would remove what he boasted over him with.

* Shaykh: That is, as if he is saying: You have now humbled me and claimed that you are more powerful than me in people. So he invoked against him that He remove what he boasted of. This is one possibility. And the possibility that "perhaps" (ʿasā) is what?

* Student: As an expression of expectation.

* Shaykh: As an expression of expectation.

* Student: That Allah the Exalted sends down upon him what he deserves.

* Shaykh: Yes, good; because perhaps this matter you boast of over me may turn around, so Allah gives this man something better than the second man's garden, and sends upon it a punishment from heaven.

Did what he expected happen?

* Student: Yes.

* Shaykh: Recite what indicates that?

* Student: ﴿So he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾.

* Shaykh: No, ﴿And his fruit was encompassed [by ruin], so he began to turn his palms over regarding what he had spent on it﴾. Good.

Regarding the saying of Allah the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿Wealth and children are adornment of the worldly life﴾: why did He not mention daughters, ﴿wealth and children﴾?

* Student: Because people's habit is to boast of sons, not of daughters, especially in the pre-Islamic period, when they boasted of sons and not of daughters.

* Shaykh: They boasted of wealth and sons.

* Student: And not of daughters.

* Shaykh: And they did not boast of daughters; rather, on the contrary. Recite to me a verse that indicates their condition regarding daughters.

* Student: ﴿And when one of them is given news of a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief﴾.

* Shaykh: Yes, continue. Have you not memorized the Qur'an? ﴿And he suppresses grief﴾, what comes after it?

* Student: ﴿And he suppresses grief (58). He hides himself from the people because of the evil of what he has been given news of. Shall he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the dust? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide﴾ [An-Nahl 58-59].

* Shaykh: Well done, may Allah bless you.

The saying of Allah the Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And [mention] the Day We will set the mountains in motion﴾. Where is the governing element (ʿāmil) of ﴿the Day﴾? ﴿And the Day We set the mountains in motion﴾?

* Student: "And the Day We set in motion, We the mountains."

* Shaykh: No, where is the governing element?

* Student: We said: it is a temporal adverb.

* Shaykh: Yes, "the Day" is an adverb of time. Does every adverb or prepositional phrase need a governing element?

* Student: An implied governing element.

* Shaykh: The estimate?

* Student: "Remember."

* Shaykh: Remember ﴿the Day We set the mountains in motion﴾. And what is the meaning of His saying ﴿You will see the earth bare﴾?

* Student: "Desolate."

* Shaykh: Desolate?

* Student: That is, bare, apparent.

* Shaykh: Bare, meaning apparent.

* Student: There is nothing in it...

* Shaykh: There are no mountains in it, nor valleys, and it is not curved so that most of it is hidden from the viewer; rather, it will be flat and extended, as came in the hadith: "Like the spreading of a leather hide" [[Narrated by Ibn Majah (4081) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]].

The saying of Allah: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾: which book is it?

* Student: The pages of deeds.

* Shaykh: The pages of deeds, meaning that in which the deeds were written. Well done. Because the noble angels write down everything a person does. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And We are closer to him than his jugular vein. When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left. Not a word does he utter except that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf 16-18]. ﴿Raqib﴾ means present, not absent, and whatever word he utters is written down.

* * *
* Student: May Allah be pleased with you, O Shaykh. (...) the example of the garden, and the example of the earth and the grass, O Shaykh, differs from the context, since some people say this is not (...). If it is said of the two men, the representation of the two men indicates that it is true; the representation of the earth afterward indicates that it is like (...).
* Shaykh: Correct. The preponderant view is that His saying ﴿And present to them the example of two men﴾ is in reality, not a hypothetical; this is the preponderant view, because this dialogue with his companion indicates that it is true, something that actually occurred.

* Student: Shaykh, may Allah pardon you, what is the meaning of ﴿I did not associate anyone with my Lord﴾?

* Shaykh: No, yes, you.

* Student: May Allah pardon you, O Shaykh. In His saying ﴿And mention your Lord﴾, we said in its explanation: "And mention that your Lord..." So how do we respond, O Shaykh, to those who distort the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And your Lord comes﴾?

* Shaykh: We do not reject every interpretation. We say: an interpretation that has evidence we accept, and an interpretation that has no evidence we reject. For example, ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angel, rank upon rank﴾ [Al-Fajr 22]: it is clear that the meaning is that He Himself, the Mighty and Majestic, comes. As for this interpretation, "remember the command of your Lord," or ﴿When you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah﴾ [An-Nahl 98], meaning when you intend to recite it, and what is similar to that, for which there is evidence, this is not denied; because when we turn the apparent wording toward what the evidence indicates, that becomes the explanation. Have you understood?

* Student: Explaining a verse of the Qur'an in accordance with the sciences of the modern age?

* Shaykh: If it is correct, there is no harm.

* Student: And if it involves rejecting the explanation of the verse?

* Shaykh: I say: if it is correct. But some brothers who explain verses in line with the age load them with what they cannot bear. However, if it is correct, there is no objection, such as: ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾ [An-Nahl 8]. If a person says, for example: these airplanes that carry people now, and others will come after them, this is included in His saying ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾; we say: this is correct.

* * *
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will say: O woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?﴾ The phrase ﴿mal hadha al-kitab﴾ before you now: is it written according to the well-known rules of our age? It is not, because (mal) and (hadha) are written separately, whereas by the well-known rules among us, (ma) is written alone and (li-hadha) together. ﴿Mal hadha al-kitab﴾ means: what is wrong with this Book? ﴿Leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it﴾ means: has recorded it in number, as if they were trying to escape from it, but this will not benefit them.

﴿And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾. ﴿They will find what they did present﴾: will their worldly deeds return on the Day of Resurrection? No; rather the meaning is ﴿they will find what they did present﴾, meaning the reward for what they did, or they will find the reality of what they did. An implied element is necessary, because their worldly deeds perished with their passing, but they were recorded; so what they did they will find in this Book ﴿present﴾.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾: He does not wrong anyone for what? For the perfection of His justice, the Mighty and Majestic; He does not wrong anyone, so He does not add to an evildoer a single bad deed, nor diminish from a doer of good a single good deed. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will fear neither injustice nor deprivation﴾ [Ta-Ha 112].

This verse: ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ is among the negated attributes of Allah, correct? Are there affirmed attributes of Allah? Yes; most of the attributes mentioned to us are affirmed attributes. Negated attributes are not completed in faith until you believe in the affirmation of the perfection of their opposite. So what is the opposite of wronging?

* Students: Justice.

* Shaykh: Justice. And why is wronging negated of Him? For the perfection of His justice. This is necessary, since bare negation cannot be among the attributes of Allah. Bare negation, pure negation, cannot be among the attributes of Allah. Pay attention to this rule: (Bare negation, i.e., that which does not include a perfection, cannot be among the attributes of Allah the Mighty and Majestic; rather, every negation that Allah negates of Himself must include the perfection of its opposite). It is necessary. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (Because pure negation is pure non-existence.) Negation is non-existence; this is one point. (And because if negation does not include a perfection, it may be due to incapacity to receive it.) That is, if a negated attribute does not include a perfection, it may be due to the thing's not being capable of receiving it. And if it does not include a perfection, it may be due to the reverse. Note these rules: if it does not include a perfection, it may be due to incapacity to receive it. How so? Do we not say that a wall does not wrong? Indeed. Is that a perfection of the wall? No. Why? Because the wall is not capable of being described with wronging or with justice, so negating wrong from the wall is not one of its perfections.

And the negation of a defect, if it does not include a perfection, may be a deficiency due to the incapacity of the one described to do its opposite. If you describe a person as one who does not wrong because he is a weak man who cannot wrong others, nor even claim his right from others, is that praise? No. Listen to the words of the poet:

A tribe that does not betray a covenant, and does not wrong people even to the weight of a mustard seed.

Does he praise them for fidelity and not wronging, or does he blame them for that? He blames them: they do not betray a covenant because they are unable to, and they do not wrong people because they are unable to.

So the summary, my brothers, is that every attribute that Allah describes Himself by, if it is a negation, we must believe in the affirmation of what? The perfection of its opposite.

On this rule: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead?﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 33]. He negated weariness, which is incapacity to create the heavens and the earth, why? Because of the affirmation of the perfection of its opposite, which is power. So now we believe that Allah the Exalted has a power that is not touched by incapacity. ﴿And We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38], meaning no weariness or exhaustion, and that is due to the perfection of His power, the Majestic and Exalted. This is a rule that benefits you in the chapter of creed: that everything Allah negates of Himself is for the affirmation of the perfection of its opposite. Negating wrong, because He is just; negating incapacity, because He is capable; negating heedlessness, because He is watchful over everything.

﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾: we said, for the perfection of His justice. But the Jahmiyyah said: He does not wrong because wronging is not conceivable, not because He is able to wrong but does not. No: it is because wronging is inconceivable. How so? They said: since all creation is Allah's creation and belongs to Allah, if He punishes a doer of good, He has punished His own property; there is no wronging in that, since He does what He wills in His dominion.

But this saying of theirs is false, because Allah the Mighty and Majestic, having promised reward to the doers of good and punishment to the evildoers, if He then rewards the evildoer and punishes the doer of good, the least that can be said is that He, the Mighty and Majestic, far exalted above it, has broken His promise. This is the least of what is said about it, and there is no doubt that this contradicts justice and truthfulness. So we say to them: Allah the Mighty and Majestic said in a sacred hadith: "O My servants, I have forbidden injustice to Myself" [Narrated by Muslim (2577) from the hadith of Abu Dharr]. He forbade it to Himself, and this shows that He is capable of it but has forbidden it to Himself, for the perfection of His justice, the Majestic and Exalted.

So we say: Allah does not wrong anyone for the perfection of His justice, not because wronging is impossible, as the Jahmiyyah claimed. To this, Shaykh Ibn al-Qayyim says in the Nuniyyah:

"And wronging, in their view, is impossible in its very essence..."

Wronging is not possible because it is His dominion: we say this is an error, and it entails denying Allah the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 50:

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾ [al-Kahf 50]. (Idh) appears often in the Qur'an, and the grammarians (al-mu'rabun, those who study i'rab, grammatical inflection) say: what is it? Its governing element is omitted, and the estimated meaning is "Remember" (udhkur): ﴿when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. The angels (al-mala'ikah) are an unseen world (alam ghaybi) that Allah created from light. The Prophet ﷺ informed us that Allah created them from light, and Allah Most High informed us in the Qur'an that He created the jinn from fire and created mankind from clay. So the creatures we know of are: angels from light, jinn from fire, and humans from clay. The angels, then, are an unseen world. Must we believe in them or not? We must, and it is one of the pillars of faith.

The angels are unlike the devils (shayatin), as the verse makes clear. They are more capable and purer than the devils, and they have an influence that the devils do not have. The devils cannot ascend to the heaven, can they? Rather, whoever attempts it is pursued by a burning meteor. The angels in the heaven ascend with the souls of the children of Adam until they reach Allah, Mighty and Majestic. They have also filled the heavens. So we must believe in the angels with unwavering faith, and that they are an unseen world. Yet they may at times be from the perceptible world by the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as Gabriel (Jibril, peace be upon him) was seen by the Prophet ﷺ twice; he has six hundred wings. Glory be to Allah! He filled the horizon, and he is one. This is evidence of the greatness of his creation. And the greatness of Gabriel's creation is evidence of the greatness of whom?

* Students: The Creator.

* Shaykh: The Creator, Majestic and Exalted is He. Sometimes Gabriel, whose description and creation are as such, comes in the form of a man, does he not? He comes in the form of a man, but this transformation is not by his own power, rather by the power of his Creator, Majestic and Exalted is He. Allah has given them the ability to take forms and transform by the will of Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He. So the angels are fundamentally an unseen world, and they may be from the world of witnessing, but not always, rather sometimes. And Allah knows best.

* * *

He says: What is your opinion of Tafsir al-Jalalayn, and what is the best tafsir in your view?

Tafsir al-Jalalayn is good, but it is only suitable for the student of knowledge, because in reality its tafsir is like symbols, though it is full of knowledge. Also, it contains things that contradict the methodology of Ahl as-Sunnah wal-Jama'ah in the chapter of the divine attributes (sifat). So it is not suitable for a beginning student of knowledge, because it is of a higher level than him. But you should take the tafsir of Shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman as-Sa'di, may Allah have mercy on him, because it is easy and accessible; everyone understands it, even the common people understand it, and it contains rare benefits that you will not find elsewhere.

* * *

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

How did one of the two men supplicate against his companion that Allah send upon his garden a torment from the heaven? How was it permissible for him to ask Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to send upon his companion's garden a torment from the heaven?

* Student: Because he wronged him by arrogance towards him.

* Shaykh: Because he wronged him by his arrogance toward him. Is it permissible for a person to supplicate against his oppressor?

* Student: It is derived from this that it is permissible.

* Shaykh: Question.

* Student: Yes, it is permissible.

* Shaykh: It is permissible to supplicate against one's oppressor with the same as his oppression of him. Was the supplication answered?

* Student: Yes, it was answered (...).

* Shaykh: What became the end of his garden?

* Student: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will give me something better than your garden and send upon it a calamity from the heaven, so that it becomes a barren slippery ground. Or its water will sink away, and you will not be able to find it﴾. This is what happened (...).

* Shaykh: (...) What happened? This is every supplication.

* Student: The water became sunken and he could not (...).

* Shaykh: Did Allah not say: ﴿and his fruits were encompassed﴾? This is the point of evidence: ﴿his fruits were encompassed﴾.

Did he show regret over what happened?

* Student: He showed regret.

* Shaykh: He showed regret. How?

* Student: ﴿He turned his palms over regarding what he had spent upon it﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿He turned his palms over regarding what he had spent upon it, while it lay in ruins upon its trellises﴾. He looks at it with a look of anguish and grief.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, explaining the state of the worldly life. How?

* Student: Allah Most High said: ﴿And present to them the parable of the life of this world: it is like water which We send down from the sky, and the plants of the earth mingle with it, and then it becomes dry stalks which the winds scatter﴾.

* Shaykh: What is the matter of the case?

* Student: The form of the mingling of plants.

* Shaykh: Indeed Allah..

* Student: Indeed Allah, Glorified and Exalted, sent down (...) and it grew in the earth, and it became like spring, and the plants intermingled with one another and flourished. Then after that it became dry, withered stalks, and so is the life of this world: it flourishes for its owner, but either he leaves it by death, or it departs and moves on.

* Shaykh: The life of this world is just so: either its owner separates from it or it separates from him, and there is no escape.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Able over all things﴾. Is it in the sense of qadir (Able) or is it more intensive?

* Student: In the sense of qadir.

* Shaykh: Yes, in the sense of qadir. Then why did He not say: "And Allah is ever Able over all things (qadiran)" as in another verse?

* Student: Because it is more general (...).

* Another student: Muqtadiran is more intensive.

* Shaykh: Muqtadiran is more intensive.

* Student: Because it indicates (...) the known.

* Shaykh: Even the power, but because the pattern of the word indicates intensification in it, and that it is more emphatic than ﴿And Allah is ever Competent over all things﴾ [al-Ahzab 27].

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: ﴿wealth and children﴾. Why did He not mention daughters?

* Student: Sons were mentioned because it is the custom of the Arabs to boast of sons rather than daughters.

* Shaykh: Yes. Why did He not mention palaces and ships?

* Student: Because they are included within wealth.

* Shaykh: They are included in wealth, good.

What is the comprehensive statement on the meaning of ﴿the enduring good deeds﴾?

* Student: ﴿The enduring good deeds﴾, a hadith has been narrated, O Shaykh..

* Shaykh: The comprehensive meaning, no.

* Student: They are everything that remains of the remembrance of Allah: glorification, magnification and charity.

* Shaykh: That is, all righteous deeds. Included in that are glorification, magnification, declaring Allah's oneness (tahlil), prayer, enjoining good and forbidding evil, seeking knowledge, and other things; all of these are included in this.

* * *

﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾: ﴿idh﴾ is an object of an omitted verb, the estimated meaning being: remember when We said to the angels. That is, mention this to the nation so that it may take a lesson from it, and so that the virtue of the children of Adam before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, becomes clear.

﴿When We said to the angels﴾: al-mala'ikah is the plural of malak, after the known morphological derivation of the scholars of sarf (morphology). And they are, as we explained yesterday, an unseen world that Allah Most High created from light.

﴿"Prostrate to Adam"﴾: Some of them said it was a prostration of greeting and not a prostration upon the forehead. But in this view there is a problem, because they fled from it being a prostration upon the forehead, since prostration is not valid except to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and it is shirk if it occurs to other than Allah. However, what we must do is take the words at their apparent meaning, and say: the origin is that it is a prostration upon the forehead. And when it is in compliance with the command of Allah, it is not shirk, just as killing a soul without right is one of the major sins, but if it occurs in compliance with the command of Allah, it is an act of obedience among the acts of obedience.

Abraham the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, was commanded to slaughter his son.
