He himself carried out the slaughter, and there is no concealing the transgression in this, nor the severing of kinship in this. But since it was in compliance with the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, it became an act of obedience.

So the prostration to Adam, were it not for the command of Allah, would have been shirk. But when Allah commands it, the whole matter belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So the correct view is that the verse is on its apparent meaning, and that what is meant is prostration upon the forehead, but since it was by the command of Allah, it was an act of obedience to Allah. Adam is the father of mankind; Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created him from clay and created him with His own hand. The people of knowledge said: Allah did not mention anything as made by His hand except Adam, the Garden of Eden, for He created it with His hand, and He wrote the Torah with His hand, Majestic and Exalted is He.

These are three things, all of which were by the hand of Allah, unlike others that are created by the word "Be, and it is." Adam, peace be upon him, was created by Allah Most High with His hand. And Adam was a prophet, not a messenger, because the first messenger sent to mankind was Noah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him when people differed: ﴿Mankind was one community; then Allah sent prophets as bearers of good tidings and warners﴾ [al-Baqarah 213]. That is, the meaning is: mankind was one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bearers of good news and warners. So the first messenger was Noah, peace be upon him, and not Adam. Adam was a prophet spoken to (mukallam). If someone says: how can he be a prophet and not a messenger? We say: yes, he can be a prophet and not a messenger, because there was no call requiring a message. The people were upon one religion, mankind had not yet spread much, and they had not been greatly tempted by the world; they were a small group, so they followed their father and did his deeds. When the community spread, multiplied and differed, Allah sent the messengers.

﴿"Prostrate to Adam." So they prostrated﴾ in compliance with the command of Allah. ﴿Except Iblis﴾ did not prostrate. Iblis is the devil (shaytan), and he did not prostrate. Allah clarified this by His saying: ﴿He was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord﴾. The clause ﴿he was of the jinn﴾ is a resumptive clause, explaining Iblis's state: that he was of the jinn, that is, of this category, though he was their father, but he was of this category.

﴿So he defied the command of his Lord﴾: that is, he went out of obedience to Allah Most High in His command. The root of fusuq is going out, and from it the saying: "the fruit fusaqa" when it split open and opened. ﴿So he defied the command of his Lord﴾, and so on. If someone says: the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is that Iblis was of the angels, the answer is: No, that is not the apparent meaning, because He said: ﴿except Iblis﴾, then mentioned that he was of the jinn. Yes, the Qur'an indicates that the command was directed to Iblis as it was directed to the angels, but why? The scholars said: he used to come to the angels and gather with them, so the address was directed to this assembly of angels who were created from light, and to the devil who was created from fire. The angels returned to their origin, and the devil returned to his origin, which is arrogance, refusal, and disputing with falsehood, for he refused, was arrogant, and disputed. What did he say to Allah? He said: ﴿I am better than him﴾ [al-A'raf 12]: "How do You command me to prostrate to one who is inferior to me?" Then he gave a reason that works against him, saying: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾ [al-A'raf 12]. Yet the thing created from clay is better than the thing created from fire, because what is created from fire: fire is burning and blazing, and it has the mark of haste; you see its flame going right and left, having no settled base. In short, Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, in the book Ighathat al-Lahfan, mentioned many differences between clay and fire. So he is not better than Adam merely because he was created from fire. Then, even supposing he was created from fire and was better than Adam, is it not more fitting for him to comply with the command of his Creator? Indeed, but he did not do so, and he was arrogant. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, clarified the state of this devil, He said: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me, while they are an enemy to you? Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾.

﴿Will you then take﴾: the address returns to those who took Iblis and his offspring as allies besides Allah, so they worshipped the devil and abandoned the worship of the Most Merciful. Allah Most High said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan, for he is to you a clear enemy? And that you should worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Ya-Sin 60-61]. Here He says: ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me, while they are an enemy to you?﴾

﴿And his offspring﴾: that is, those who were born of him. Some of the early scholars were asked by people who were overly deep in such matters: "Does the devil have a wife?" He said: "I was not present at the marriage contract." Is this a correct answer or not? He said: "I was not present at the contract." The question: does he have a wife? There is no need for this; we believe that he has offspring. As for whether from a wife or not, we do not know. Did Allah Most High not create Eve from whom?

* Students: From Adam.

* Shaykh: From Adam. So it is possible that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created his offspring from him, just as He created Eve from Adam. These matters, the matters of the unseen, a person should not raise objections to them based on matters of the witnessed world, because these are matters beyond our level. We believe that he has offspring, but must we believe that he has a wife?

* Students: We are not obliged to.

* Shaykh: We are not obliged to, yes. ﴿Will you then take him and his offspring as allies besides Me﴾: that is, you befriend them and take their commands besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿While they are an enemy to you﴾: this is the point of denunciation. That is, how can you take these as allies when they are enemies? This is foolishness, deficiency of intellect, and deficiency of judgment, that a person should take his enemy as a friend. Allah Most High said: ﴿Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾: that is, wretched is this exchange for them. And what is the better exchange? That they take Allah as their ally, not Satan.

﴿Wretched is the exchange for the wrongdoers﴾. As for His saying ﴿for the wrongdoers﴾ here, one may say that it means the disbelievers, because they are the ones who took Satan and his offspring as allies absolutely. And one may also say that "the wrongdoers" encompasses the disbelievers and those whose wrongdoing is less than disbelief.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take those who mislead as helpers.﴾ [Al-Kahf 51]. This means that these (the devils) do not deserve to be taken as allies, because they have no share in the governance and management of the universe. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, because the heavens and the earth were created before the devils. ﴿Nor the creation of themselves﴾ means: some of them from others; that is, He did not make some of them witness the creation of others. So how can you take them as allies when they did not share in the creation, did not create anything, and did not even witness the creation of the heavens and the earth?

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, and I would not take those who mislead as helpers.﴾ [Al-Kahf 51]. This means that these do not deserve to be taken as allies, because they have no share in the governance and management of the universe. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, because the heavens and the earth were created before the devils.

﴿Nor the creation of themselves﴾: that is, some of them from others; meaning He did not make some of them witness the creation of others. So how can you take them as allies when they did not share in the creation, did not create anything, and did not even witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves? In this verse there is evidence that whoever speaks about any matter concerning the heavens and the earth without a legal (shar'i) proof or a sensory (hissi) proof, his words are not to be accepted.

For example, if someone says: "The heavens were formed from such-and-such, and the earth was formed from such-and-such," or some say: "The earth is a piece of the sun," and similar statements whose correctness we do not know, then what do we say to him? What do we say? We say: Allah did not make you witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, and we will not accept from you any of this unless we find a sensory proof from which there is no escape, and then we believe it, because the Qur'an does not contradict observable realities.

﴿And I would not take those who mislead as helpers﴾: the pronoun in ﴿I would not﴾ refers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿Taking those who mislead as helpers﴾ means supporters who support My religion. Why? Because the one who misleads turns people away from the religion. So how would Allah, Mighty and Majestic, take those who mislead as helpers? This is an indication that it is not befitting for you, O human, to take those who mislead as helpers whom you rely upon for support, because they will not benefit you; rather, they will harm you.

Therefore, do not rely on the foolish, nor rely on the people of deviant desires, because they cannot benefit you; rather, they will harm you. If Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not take those who mislead as helpers, then we too should not take those who mislead as helpers, because there is no good in them. In this is a prohibition against evil companions (biṭānat al-sū'), and against associating with people of evil, and that a person should beware of evil companions.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 52:

﴿And [remember] the Day He will say, "Call upon My partners, whom you claimed [to be Mine]."﴾ [al-Kahf: 51-52]

That is: remember the day when He says, "Call upon My partners whom you claimed." They will call upon them, but they will not respond to them. And when is this? This will be on the Day of Resurrection, when it will be said to them: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?" ﴿They will call upon them, but they will not respond to them﴾, because at that time Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: ﴿Whose is the dominion today?﴾ [Ghafir: 16], and He will answer Himself: ﴿To Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. So these idols will not benefit their worshippers; rather, they and their worshippers will be cast into the Fire. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you will be going into it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 98].

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction (mawbiqan)﴾ [al-Kahf: 52]. Al-Mawbiq (destruction): the place of perdition. That is, We will place between them something that makes it impossible for them to go to their partners, or for their partners to come to them; rather, it is a place of ruin. It is an expression of despairing these people of benefiting from their partners on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And We placed between them a barrier of destruction﴾. Consider: if there were between you and your companion, or someone you seek help from, a trench of fire, could you go to him to help him, or could he come to you to help you? No, it is impossible. Allah will place between these people on the Day of Resurrection a mawbiq.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 53:

﴿And the criminals will see the Fire﴾ [Al-Kahf: 53]. "Al-mujrimun" (the criminals): meaning the disbelievers, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Indeed, We will take vengeance upon the criminals﴾ [As-Sajdah: 22].

﴿So they will be certain that they are going to fall into it﴾ [Al-Kahf: 53]. "Zannu" (they were certain): here "zann" means "yaqin" (certainty), that they were certain they would fall into it. The word "zann" comes with the meaning of certainty, as in the Most High's words: ﴿Those who are certain that they will meet their Lord﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 46]. "Yazunnun" (they are certain): what does it mean?

* Student: They are certain.

* Shaykh: Yes, they are certain that they will meet Allah. Otherwise, zann in the sense of inclining towards one of two doubtful possibilities is not sufficient for faith. But they "yazunnun," that is, they are certain. Here they saw it and became certain that they would fall into it.

﴿And they will find no escape from it﴾ [Al-Kahf: 53]. We ask Allah for well-being. Meaning: they will not find a place to turn away to. This is not included in the "zann," because if it were included in the "zann" they would have said "wa-lan" (and they will not). Rather, this is a new statement; that is, when they saw it and were certain they would fall into it, ﴿they found no escape from it﴾, i.e., no place to turn to in order to be saved from it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 54:

﴿And We have certainly diversified in this Quran for the people from every [kind of] example.﴾ [al-Kahf: 54]. ﴿Sarrafna﴾ means: We varied. To diversify (tasrif) a thing means to vary it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿the turning of the winds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164], meaning their variation from south to north, east to west. ﴿Sarrafna﴾ means: We varied in this Quran every kind of example. And so it is in reality, for the word of Allah is true. You find the examples of the Quran varied: at times to establish the resurrection, at times to establish the oneness of Allah, at times to explain the state of this world, at times to explain the state of the Hereafter, and at times they are lengthy and at times they are brief. They are of various types, each type in its place of eloquence and fluency and other things.

And His saying: ﴿min kulli mathal﴾ ("from every example") means: from every genus and category. This is an example of such-and-such, and this is an example of such-and-such. Why? So that people may remember, take heed, and understand them. However, there are people who do not take heed from these examples, but on the contrary.

Hence He said: ﴿And man is ever most contentious of anything﴾ [al-Kahf: 54]. As for His saying ﴿wa kana al-insanu﴾ ("and man is"), some exegetes say: "al-insan" means the disbeliever. But there is a consideration in this, because there is no evidence for it. Rather, we say: man, in terms of his humanity, is most contentious of anything; that is, most of what he possesses is disputation. This is in terms of his humanity. But in terms of faith, the believer is not contentious; rather, he submits to the truth and does not dispute it. Hence 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "No people were given disputation except that they went astray." I seek refuge in Allah from that.

Reflect on the state of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and you will find that they submitted in the utmost submission to what the Sharia brought, and did not dispute, and did not say: "Why?" When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perform ablution from eating the flesh of camels, and do not perform ablution from eating the flesh of sheep," did the Companions say: "Why?" No, they did not dispute; rather they said: "We hear and we obey." And likewise the rest of the commands. But man, in terms of being a human, most of what he has is disputation.

Note, then, that if such a phrase occurs to you in the Noble Quran, do not restrict "al-insan" to the disbeliever unless the context specifies that. If the context specifies that, then this is a general term intended for what? The specific. But if the context does not specify, then take it as general, but take it as a human by the attribute of humanity, and when faith predominates over humanity, its requirements are nullified.

﴿And man is ever most contentious of anything﴾: this was said by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with them both, when he came to them and found them sleeping, and said: "Will you not get up?" 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, our souls are in the hand of Allah, and if He willed, He would awaken us." The Messenger (ﷺ) turned away while striking his thigh and saying: "﴿And man is ever most contentious of anything﴾."

There is no doubt the Messenger knew that their souls are in the hand of Allah, and the Messenger (ﷺ) said regarding the obligatory prayer: "Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it," so he excused the sleeper. He (ﷺ) knew that, but he wished to urge them, and 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, wished to deflect blame from himself and his wife Fatimah.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 55:

﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them, and from asking their Lord for forgiveness, except that the way of the former peoples should befall them, or that the punishment should come upon them face to face.﴾ [al-Kahf: 55]

Meaning: What prevented people from faith and seeking forgiveness is a deficiency in the clarity (of the message). Since He mentioned that Allah has struck for people every kind of parable, and it was obligatory upon a person, when parables are struck for him, that he believe, yet what prevented him from faith is not a deficiency in the clarity; the matter is evident and manifest, and all praise is due to Allah. The Prophet ﷺ brought it pure and clean, but it is obstinacy. For this reason He said: ﴿except that the way of the former peoples should befall them﴾, meaning they are only waiting for the way of the former peoples.

﴿or that the punishment should come upon them face to face﴾. His saying: ﴿that they should believe﴾, ﴿and that they should ask their Lord for forgiveness﴾: "yastaghfiru rabbahum" means they seek His forgiveness. The believer frequently seeks forgiveness, and the disbeliever, when he believes, must seek forgiveness of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the sins that he committed. So when he believes and seeks forgiveness, the sins that were upon them are removed. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve: if they desist, what has passed will be forgiven for them﴾ [al-Anfal: 38].

﴿or that the punishment should come upon them face to face﴾, meaning: in confrontation, direct observation, and immediacy. And what is the way of the former peoples? The way of the former peoples is their being seized by a general punishment; this is the way of the former peoples. But Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, did not seize this Ummah with an all-encompassing punishment, because the Prophet ﷺ "supplicated to his Lord that He not seize his Ummah with a general famine, and Allah answered his supplication."

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bringers of good news and warners. And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby, and they take My signs and that with which they are warned as mockery﴾ to the end of the verse [al-Kahf: 56]. This is the function of the messengers: ﴿We do not send the messengers﴾ from the first of them, who was Noah, to the last of them, Muhammad (ﷺ), except for these two purposes: ﴿bringers of good news and warners﴾. That is, We did not send them in order to compel people to faith or to guide people. They are bringers of good news and warners. Bringers of good news to whom? To the believers, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah, and warners to the disbelievers: ﴿and warn those who say, "Allah has taken a son"﴾ [al-Kahf: 4].

﴿Except as bringers of good news and warners﴾: (mubashshirin) and (mundhirin) are both in the accusative. In what respect? As a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the messengers; that is, "except while being bringers of good news and warners."

﴿And those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood﴾: al-mujadalah (disputation) means al-mukhasamah (contention), and contention is called mujadalah because each party twists its argument toward the other, and you know that jadal is the twisting of a rope until it becomes firm and strong; this is the origin of mujadalah. So yujadilu means yukhasimu (contends). ﴿Those who disbelieve dispute with falsehood﴾, and contention with falsehood is itself falsehood. An example of this is their saying: ﴿Is it a mere human who guides us?﴾ [at-Taghabun: 6]. "Would humans guide us?!" They say: ﴿If Allah had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 24]. They say: if those worshipped besides Allah are fuel for Hell, then Jesus is fuel for Hell, and similar disputation. They dispute, and He says: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78]. The kinds of disputation are many.

Regarding the dispute about Jesus, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾ [al-Anbiya: 101], and Jesus, peace be upon him, is among them, ﴿they will be kept far from it﴾.

* It is derived from the verse that every person who disputes in order to refute the truth has a share in this verse; that is, there is in him a share of disbelief, and we seek refuge with Allah, because the disbelievers are the ones who dispute with falsehood in order to refute the truth thereby.

If someone says: how can the doubts that people raise be called falsehood, when they are doubts?

We say: one looks at the purpose. What is their aim in them? To refute the truth. For example, among those who deny that Allah is established upon the Throne, they say: "If He were established upon the Throne, He would be a body." What do they intend by this? The denial of the reality of istiwa' (establishment).

We say: these people have disputed with falsehood in order to refute the truth. As for the question of whether Allah is a body or not a body, that is a different matter. But they brought this statement for what purpose? To refute the truth. We do not deny them the question of whether He is a body or not a body; we deny that they denied the reality of istiwa'. As for the body or non-body, that is a separate discussion, namely that we neither deny nor affirm the wording. As for the meaning, we say: Allah the Exalted is self-subsisting, described by His attributes, does what He wills, establishes Himself upon His Throne, descends to the lowest heaven, comes to judge between His servants, is pleased, rejoices, laughs, and say whatever you wish; but as for this wording, we neither affirm it nor negate it. The point is that whenever you see a person who wants to nullify the truth, he has a share in this verse.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they take My signs and that with which they are warned as mockery﴾. "Taking" means making them into something: ﴿My signs﴾ means the Qur'an, and ﴿that with which they are warned﴾ means the punishment with which they were warned. They took them as mockery. For example, the disbelievers mocked when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed about the tree of Zaqqum: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire﴾ [as-Saffat: 64], at its bottom. They laughed: how can a tree grow at the root of the blazing Fire, when it is the furthest thing from fire? Fire is hot and dry, and the tree is moist and cool; how could this be? So they mocked and said: this is the raving of Muhammad, peace be upon him. They took the signs of Allah and what they were warned of as mockery. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it﴾ [as-Saffat: 66], and ﴿then they will drink on top of it from boiling water, drinking like thirsty camels﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 54-55]. We seek refuge with Allah. They fill their bellies from this Zaqqum to completion, and then they burn from thirst, and what are they given to drink? They are given scalding water. ﴿Then drinking on top of it﴾ means on top of what is in their bellies of boiling water, and yet drinking not in the ordinary manner of humans, but like the drinking of thirsty, parched camels (al-Hīm). This is the tree they mocked, from which they fill their bellies in the Fire of Hell.

﴿They take My signs﴾ means the Qur'an, ﴿and that with which they are warned﴾ means what they were warned of concerning the threat, whether the warning came in the Qur'an or in the Sunnah. They took it as mockery, that is, as a laughingstock, a game, and a scorn.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 57:

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord but turned away from them and forgot what his hands had put forth?﴾ The phrase ﴿who is more unjust﴾ has already passed over us at the beginning of the surah, and here it appears again. How do we reconcile the two? ﴿Who is more unjust﴾ ﴿who is more unjust﴾; because ﴿who is more unjust﴾ means "no one is more unjust," and this may seem to be a contradiction. At the beginning of the surah, what did Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say? ﴿Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ And here He says: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord but turned away from them﴾ [al-Kahf 57]. This is a contradiction. The best that has been said about this is that every statement is relative to what is similar to it; that is, "who is more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord and turned away from them" among those who are reminded and then turn away. A person may be reminded of something and turn away, but what is most severe is that he be reminded of what? 

* Students: Of the verses of Allah.

* The Shaykh: Of the verses of Allah, and then he turns away. This is the most severe thing. In fabricating lies, a person may fabricate lies against so-and-so and so-and-so, but the greatest injustice of fabrication is against Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. If you adopt this principle, you will be spared many difficulties.

As for the view that "more unjust" and "more unjust" share the same meaning of injustice, this is open to question, even though it has been said; for it is not possible to say that ﴿who is more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord but turned away from them﴾ equals one who fabricated a lie against Allah.

﴿And who is more unjust than one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord but turned away from them﴾. Are the ﴿verses of his Lord﴾ the cosmic (kawniyyah) or the legislative (shar'iyyah) ones? Both the cosmic and the legislative. The cosmic: that it be said to him that the eclipse of the sun and the moon is a means by which Allah frightens His servants, and he turns away from this and says: "Never! The eclipse of the moon is natural, and the eclipse of the sun is natural; there is no warning and no warner." This is turning away. As for the legislative verses, many are reminded of the verses of Allah but turn away.

﴿And forgot what his hands had put forth﴾: that is, he forgot what his hands had put forth of disbelief, sins, arrogance and other things that prevent him from accepting the truth. For a person, may Allah protect us, the more he plunges into sins, the further he becomes from turning towards the truth, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff 5]. Therefore you must know that among the most severe punishments for sins is that a person be punished with a sickness of the heart, may Allah protect us. If a person is punished by the loss of a beloved one or the loss of a beloved possession, this is undoubtedly a punishment; but if he is punished by the stripping away of the heart, may Allah grant us well-being, this is the most severe punishment. Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

By Allah, what I fear of sins is not them, for they are on the path of pardon and forgiveness;
But what I fear is the stripping away of the heart from adopting this Revelation and the Qur'an.

This is what the sensible person fears. As for other calamities, they are expiations, and what is lost is replaced.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it﴾; ﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾ means: We made. ﴿Over their hearts﴾: whose hearts? Of the one who was reminded of the verses of his Lord and turned away from them; the pronoun is returned to a singular form in consideration of the meaning. ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾: that is, veils, may Allah protect us, ﴿lest they understand it﴾.

* * *

Discussion of what preceded. The words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾. Why did Allah command the angels to prostrate to Adam?

* Student: (...) Out of honour for the children of Adam.

* The Shaykh: Yes, out of honour for Adam and his descendants. If someone says: prostration to other than Allah is shirk, what is the answer?

* The Student: The correct view, O Shaykh (...), in the Qur'an is following the command of Allah, and following the command of Allah is obedience, like the remembrance of Allah when one enters the toilet, and withholding speech; the remembrance of Allah at the toilet is obedience and not disobedience. And if we say..

* The Shaykh: What? You have recited to us this whole world, and what..

* The Student: (...) obedience, O Shaykh.

* The Shaykh: I say to you: how do the angels prostrate to Adam when prostration to other than Allah is shirk?

* The Student: We said: correct, O Shaykh; but there is...

* The Shaykh: Correct? So the angels are polytheists?

* The Student: No; because there was compliance with the command of Allah, O Shaykh, and compliance with the command of Allah is obedience and not shirk.

* The Shaykh: So, then, when Allah commanded it, it was not shirk, and the one who made it shirk is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. It is Allah who made prostration to other than Allah shirk; so when He commands it, it becomes obedience.

If someone says: this is a prostration of greeting, not placing the forehead on the ground, what do we say to him?

* Student: This is what Allah commanded.

* The Shaykh: We say: is your statement a contradiction?

* The Student: A clear contradiction of the apparent meaning of the verse.

* The Shaykh: A contradiction of the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and we cannot turn the speech away from its apparent meaning except with evidence. Clear?

If someone says: Is Iblis one of the angels?

* Student: No, he is not one of the angels.

* The Shaykh: He is not among them?

* The Student: He is not among them.

* The Shaykh: How is his exception from them valid, ﴿except Iblis﴾?

* The Student: It is specified in the verse that Iblis is from the jinn.

* The Shaykh: Yes?

* The Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: This exception is called by the grammarians a disjunctive (munqati') exception. Good.

The interrogative in His words: ﴿Will you then take him﴾?

* Student: The interrogative is for denunciation and reproach.

* The Shaykh: For denunciation.

The benefit of His words: ﴿while they are an enemy to you﴾?

* Student: Inciting and urging the opposition to Iblis and his offspring.

* The Shaykh: Yes, inciting and urging opposition to Iblis; that is, how can you do this, taking him as a protector while he is an enemy? Good.

Is it derived from this that if a person wants to warn someone against something, he should explain its harms to him?

* Student: Yes, O Shaykh, it is derived from it.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is derived from it; and likewise, if he is commanding him to something, he should mention its benefits and advantages, so as to move the soul to abandon what is forbidden and to do what is commanded.

What is the connection of His words: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ with what precedes it?

* Student: It serves as clarification, or as [showing] their lack of knowledge and lack of entitlement.

* The Shaykh: It clarifies their lack of entitlement to be protectors, because they have no share in lordship, right?

Is it derived from this sentence that whoever speaks about the creation of the heavens and the earth, or about the creation of man and the faculties Allah placed in him, we do not accept his word except with evidence?

* Student: Yes.

* The Shaykh: Yes, except with sensory evidence that convinces us.

What is the function of the messengers?

* Student: Conveying, giving glad tidings and warning.

* The Shaykh: Do they have control?

* Student: No, they do not have control.

* The Shaykh: Do they have the guidance of creation?

* Student: No.

* The Shaykh: That is so.

Are the scholars' function preaching, glad tidings and warning, or enabling people to be guided?

* Student: The scholars, O Shaykh, follow the messengers.

* The Shaykh: They follow the messengers; so if the messengers do not have the guidance of creation, then neither do the scholars. Praise be to Allah.

* * *
* Student: The words of the Exalted: ﴿He leaves no small or great thing but that He has enumerated it﴾. Is it taken from it a refutation of those who say that naming sins "minor" (saghira) is not found in the Qur'an?
* The Shaykh: What?

* Student: Some of them say, O Shaykh: the division of sins into minor and major is not found in the texts; what is found is naming some sins as major only, while minor ones are not mentioned. Is a refutation of this taken from the verse?

* The Shaykh: Those who say this have a deficiency in intellect; intellect is not the opposite of madness. ﴿If you avoid the major sins that you are forbidden﴾ [al-Nisa' 31]. Is there a major sin that has no corresponding minor sin?! The answer is no. ﴿Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for minor lapses﴾ [al-Najm 32]. It is clear.

This is analogous to those who say: we say that faith increases and we do not say that it decreases. How can it increase? Can increase be conceived without decrease? It cannot be conceived. As for what has been mentioned, it indicates that the minor sins of disbelievers are not erased, unlike the believer, for if he avoids major sins, his minor sins are erased thereby.

* Student: May Allah pardon you, O Shaykh. If we consider that Allah, the Exalted, created Adam with His hand, and made the angels prostrate to him, out of honour and dignity for him, and if we consider the obedience of the angels to Allah, the Exalted, more than the obedience of many humans, what is the preference between them, O Shaykh? Because if we speak generally, the angels are better; and if we speak particularly: then Adam, whom Allah created with His hand and to whom the angels prostrated?

* The Shaykh: This is a matter on which the scholars differed: is the believing human better, or are the angels better?

As for whether humans in general are better or the angels are better: there is no doubt that the angels are better, because among humans there are believers and disbelievers, while the angels are all believers. But is the believing human better than the angels?

This is a matter people have delved into, and in my view it is among the superfluities of knowledge, and it deserves what is said in His words: ﴿So do not argue concerning them except with an outward argument﴾ [al-Kahf 22]. Shaykh al-Islam, may Allah have mercy on him, says: in the end humans are better, and in the beginning the angels are better, because no disobedience to Allah has proceeded from the angels, while the angels were created from light, and humans had sins proceed from them and were created from dust. But I say: there is no need for this. As for his statement, peace and blessings be upon him: "Allah, the Exalted, said: whoever remembers Me in a gathering, I remember him in a gathering better than theirs," it does not indicate the absolute preference of the angels over humans; rather, the better gathering is only those specific ones.

* Student: May Allah reward you with good. Regarding His words: ﴿And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration﴾ [Yusuf 100]. Is there not in the verse that Allah commanded them, as in this verse?

* The Shaykh: Well said. The story of Yusuf, peace be upon him, is that he ﴿raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration﴾, and it is apparent that they prostrated with their foreheads.

The answer: this was in the law of those before us; or it is said that, in their astonishment, they intended bowing, but they fell to the ground; or it is said that this dream was shown to Yusuf earlier, when he saw eleven stars, the sun and the moon prostrating to him, so this was taken as an interpretation of their prostration to him, just as Ibrahim, peace be upon him, took his dream as an interpretation of the sacrifice of his son.

* * *
Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings﴾ [al-Kahf 57].
﴿Indeed, We have placed﴾ means: We made. ﴿Over their hearts﴾: that is, the hearts of those who, when reminded of the verses of Allah, turn away from them. And at that point, does the pronoun return to the wording or to the meaning? It returns to the meaning; because "man" (مَن), whether it is a relative pronoun or a conditional, permits the pronoun referring to it to return to its wording, making it singular, and to return to its meaning, making it plural or dual according to context. Have you understood?

If you say: "I like the one who stood (يعجبني من قام)", here did we observe? Where are your understandings, O people?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: "I like the one who stood (يعجبني من قام)": did we observe [the wording]?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Fine. If you say: "I like the two who stood (يعجبني مَن قاما)".

* Student: The meaning.

* The Shaykh: The meaning.

If you say: "I like those who stood (يعجبني من قاموا)".

* Student: The meaning.

* The Shaykh: The meaning.

"I like those women who stood (يعجبني من قمن)?"

* Student: The meaning.

* The Shaykh: The meaning.

Sometimes the meaning is observed once and the wording another time, and the meaning is balanced; that is, pronouns may return observing both considerations within a single context.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds﴾ [al-Talaq 11]. Did he observe the wording?

* Students: The wording.

* The Shaykh: He observed the wording; that is, when it is singular, it observes the wording.

﴿He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Talaq 11]: the wording or the meaning?

* Student: The meaning.

* Another student: The wording.

* The Shaykh: "He will admit him (يُدْخِلْهُ)"?

* Students: The wording.

* The Shaykh: The wording. "Gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever" [al-Talaq 11]?

* Students: The meaning.

* The Shaykh: The meaning.

﴿Allah has certainly provided excellently for him as provision﴾ [al-Talaq 11]?

* Students: The wording.

* The Shaykh: The wording. Look: the context is one, yet observe the wording first, then the meaning second, then the wording third.

* * *
He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings lest they understand it﴾ [al-Kahf 57]: coverings. ﴿Lest they understand it﴾: that is, lest they comprehend the Qur'an and so do not understand it. In this there is an exhortation to understanding the Qur'an, and that a person should read the Qur'an and learn its meaning, as the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, did not go beyond ten verses until they had learned them along with what they contain of knowledge and action.

﴿And in their ears is deafness﴾ [al-Kahf 57]. Look, may Allah protect us: the hearts have a covering over them, and the ears have deafness in them so they do not hear; so they neither hear the truth nor understand it.

﴿And in their ears is deafness. And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, ever﴾ [al-Kahf 57]. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: if you call them, O Muhammad, to guidance, ﴿they will never be guided then﴾; that is, as long as their hearts are under coverings and their ears have deafness, they will never be guided. And from where would guidance reach them? The ears do not hear the truth, and the hearts do not understand the truth, and we seek refuge in Allah: from where would they be guided?

If someone says: does this contain despair for the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that even if he calls, it will not be accepted from him; or does it contain consolation for him?

The second: it contains consolation for him, and that if these people do not accept the truth, then do not concern yourself with them; they will never be guided, then, ever.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 58:

﴿And your Lord is the Oft-Forgiving, the Possessor of mercy. If He were to call them to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment.﴾ [al-Kahf: 58]. This also contains consolation for the Messenger ﷺ from another angle: the Prophet ﷺ may say, "Why have they not been hastened to punishment? How do they deny me while I am the Messenger of Allah and they have not been punished?"

So Allah explains to him that the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is ﴿al-Ghafur﴾ (the Oft-Forgiving), i.e., the One who covers sins, ﴿dhu ar-rahmah﴾ (the Possessor of mercy), i.e., the One who is gentle with the sinner. For this reason He said: ﴿If He were to call them to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened for them the punishment.﴾ Because if Allah wanted to call people to account for what they have earned, He would have hastened the punishment for them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has explained this punishment in other verses, when He said: ﴿And if Allah were to call the people to account for what they have earned, He would not leave upon its back [the earth] a single creature﴾ [Fatir: 45], meaning He would have destroyed them immediately, ﴿but He defers them to a specified term﴾ [Fatir: 45].

﴿Rather, for them is an appointed time, and they will find no refuge other than it﴾ [al-Kahf: 58]. ﴿Bal⁠﴾ (rather) here is for nullification, an idrab ibtali (a retracting transition): i.e., rather, they will not escape punishment when it is deferred from them.

﴿For them is an appointed time; they will find no refuge other than it﴾: i.e., no shelter (ma'lja'). When is this? On the Day of Resurrection. It may also be that what befalls the disbelievers at the hands of the believers, such as killing, is meant, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people. And He will remove the rage of their hearts﴾ [at-Tawbah: 14-15]. So we say: ﴿Rather, for them is an appointed time; they will find no refuge other than it﴾. We say: this may mean what will befall them of killing and seizure in this world, or what will befall them on the Day of Resurrection from which there is no escape.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 59:

﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they did wrong﴾ [al-Kahf 18:59], ﴿Those cities — We destroyed them﴾. A questioner may say: there is a difficulty here. ﴿Those cities — We destroyed them﴾, and "cities" (al-qura) are inanimate, and an inanimate thing is not referred back to by a plural pronoun. That is, you would not say, for example: "These houses — We built them (plural)." No, you say: "These houses — We built them (feminine singular)," "those cities — We destroyed them (feminine singular)." So why did He say: ﴿We destroyed them﴾ (ahlaknahum)?

We say: He said this because the ones who are destroyed are the people of the cities. This is clear evidence that "al-qura" (cities) may be intended to mean their inhabitants, and may also be intended to mean the gathered buildings. Do you understand? The word "qura" (cities), now and then, is sometimes intended to mean its inhabitants, and sometimes it is intended to mean the gathered dwellings. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the cities until He sent to their mother [city] a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would not destroy the cities unless their people were wrongdoers﴾ [al-Qasas 28:59]. The meaning of "cities" here is their inhabitants, because Allah said in the same verse: ﴿unless its people were wrongdoers﴾. And it may be intended to mean the gathered buildings; the gathered [community] is also called a city (qarya).

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And those cities — We destroyed them when they did wrong﴾, and the meaning of "wrong" here is disbelief. ﴿And We appointed for their destruction an appointed time﴾ [al-Kahf 18:59]; that is, We appointed a time for their destruction. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, does what He wills: if He wills, He hastens the punishment, and if He wills, He delays it. But when the appointed time comes, it is not postponed. For this reason Noah, peace be upon him, said to his people: ﴿He will forgive you some of your sins and defer you to a specified term. Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, cannot be deferred﴾ [Nuh 71:4]. When it comes, it is impossible for it to be deferred; but it is a specific term fixed by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at the time that His wisdom requires.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 60:

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Moses said to his young servant, "I will not cease [traveling] until I reach the junction of the two seas, or I will continue for a long period."﴾ [al-Kahf: 60] ﴿When he said﴾ is an object of a verb that is omitted, and the implied meaning is: "Remember when he said." This surah, glory be to Allah, contains a number of stories. Moses, son of 'Imran, peace be upon him, once addressed the Children of Israel, and one of them stood up and said: "Is there anyone on the earth more knowledgeable than you?" He said: "No."

He said, "No," on the basis of what? On the basis of his assumption that there was no one on the earth more knowledgeable than him, so Allah rebuked him for that. Why did he not refer the knowledge to Allah? Because "over every possessor of knowledge is one who is more knowing" (Qur'an 12:76). No human has absolute knowledge. Furthermore, his statement "No" is open to scrutiny from another angle: did he travel the entire earth and know that no one was more knowledgeable than him? No. Moreover, is there no one more knowledgeable than him in every matter? No. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: "Indeed, I have a servant who is more knowledgeable than you." Where is he? He said: "At the junction of the two seas," and He described to him a sign. What is the sign?

The sign is that he would lose the fish. So he took a fish with him in a basket (maktal), meaning something like a basket, and he and his young servant Yusha' ibn Nun set out. This is related in al-Bukhari. Where did they set out to? To the junction of the two seas, so that he could see who this person was who was more knowledgeable than him, and so that he could learn from him as well. Then they both took shelter at a rock and slept, and the fish was in the basket. When they awoke, in their haste, they did not search the basket, and the fish, by the command of Allah, came out and entered the sea. The rest of the story will come, Allah willing, in the next lesson.

* * *
In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and all his companions. And I ask Allah the Exalted to bless us in this noble Qur'an.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears is deafness.﴾ What is the meaning of "akinnah"?

* Student: Plural of kinnat, which are coverings.

* Shaykh: Plural of kinn, which are coverings.

Did Allah place these coverings because of them, or by mere will?

* Student: No, because of them.

* Shaykh: The evidence?

* Student: The evidence is ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided﴾.

* Shaykh: No, the evidence?

* Student: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people at all, but it is the people who wrong themselves﴾ [Yunus: 44].

* Shaykh: No.

* Student: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾.

* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5], and there are similar verses: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13].

Does the verse indicate that it is very important for a person to understand the Noble Qur'an and not merely recite it?

* Student: Yes, the verse is evidence for this.

* Shaykh: What is the evidence?

* Student: His saying ﴿lest they understand it﴾, because they were punished...

* Shaykh: ﴿Coverings lest they understand it﴾ is like this?

It is the custom of the righteous predecessors (salaf) that they?

* Student: That they would recite ten verses and not...

* Shaykh: They would not go beyond them.

* Student: Until they knew their meanings (...).

* Shaykh: And acting upon them. May Allah bless you.

Regarding His saying: ﴿And if you call them to guidance, they will never be guided, then, ever﴾?

* Student: This does not contain despair for the Prophet, peace be upon him, but rather consolation for him.

* Shaykh: It contains consolation for the Messenger ﷺ and not despair for him. The meaning is that they will not be guided, because He, glory be to Him, knew that they would not be guided, so do not grieve over them.

His Exalted saying: ﴿And those cities—We destroyed them when they wronged.﴾ What is meant by "the cities"?

* Student: The people of the cities.

* Shaykh: Like what? Do you not know a city that Allah destroyed?

* Student: Yes, like...

* Shaykh: The people of Noah.

* Student: The people of Noah, the people of 'Ad, the people of Thamud.

* Shaykh: Yes, and others.

Is it derived from the noble verse that wrongdoing is a cause of destruction?

* Student: Yes indeed.

* Shaykh: How so?

* Student: His saying ﴿when they wronged﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿When they wronged﴾, so Allah destroyed them when they wronged.

His saying: ﴿And We appointed for their destruction a appointed time﴾. What is the meaning of this, or its connection to what precedes it?

* Student: That is: a term (ajal).

* Shaykh: A term, yes, lest someone say: does punishment befall from the moment of wronging, or is it delayed, or the like? So it is said: Indeed Allah, Exalted, has appointed for it a set time.

His saying: ﴿When Moses said to his young servant﴾. Who is this young man? Is he his son?

* Student: No, he is not his son.

* Shaykh: Who?

* Student: Yusha' ibn Nun, O Shaykh.

* Shaykh: His name is Yusha' ibn Nun, but what is his relation to him?

* Student: A young servant of Moses.

* Shaykh: That is, a servant to him. Good.

The cause of this statement?

* Student: Moses said to his young servant that he (...) the Children of Israel (...), so he said to him—this is Yusha' ibn Nun—"Is there anyone more knowledgeable than you?" He said, "No one more knowledgeable than me." Allah, Exalted, informed him, and Allah, Exalted, said: He will find His servant at the junction of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than him, so he went.

* * *
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when Moses said to his young servant, "I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas or continue for a long period."﴾ [al-Kahf: 60]
﴿I will not cease﴾ means: I will not stop. The predicate is omitted, and the implied meaning is: "I will not stop traveling until I reach this, or I continue for years." He made the goal one of two things: either he reaches the junction of the two seas even in a short time, or he remains for long periods—perhaps eighty years or more—until he reaches this man whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, informed him of.

And what is the junction of the two seas? It is said: its location is known only to Allah, but Moses knew it. It is also said: it is the meeting point of the Red Sea with the Mediterranean Sea, and previously there was land between them until the canal was opened. And it is not unlikely that he was told: "A servant of Ours is at the junction of the two seas," and he went to this place.

﴿Or I continue for a long period﴾: "or" here indicates a division, meaning: either this or that. It is also said that "or" means "except," i.e., "until I reach the junction of the two seas, unless I continue for a long period before reaching it." But the first meaning is more sound.

﴿Or I continue for a long period﴾: so what did he do? He prepared himself for that and set out.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 61:

﴿فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا﴾ ﴾ أي: بين البحرين، ﴿نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا﴾ [الكهف ٦١]، ﴿نَسِيَا﴾ أضاف الفعل إليهما، مع أن الناسي هو الفتى، وليس موسى، لكن القوم إذا كانوا في شأن واحد وفي عمل واحد نُسِب فعل الواحد منهم أو الطائفة منهم إلى الجميع، ولهذا يخاطب الله عز وجل بني إسرائيل في عهد الرسول ﷺ، فيقول: ﴿وَإِذْ فَرَقْنَا بِكُمُ الْبَحْرَ فَأَنْجَيْنَاكُمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ [البقرة٥٠]، ﴿وَإِذْ قُلْتُمْ يَا مُوسَى لَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لَكَ حَتَّى نَرَى اللَّهَ جَهْرَةً﴾ [البقرة ٥٥]، مع أنهم ما قالوا هذا لكن قاله أجدادهم.

﴿نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا﴾ نسيان ذهول أو نسيان ترك؟ نسيان ذهول، وليس نسيان ترك، وهذا من حكمة الله عز وجل أن الله أنساهما ذلك لحكمة، ﴿نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا﴾.

وهذا الحوت جعله الله سبحانه وتعالى علامة لموسى، أنك متى فقدت الحوت فثم مجمع البحرين، وهذا الحوت سبق لنا في الليلة الماضية أنه كان في مِكْتَل، وكان يقتاتان منه، لما وصلا إلى مكان ما ناما فيه عند صخرة، فلما استيقظا وإذا الحوت ليس موجودًا، لكنه -أي الفتى- لم يتفقد المكتل، ونسي شأنه وأمره، هذا الحوت -سبحان الله- طلع، خرج من المكتل ودخل في البحر، وجعل يسير في البحر والبحر ينحاز عنه.

﴿فَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ سَرَبًا﴾ [الكهف ٦١]؛ أي: مثل السرب، السرب: السرداب؛ يعني أنه يشق الماء ولا يتلاءم الماء، وصفه بعض التابعين قال: هكذا؛ يعني: حجز، وهذا من آيات الله، وإلا فقد جرت العادة أن الحوت إذا انغمس في البحر أيش يعمل البحر؟ يتلاءم عليه، لكن هذا الحوت من آيات الله، أولًا: إذا كان قد ذبح أو قد مات وأنهما يقتاتان منه، كونه حيي، وقام ودخل البحر وصار طريقه على هذا الوجه، هذا من آيات الله عز وجل.

﴿فَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ﴾، ﴿فَاتَّخَذَ﴾ الضمير يعود على أيش؟ على الحوت، ﴿سَبِيلَهُ﴾: طريقه، ﴿فِي الْبَحْرِ سَرَبًا﴾ يعني: مثل السَرَب، السرب ما نسميه إحنا بالسرداب؛ يعني الشق الطويل.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 62:

﴿So when they had passed on﴾ [al-Kahf 18:62]: the subject (al-fa'il) is Musa and his servant, and "passed on" (jawaza) means they went beyond that place. Musa said to his servant, ﴿Bring us our morning meal﴾ [al-Kahf 18:62]. There is no doubt that this was in the morning, because al-ghada' (the morning meal) is the food eaten in the early part of the day.

﴿Indeed, we have suffered fatigue from this journey of ours﴾ [al-Kahf 18:62]: i.e., nasab means tiredness. As for his words ﴿from this journey of ours﴾, what is meant is not the whole of their journey from the moment they set out, but from the moment they left the rock. That is why he asked for the morning meal: from the moment they left the rock, they became tired and asked for food. The people of knowledge said: this is one of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for they had travelled a long distance before that without becoming tired, and when they passed beyond the place, they quickly grew weary, so that they would not go further away from the place.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 63:

﴿So when they had passed on, he said to his servant, "Bring us our morning meal; we have certainly suffered fatigue from this journey of ours."﴾ ﴿He said, "Did you see? When we retreated to the rock, indeed I forgot the fish."﴾ "Ara'ayta" (أرأيت) means: pay attention, or has a meaning similar to it. ﴿When we retreated to the rock﴾ means we returned to it and took it as a resting place, because they had both slept. ﴿Indeed I forgot the fish.﴾ What is the meaning of "forgot"? It means I forgot to check on it and attend to its matter; otherwise the fish was well known, it was in the basket, but he forgot whether it remained or had not remained.

﴿And none caused me to forget it except Satan, that I should mention it﴾ The phrase ﴿that I should mention it﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the pronoun (ha') in ﴿caused me to forget it﴾. That is: none caused me to forget its mention except Satan.

﴿And it took its way into the sea in an amazing manner﴾ ﴿Its way﴾ means its path. ﴿In an amazing manner﴾ means a place of wonder, and it is a place of wonder: flowing water through which this fish passed, and its path became a tunnel. So this path was a tunnel for the fish, and an amazement for Musa and his servant, and also an amazement for us; because water normally closes up behind what passes through it, but this fish, by the permission of God, did not let the water close up.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 64:

﴿And he took his way in the sea, a wonder (63). He said: "That is what we were seeking"﴾ [al-Kahf: 63, 64]. Musa, upon him be peace, says: ﴿That is what we were seeking﴾, meaning: that is what we were looking for; because Allah had informed him that when the fish was lost, that would be the place of their meeting with whom? With al-Khadir (the servant of Allah whom Musa met, according to the sura), ﴿He said: "That is what we were seeking." So they went back, retracing their footsteps, [following] their track﴾ [al-Kahf: 64]. Meaning: he returned, after having covered a distance in which he became weary.

﴿They went back on their footsteps﴾ means: they were tracing their steps, so that the place where they had sheltered would not be lost to them. ﴿Retracing their footsteps﴾ means: they were following the trail.

﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants﴾ [al-Kahf 18:65], who was al-Khidr, as has been authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Is ﴿a servant from among Our servants﴾ one of the righteous worshippers? Or one of the friends of God (awliya') who have karamat (miraculous gifts granted to saints)? Or a prophet? Or a messenger? All of these are possible, but the texts indicate that he was neither a messenger nor a prophet. Rather, he was a righteous servant to whom God granted karamat, in order to show that Musa did not encompass all knowledge, and that a great deal of knowledge escaped him.

﴿We gave him mercy from Us and taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾ [al-Kahf 18:65]. ﴿We gave him mercy from Us﴾ means that God made him one of His friends. ﴿And taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾ means knowledge that people do not perceive, knowledge specific to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, namely the knowledge of the unseen in this particular story, and it is not the knowledge of prophethood. However, it is a special knowledge, because this knowledge which al-Khidr was given access to cannot be grasped. Isn't that so? It cannot be grasped. It is not something built upon the perceptible, such that the future is built upon the present; it is something hidden. ﴿And taught him knowledge from Our presence﴾ means information that human beings cannot access.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Musa said to him, "May I follow you, on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, [some] right guidance?"﴾ [al-Kahf 18:66]. Reflect on this courtesy (adab) from Musa, peace be upon him, even though Musa is more excellent than him, ﴿and he was honored with Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab 33:69]. Yet he is gentle in this manner, because he would be taking from him knowledge that Musa did not possess. In this is evidence that the seeker of knowledge should be gentle with his shaykh and his teacher, and treat him with honor.

﴿May I follow you, on condition﴾: he said, ﴿May I follow you﴾, and this is a request, a gentle request. He also made clear to him that he did not wish to follow him in order to eat of his food and drink of his drink. No, ﴿on condition that you teach me of what you have been taught, [some] right guidance﴾.

Al-Khidr, there is no doubt, would be pleased by one who takes knowledge from him, and every person whom Allah has given knowledge should be pleased that this knowledge is taken from him, because knowledge taken from a person during his lifetime benefits him after his death, as came in the authentic hadith: "When a person dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: ongoing charity (sadaqah jariyah), or knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him."

(67-69)

So he said to him: ﴿Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience over that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ [al-Kahf 18:67-68].

﴿Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me﴾, and he explained to him his excuse for being unable [to be patient], so he said: ﴿And how can you have patience over that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾. And where is the evidence for al-Khidr that Musa had not encompassed that in knowledge? Because he said: ﴿on condition that you teach me﴾, and this indicates that he has no knowledge of what al-Khidr has. So he said: ﴿And how can you have patience over that which you do not encompass in knowledge?﴾ [68]. He said: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter﴾ [al-Kahf 18:68-69].

What Musa, peace be upon him, said, he said within himself at that moment, that he would be patient, but he attached it to the will of Allah, so that this would not be self-reliance and self-admiration. ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills﴾. This is like the statement of Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when his father said to him: ﴿Indeed, I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you﴾ [al-Saffat 37:102], he said: ﴿O father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, what?﴾ [He said:] ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, of the patient﴾ [al-Saffat 37:102]. Musa, peace be upon him, said to al-Khidr: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient﴾, and also: I will be patient with what you do and I will carry out what you command.

﴿And I will not disobey you in any matter﴾: he promised him two things: patience with what he does, and second, compliance with what he commands and abstention from what he forbids.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 70:

﴿And he [Khidr] said: "Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me. And how can you have patience about that which you do not encompass in knowledge?" [Musa] said: "You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in any order."﴾ [al-Kahf: 67, 69]

Hmm, I need to correct this: the passage as given is the commentary on the verse, so the translation should be the commentary text itself. Here is the faithful translation:

﴿And I will not disobey you in any order (69). He said: "If you follow me, then do not ask me about anything until I myself mention it to you."﴾ [al-Kahf: 69, 70]; meaning: until I mention to you the reason. ﴿If you follow me﴾, and it is known that he would follow him. ﴿Then do not ask me about anything﴾, whatever I do, do not ask me about it ﴿until I myself mention it to you﴾, and ﴿until﴾ here indicates a limit; meaning: until I mention to you an explanation of it. This is a instruction from a teacher to one who learns from him: that he should not hasten to respond to his teacher, but rather wait until the matter is explained to him. Without doubt, this is among the etiquettes of the student: that he not hasten to respond until the matter becomes clear, ﴿until I myself mention it to you﴾.

﴿So they set out﴾ [al-Kahf: 71]. (انطلقا) Who is the subject? Musa and al-Khidr. He is silent about the young man. Did the young man fall behind, or did he ride along? But since he was a follower, he was not mentioned. What appears to be the case, and Allah knows best, is that he was a follower, but since he had no connection to the matter, and the principal figure is Musa, his mention was omitted. He too is a follower. ﴿So they set out, until when they boarded the ship, he tore it open﴾. That is, they were walking along the seashore, then a ship passed by and they boarded it. When they boarded the ship, al-Khidr stood up and tore it open. Did he tear it open with a mikhraq (a drill)?

No, rather he pulled out one of its planks through which water would enter. Musa said to him: ﴿Have you torn it open to drown its people?﴾ [al-Kahf: 71]. This is an objection. An objection from whom? From Musa to al-Khidr, even though al-Khidr had said to him: ﴿You will find me, if Allah wills, patient﴾, yet he did not remain patient, because this is a grave problem: a ship in the sea, which he tears open so that it drowns.

The lam in His words ﴿to drown﴾ (لِتُغْرِقَ) is not a lam of purpose (ta'lil), but the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah). That is, if you tear it open, it will drown. Otherwise, there is no doubt that Musa, peace be upon him, did not know al-Khidr's purpose, and there is also no doubt that he knew al-Khidr did not want to drown its people, for if he had wanted to drown its people, the first to drown would have been he and Musa. But the lam here is the lam of consequence, and the lam of consequence occurs in many places, even in the Qur'an, such as the saying of Allah the Most High: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas: 8]. If we asked any person: did the family of Pharaoh pick up Musa so that he would become an enemy and a grief to them? Never. Rather, this is the end result.

﴿to drown its people. You have certainly done a thing, imr﴾ [al-Kahf: 71]. That is, a great thing. For Musa, peace be upon him, was strong and firm regarding the cause of Allah. So he objected to him and made clear that his act would have the consequence of drowning, and he increased the rebuke in His words: ﴿You have certainly done a thing, imr﴾, that is, a great thing. The sentence here is emphasized with three emphatics, O brothers: three emphatics: the lam (of emphasis), qad, and the implied oath indicated by the lam. We said: great. From this is the saying of Abu Sufyan to Heraclius when he related to him about the Messenger ﷺ, described to him his condition, his attributes, and his noble character, and then he departed with his people. He said: «Indeed the affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become great; indeed the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him». By Ibn Abi Kabshah he meant the Messenger ﷺ. And amira amruhu (أمِر أمره) means: it became great. ﴿You have certainly done a thing, imr﴾.

﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ [al-Kahf: 72].

The answer: *balā* (بلى), or *lā* (لا)?

* Students: *Balā* (بلى).

* The Shaykh: Musa apologized.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 73:

﴿He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.﴾ [al-Kahf: 73] ﴿Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot.﴾ The reason for Musa's forgetting is that the matter was so great that it overwhelmed him: the ship being damaged while he was on its deck, with al-Khadir on its deck and its people with him. This kind of thing necessarily causes a person to forget what came before, because of how strongly such an event impacts the soul. He made an excuse: ﴿Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot.﴾ That is, for my forgetting. For this reason we say, in the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of (مَا, ma), that it is a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), meaning: for my forgetting of that, which is your saying: ﴿Indeed, you will not be able to have patience with me.﴾ ﴿And do not burden me with difficulty in my affair.﴾ That is, do not make things heavy on me and make matters hard for me. And this, Allah knows best, was a preface to what comes after.

﴿So they set out﴾ [al-Kahf 18:74]. Set out from where? From the ship, after it had anchored at the harbour. ﴿Until, when they met a boy and he killed him, [Moses] said, "Have you killed an innocent soul without [its having killed] another?"﴾ [al-Kahf 18:74]. Here he said ﴿فَقَتَلَهُ﴾ (faqatalahu, "and he killed him") and did not say ﴿قَتَلَهُ﴾ (qatalahu, "he killed him"). In the ship he said ﴿خَرَقَهَا﴾ (kharaqaha, "he damaged it") and did not say ﴿فَخَرَقَهَا﴾ (fakharaqaha). The reason is that the killing of a soul is treated as something to be considered for a little while, as if something happened before the killing and then he killed him, the boy, the young child. Moses, peace be upon him, did not show patience.

﴿He said, "Have you killed an innocent soul without [its having killed] another? You have certainly done a terrible thing."﴾ In one reading it is ﴿زَاكِيَةً﴾ (zakiyah) instead of ﴿زَكِيَّةً﴾ (zakiyyah). The word ﴿زَكِيَّةً﴾: because he was a young boy, and a young boy has good deeds recorded for him while bad deeds are not recorded against him. So he is pure (zakiyy) because he is young; bad deeds are not recorded against him and good deeds are recorded for him.

﴿Without [its having killed] another﴾ means that he had not killed anyone, so that he [the boy] should be killed in retaliation. But if he had killed, would he be killed or not? Our law is that he is not killed. One who is not mukallaf (legally accountable, not yet bound by the obligations of the law) is not killed for intentional homicide, because he has no intent (amd).

﴿You have certainly done a terrible thing﴾. This expression is stronger than the first one. What did the first one say? ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إِمْرًا﴾ (laqad ji'ta shay'an imra, "you have certainly done a grave thing"). But here he said ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا نُكْرًا﴾ (laqad ji'ta shay'an nukra), that is, a great abomination (munkaran 'azheeman) in that you killed a soul. The difference between this and that is that damaging the ship may or may not lead to drowning, and in fact the ship did not sink. But killing a soul is an abomination with no possibility of doubt.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Karim) on Surah 18 (al-Kahf), verse 75:**

﴿Indeed, you have done a terrible thing (74)﴾ ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾ [al-Kahf: 74, 75]. Here there is a stronger rebuke directed at Musa. In the first instance he said, ﴿Did I not say that you…﴾, and in the second he said, ﴿Did I not say to you…﴾. The meaning is: it is as if you did not understand, and will not understand. This is why people distinguish between the two sentences. If you speak to a person about something and he opposes you, you say the first way: "Did I not tell you that you…" But if you say: "Did I not tell you…", the meaning is: the instruction reached you in a way that leaves no room for doubt, and despite that you opposed it. So al-Khidr's rebuke of Musa in the second case is what? Stronger. ﴿He said, "Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me?"﴾

Then Musa said to him, when he saw that he had no excuse left: ﴿He said: If I ask you about anything after this, then do not keep me as your companion﴾ [al-Kahf 18:76]; meaning: prevent me from accompanying you. In Musa's words ﴿do not keep me as your companion﴾ there is an indication that he (peace be upon him) regarded himself as lower in rank than the other, for otherwise he would have said: "If I ask you about anything after this, then what? Then I will not accompany you." Instead he said ﴿do not keep me as your companion﴾, meaning: and prevent me from that.

﴿You have indeed reached from my side an excuse﴾ [al-Kahf 18:76], meaning: you have arrived at a state in which you are excused. For how many times did he object to him? Twice, even though Musa had committed himself not to ask, when he said: ﴿He said: You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter﴾.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 77:**

﴿So they both set out until, when they came to the people of a town, they asked its people for food, but they refused to entertain them.﴾ Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not specify the town, so there is no need for us to search for this town. We say: it is a town that Allah left unspecified, so we leave it unspecified. ﴿They asked its people for food﴾, meaning: they requested food from its people. ﴿But they refused to entertain them﴾. There is no doubt that this is contrary to the perfection of faith, because the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him honour his guest." Yet these people refused to host them. Their recompense should have been that they be treated only in the same manner as they behaved, but the matter turned out otherwise, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, facilitates for His believing servant that which brings about good.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The Prophet ﷺ sent out a detachment, and they alighted as guests with a people, but the people refused to host them, so they moved to one side. Then Allah afflicted the chief of that people with a scorpion that stung him, and it was severe. Some of them said to the others: 'Is there anyone who can perform ruqyah (incantation healing)?' They said: 'We know of no one except these men of the group.' So they came to the Companions and said: 'Verily our chief has been stung. Is there anyone among you who can perform ruqyah?' They said: 'Yes, but we will not perform it except for such-and-such a number of sheep.' He said: 'That is yours.' So one of the men of the detachment went and began to recite Surah al-Fatihah over this stung man, and he rose as if he had been freed from a fetter."

Consider the gentleness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in that He facilitated hospitality for the Companions despite those who refused to host them. Their companion was not harmed by anything except the pain of the sting, which ended by the man's recitation over him. The point is that Musa and al-Khidr asked the people of the town for food, but they refused to host them. Allah says: ﴿They found in it a wall about to collapse, so he set it upright﴾. ﴿A wall about to collapse﴾: how can it wish to collapse? Does the wall have a will?

The answer: Yes, it has a will, and that is its inclination, for its inclination indicates a desire to fall. Do not be surprised that inanimate objects have a will, for Uhud, of which the Prophet ﷺ said: "It loves us and we love it," was inanimate, and love is an attribute beyond mere will.

As for the view of some people who permit metaphor (majaz) in the Qur'an and say that this is a figure of speech (kinayah) and that the wall has no will, there is no basis for it.

﴿About to collapse﴾, meaning it was leaning and about to fall. ﴿So he set it upright﴾: who set it upright? Al-Khidr set it upright. But how did he set it upright? Allah knows best. It may be that he set it upright with his own hand, and that Allah gave him strength, and the wall became straight; or it may be that he built it with ordinary construction. The point is that he set it upright.

﴿He said: "If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it."﴾ This expression is very gentle, unlike the first expression. He did not object to his rebuilding it, nor did he say: "How will you rebuild it when they refused to host us?" Rather he said: ﴿If you had wished﴾, and this is undoubtedly a refined, indirect manner of speech, ﴿If you had wished, you could have taken a wage for it﴾, because he, peace and blessings be upon him, had already put forward what prevents him from objecting to al-Khidr.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 78:

﴿He said, "This is the parting between me and you."﴾ The one who said it was al-Khidr. He means: what is between me and you has ended, so there is no companionship. ﴿I will inform you﴾, i.e., I will inform you soon, ﴿of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.﴾ I said "I will inform you soon" because the particle sīn (the prefix sa- indicating the near future) indicates nearness, unlike sawfa, and it also conveys, along with nearness, certainty. ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.﴾ "Ta'wil" means: its tafsir (explanation) and the clarification of its meaning.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 79:

﴿As for the boat﴾ [Al-Kahf: 79], and he means by it the boat that he damaged, so what is the "al" (the definite article) in "as-safinah" (the boat) for?

* Student: For the prior mention (al-'ahd al-dhikri).

* The Shaykh: For the prior mention, yes. ﴿As for the boat﴾ means: the one he damaged. ﴿It belonged to poor people who worked on the sea﴾; meaning they sought their livelihood by it. "Masakin" means poor people in need, and the plural is at least three; it may be three, ten, twenty or thirty. Its exact number is not necessary for us to know.

﴿who worked on the sea. So I wished to damage it﴾; meaning to make a defect in it. Why? He said: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾. ﴿So I wished to damage it﴾, so that when it passed by this king, he would say: this is a defective boat, I have no need of it, because he only takes the sound, good boats. As for this one, he has no need of it. From this, people have derived that a person who fears for himself the evil eye should not display himself in a way that attracts attention, out of fear of the evil eye. That is, he should not wear very beautiful clothes that attract attention, or adorn himself in a way that draws the eye. For instance, if we supposed that this man had two large, beautiful eyes with strong sight, would we say to him: walk with your eyes closed?

* Students: He wears glasses.

* The Shaykh: He may wear glasses, or if he does not have glasses, he reduces how wide he opens his eyes, so that he is not harmed. In any case, he has a point of view. The action of al-Khidr has a justification, and from it a great benefit is derived: the sacrifice of part of a thing to repair the rest of it. Sacrificing part of a thing to repair the remainder is permissible, and doctors now practice it. You find, for example, that they take a piece from the thigh to repair something in the face or the head or the like, and there is no harm in it.

And the scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, derived from this that if an endowment (waqf) is ruined and destroyed, there is no harm in selling part of it and using the proceeds to repair the rest.
