﴿So I wished to damage it, and there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾. So the difficulty regarding the matter of the boat is now resolved.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 80:

﴿And as for the boy, his parents were believers﴾ [al-Kahf: 80], the boy was young, his parents were believers. ﴿So we feared that he would overburden them with rebellion and disbelief.﴾ ﴿We feared﴾: here He says it in the plural, and with respect to al-Khidr it is an actual event, while with respect to Musa it is an expected one. As for the ship, He said ﴿So I intended﴾ and did not say "we intended," because Musa could not have been expected to intend that. But Musa, peace be upon him, and other reformers, fear that a person may disbelieve because of some matter. So this, and Allah knows best, is the reason why ﴿I intended﴾ is in the singular and ﴿We feared﴾ is in the plural.

﴿So we feared that he would overburden them with rebellion and disbelief﴾. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, informed him that the outcome of this boy would be disbelief, and that he might overburden his parents, meaning he might compel them to rebellion and disbelief, either out of his parents' love for him or for other reasons. Otherwise, the general rule is that the father influences the son, but the son may also influence the father, just as the general rule is that the husband influences his wife, and the wife may also influence her husband.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 81:

﴿Then we intended that their Lord would replace them with one better than him in purity and nearer in kinship.﴾ ﴾ [al-Kahf: 81]; meaning: if we killed him, then with Allah is what is better and more lasting. ﴿That their Lord would replace them with one better than him in purity﴾, i.e., in religion, ﴿and nearer in kinship﴾, i.e., in family ties. The meaning is that he (Khidr) and Musa (may Allah exalt his mention), with certainty regarding Khidr and by estimation regarding Musa, intended that Allah would give them in exchange someone more righteous than them in religion and more closely bound to them in kinship, ﴿and nearer in kinship﴾.

There remains a third point. Now that we know the reasoning behind the killing of the boy, can it be derived from this that a disbeliever may be killed out of fear that his disbelief will spread among the people? Yes, without doubt. The one who calls to disbelief may be killed out of fear that his disbelief will spread among the people.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 82:

He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city﴾ [al-Kahf 82], two young orphan boys whose father had died. ﴿And beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾. Beneath what? The wall. ﴿A treasure﴾, i.e., hidden wealth.

﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord﴾. Allah, may He be exalted, willed that they should reach their maturity, i.e., that they should attain full growth and come of age, reaching the age of ashudd (maturity), which according to many scholars is forty years.

The one who calls to disbelief is to be killed, out of fear that he will spread his disbelief among the people.

He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city﴾ [al-Kahf 82], two young orphan boys whose father had died.

﴿And beneath it was a treasure belonging to them﴾. Beneath what? The wall. ﴿A treasure﴾, i.e., hidden wealth, ﴿a treasure belonging to them﴾.

﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord﴾. Allah, may He be exalted, willed ﴿that they should reach their maturity﴾, i.e., that they should attain full growth and come of age, until they reach the age of ashudd, which according to most scholars is forty years.

﴿And extract their treasure﴾, because it would remain beneath the wall; had the wall collapsed and fallen, the treasure would have been exposed and the people would have taken it.

He said: ﴿And beneath it was a treasure belonging to them, and their father was righteous﴾. It was part of Allah's gratitude toward this righteous father that his children be cared for, and this is from the blessing of righteousness in fathers: that Allah preserves their children.

﴿And their father was righteous, so your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity﴾. Here He did not say "so We intended" or "so I intended"; He said "your Lord intended", because the survival of the two boys until they reach maturity is of no concern to al-Khidr or Musa. Rather, the fear, the fear that ﴿he would burden them with tyranny and disbelief﴾, applies to Musa and al-Khidr, and the intention to damage the ship came from al-Khidr, who actually damaged it. But the matter of the two boys being raised in obedience to Allah, until they grow up and extract their treasure, is not something in which Musa or al-Khidr had any part.

﴿So your Lord intended that they should reach their maturity and extract their treasure﴾. From where? From beneath the wall.

﴿As a mercy from your Lord﴾: this is a object of purpose (maf'ul li-ajlihi) whose governing verb is (intended), meaning: Allah willed that, as a mercy from Him, may He be exalted.

﴿And I did not do it of my own accord﴾, meaning: I did not do this thing by my own cleverness or my own reason, but by inspiration from Allah, may He be exalted, and by His success, because this thing is beyond what human reason can grasp.

﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾. (Ta'wil) here means its explanation (tafsir), because at the beginning he said: ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation﴾, then he concluded with his saying: ﴿That is the interpretation﴾, i.e., the explanation. It is possible that what is meant by ta'wil here in the second instance is the outcome (al-'aqibah), meaning: that is the outcome of what you could not bear with patience, because ta'wil is used to mean outcome and it is also used to mean explanation.

As for His saying: ﴿what you could not﴾, and at the beginning He said: ﴿I will inform you of the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience﴾, the use of the two forms is because: istata'a and istaṭa'a, yastaṭee' and yasṭee', each of them is a correct Arabic dialect of the language.

﴿That is the interpretation of what you could not bear with patience.﴾ In this story there are many lessons. If you wished for each one of you to mention benefits from depicting it or witnessing it, do you have the capacity for that? For example, one takes the story from the time Musa, peace be upon him, set out until he rested by the rock and parted from it; then from his boarding the ship with al-Khidr and what al-Khidr did to the ship, and the explanation of the reason for that; then the boy; then the wall. That is four topics, and each one takes one topic.

Then Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And they ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn﴾ [al-Kahf 83]..

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Leave this for the researcher.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: (...) this is for the researcher.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: The whole story or only part of it?

* The student: Because, O Shaykh, Musa is in part of the story; because Musa is more knowledgeable than al-Khidr and more excellent than al-Khidr. He is the interlocutor of Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and one of the five Ulu al-'Azm. But the meaning of the story here is a test for Musa, based on what preceded in his speech. Allah informed al-Khidr of something, of killing the boy, and of damaging the ship, by way of the unseen; not (...) damaging the ship, killing the boy and the wall. That is, it is closest to the matter of the unseen, and the unseen is known only to Allah, may He be glorified and exalted.

* The Shaykh: Yes, this is what Allah informed him of, and Allah, may He be exalted, may inform some of the awliya' of the unseen.

* The student: But Musa, O Shaykh, is more excellent than him.

* The Shaykh: Even if he is more excellent, something may be hidden from Musa, and become clear to someone else. For example, now there are virtues among the Companions, some Companions have a virtue that did not come to Abu Bakr or 'Umar.

* The student: (...) In the saying of Allah, may He be exalted: ﴿So they found a servant from among Our servants, whom We had given mercy﴾. Could someone not say that the mercy here is the mercy of prophethood, as in the saying of Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿and has given me mercy from Him﴾ [Hud 28], and the saying of Salih, peace be upon him: ﴿and has given me mercy from Him﴾ [Hud 63]?

* The Shaykh: (...) This does not indicate that he was a prophet; rather he was a righteous man. Indeed, every righteous person, Allah, may He be exalted, has shown him mercy; ﴿And admit me by Your mercy among Your righteous servants﴾ [an-Naml 19]. Every righteous servant is shown mercy.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, he is closest to that if we say so: ﴿and taught him knowledge from Us﴾ (...) mercy is for everyone, yes.

* The student: What is the basis of al-Khidr's rebuke of Musa in his saying: ﴿He said: "Had you wished, you could have taken a wage for it"﴾? What (...) this was an offer to him, there is no rebuke, and he did not say (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, this includes rebuke. That is: ﴿Had you wished, you could have taken a wage for it﴾ is a gentle offer, but behind it is criticism.

* The student: In His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and taught him knowledge from Us﴾, some have used it as evidence for affirming "ladunni knowledge" (knowledge from the presence of Allah). What is the criterion for that?

* The Shaykh: No, we say: everything that a person cannot reach by himself is from Allah's presence, may He be exalted. As for what the Sufis say about "ladunni knowledge", that he says he was present with Allah last night, stayed up with Allah, and He gave me knowledge, and things like that, all of this is among their superstitions. Isn't that so?

* The student: They say so.

* The Shaykh: Yes, they say so.

* The student: Shaykh, regarding al-Khidr and the claim that he is still living (...)?

* The Shaykh: No, there is no doubt that al-Khidr died in his time. That is why no mention of him occurred with 'Isa, nor with other prophets, nor with Muhammad (ﷺ). Because if he were alive with the life of humans, it would have been obligatory upon him to believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), to come to him, and to join him in jihad. Also, the Prophet (ﷺ) said at the end of his life: "Verily, at the end of a hundred years, none of those who are upon the earth today will remain." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (564), and Muslim (2537/217), from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar.] No, he died in his time.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 83:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn﴾ [al-Kahf 18:83]. ﴿They ask you﴾: the wāw is the subject (fā'il) of the verb, referring to the people, whether from the Jews, from Quraysh, or from others.

﴿About Dhul-Qarnayn﴾: that is, about the possessor of the two horns (Dhul-Qarnayn). He was mentioned in history, and the Jews had said to Quraysh: "Ask him about this man; if he tells you about him, then he is a prophet."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: I will recite to you a remembrance of him﴾. That is, say to the one who asked you: ﴿I will recite﴾, I will read to you, ﴿a remembrance of him﴾, and not all of his remembrance, but a part of it; he is not all of his circumstances. Then Allah related the story.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 84:

﴿Indeed, We established him in the earth﴾ ﴿We established him﴾ means: We firmly settled him in the earth; this by the firmness of his dominion, the ease of his movement, and his strength.

﴿Indeed, We established him in the earth and gave him of every thing a means﴾ means: something by which he could reach his goal.

His saying ﴿of every thing﴾ does not encompass every thing; rather, what is meant is everything he needed. The proof of this is that "every thing" is according to what it is attributed to. You see that the hoopoe said to Solomon, peace be upon him, concerning the Queen of Sheba: what is it? ﴿She has been given of every thing﴾ [an-Naml 23], and it is well known that she was not given the heavens and the earth, but rather of every thing by which the completeness of kingship is achieved. Likewise Allah the Exalted said about the wind of 'Ad: ﴿It destroys everything﴾ [al-Ahqaf 25], and it is well known that it did not destroy everything; the dwellings were not destroyed, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾ [al-Ahqaf 25].

So here, ﴿and gave him of every thing a means﴾ means: of every thing by which establishment in the earth and the strength of authority are achieved, a means.

﴿So he followed a course⦆ — "fa-atba'a" means the same as "tabi'a" (to follow). That is, he (i.e., Dhul-Qarnayn) made use of the means that Allah Most High had given him; for among people there are those who make use of them and those who do not, but this king made use (he "followed a means") and traversed the earth.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 86:

﴿Until, when he reached the setting-place of the sun﴾, the place where it sets. ﴿He found it setting in a spring of murky water, and found near it a people.﴾

It is well known that what is meant is the place where the sun sets, which is the sea; for the one who travels toward the west will strike against what? Against the Ocean (al-Bahr al-Muhit), and when the observer sees the sun, he finds that it sets in it.

The bed of the sea ﴿hami'ah﴾ means: blackened by the water, for when water remains in the earth for a long time, it becomes black.

﴿He found it setting﴾ in this spring; and it is known that it sets in this muddy spring according to human sight. Otherwise, it is far larger than the earth, and far larger and greater than this muddy spring, and it revolves around the earth. But there is no harm in a person describing a thing according to how he sees it.

﴿He found it setting in a spring of murky water, and found near it﴾, i.e., near this muddy spring, which is the sea, ﴿a people. We said: O Dhul-Qarnayn, either punish them or treat them with kindness﴾ [al-Kahf 86]. That is: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, gave him the choice between punishing them by killing, or by other than killing, or doing good to them and treating them with kindness. This is because the man was a just king, a wise king; and what indicates his wisdom and his religion is that he said: ﴿As for him who does wrong, we shall punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment. But as for him who believes and does righteous deeds, he shall have a good reward, and we shall speak to him of Our command with ease﴾ [al-Kahf 87-88]. A just judgment.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 87:

﴿As for he who does wrong﴾ — and that is by shirk (associating partners with Allah), because the word "dhulm" (wrongdoing) is applied to shirk and to other things; but the apparent meaning, and Allah knows best, is that what is intended here is shirk, because of His saying: ﴿But as for he who believes and does righteous deeds﴾.

He says: ﴿As for he who does wrong, We will punish him﴾ — the punishment that is a ta'zir (discretionary punishment), and ta'zir punishment is left to the judgment of the ruler, whether by execution or by something else.

﴿Then he will be returned to his Lord﴾ — and He is Allah, Mighty and Majestic — ﴿and He will punish him with a terrible punishment﴾. This is because punishments do not purify disbelievers; a Muslim is purified by punishments, but a disbeliever is not. He is punished in this world and in the Hereafter; we seek refuge in Allah from that.

﴿A terrible punishment﴾ — is it "terrible" (nukr) to the one punishing, or is it "terrible" in that the one being punished finds it repugnant?

The second is the one that is determined, because the punishment of Allah is not repugnant in itself; rather it is truth and justice, but the one being punished finds it repugnant and regards it as severe.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 88:

﴿And as for whoever believes and does righteous deeds, he will have a reward of the best (al-husna)﴾, which is Paradise. ﴿And we will speak to him from Our command with ease﴾. The believer who does righteous deeds: he has a reward with whom? He has a reward with Allah, and it is Paradise, as the Exalted said: ﴿For those who did good is the best (al-husna) and an increase﴾ [Yunus 26]. The Prophet ﷺ explained it: that "al-husna" is Paradise, and "the increase" is looking at the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And we will speak to him from Our command with ease﴾. This believer who did righteous deeds, it will be said to him, regarding his affair or his command, a gentle word ﴿with ease﴾, meaning: what contains ease for him. So this one (the believer) and that one (the wrongdoer) were each promised two things. The wrongdoer was promised two things: that He would punish him, then he would be returned to Allah and He would punish him. And this one (the believer) was promised two things: that he has the best (al-husna), and that he is treated with the easiest (treatment).

But reflect on the state of the polytheist: he began with his punishment, then followed it with the punishment of Allah. The believer began with the reward of Allah first, then his being treated with ease second. The difference is evident, because what is the aim of the believer and the one who does righteous deeds? It is reaching Paradise. Reaching Paradise is undoubtedly better and more honorable than being told a gentle word. This indicates that this king is eloquent and eloquent, placing matters in their proper places.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verses 89–91:

﴿Then he followed a way (sabab)﴾ [Al-Kahf: 89, 90]. Subhan Allah! He first headed west, reaching the furthest point of the inhabited land that he could reach, then he returned to the east. Generally, a kingdom extends from east to west or from west to east, while north and south [are less significant]. For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah folded the earth up for me, so I saw its easts and its wests" [Reported by Muslim (2889/19) from the hadith of Thawban], without its north and south. This is because the north and south, as many people know, are not places for habitation; their farthest reaches to the north and south are all ice, with no inhabitants. The inhabitants follow the sun from east to west or from west to east.

﴿Until, when he reached the rising place of the sun﴾, meaning: the place where it rises.

﴿he found it rising over a people for whom We had made no shelter against it﴾, to the end of the verse. ﴿He found it rising over a people﴾ who had no buildings and no shady trees. Some scholars went so far as to say: nor did they have clothing, because clothing provides a kind of cover — but Allah knows best. The point is that the sun burns them, and they have no cover from it: no shady trees, no houses, no palaces.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning: the matter is as we have said, that is, the matter is exactly so, true in its reality.

﴿And We had full knowledge of what was with him﴾. Subhan Allah, meaning: We knew with certain knowledge what he possessed of the means of kingship and its extent, and all else that was with him. And Allah knows best.

* The student: The i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿jaza'an﴾ (as a reward).

* The Shaykh: It is a ḥāl (circumstantial accusative); meaning: "for them is the best reward, being a reward (jaza'an)."

* * *

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgement.

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And when Musa said to his servant (fata)﴾ — "I will not cease until I reach the meeting place of the two seas" [Al-Kahf: 60]. What is the grammatical position of ﴿idh﴾ (when)?

* The student: It is in the position of an accusative of time (ẓarf zamān).

* The Shaykh: What is its governing element (ʿāmil)?

* The student: It is omitted.

* The Shaykh: The implied element is "remember" (udhkur), because every adverbial phrase or prepositional phrase must have a governing element.

Regarding ﴿li-fatāhu﴾?

* The student: Yusha' ibn Nun.

* The Shaykh: Yes, his name is Yusha' ibn Nun. But what is "fata"?

* The student: His servant.

* The Shaykh: His servant. Regarding ﴿lā abraḥu ḥattā ablugha﴾, where is the predicate of ﴿lā abraḥu﴾?

* The student: It is omitted.

* The Shaykh: What is the implied element?

* The student: "I will not cease traveling."

* The Shaykh: "I will not cease traveling." Where is the place of the meeting of the two seas?

* The student: It is said that it is...

* The Shaykh: There are several opinions. But what is the closest?

* The student: At the junction of the two seas, the Mediterranean with the Red Sea.

* The Shaykh: Yes, at this place, this junction; this is the closest, because Musa was in Egypt.

What is the difference between the Khidr's first words to Musa, ﴿Did I not say that you would not be able to...﴾, and the second, where he said: ﴿Did I not tell you that you...﴾?

* The student: That Musa repeatedly asked...

* The Shaykh: But what is the difference between the two expressions: ﴿Did I not say, that you...﴾ and ﴿Did I not say to you﴾?

* The student: The first contains lightness; he rebuked him gently...

* The Shaykh: It is gentler reproach than the second, because he said: ﴿did I not say that you﴾, meaning: to you or to someone else, that you cannot... But when he states it explicitly, ﴿did I not say to you﴾, it has a harsher effect on Musa's soul and greater pain in the rebuke. Now, if I say to someone, "Did I not say that you did not do such-and-such," it is not a direct rebuke; it may be addressed to someone else. But ﴿Did I not say to you﴾ is a harsher reproach than the first.

Regarding the boy whom Khidr killed, out of fear of what?

* The student: Out of fear that he would affect his parents (...).

* The Shaykh: Yes. Now how can a child affect his parents?

* The student: By love, and by frequent association.

* The Shaykh: Yes, meaning they may have become very attached to him and loved him greatly, and such a thing could affect them.

Is Khidr a prophet?

* The student: He is not a prophet.

* The Shaykh: According to the preponderant opinion, he is neither a prophet nor a messenger.

* The student: He is a saint (waliy) and a righteous servant.

* The Shaykh: Yes. The more apparent view, and Allah knows best, is that he is a waliy, because these things are karamat (marvels granted to saints): he was honoured with this knowledge that Allah taught him.

* * *

Now we begin with Dhu al-Qarnayn. First: why was he called Dhu al-Qarnayn? ﴿And they ask you about Dhu al-Qarnayn﴾. We ask: why was he called Dhu al-Qarnayn?
It has been said its meaning is the one of wide dominion from east to west, for the east is a horn and the west is a horn, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "where the horn of Satan rises" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1037) and Muslim (2905/45), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar]. So this is a metaphor for what? For the breadth of his kingdom.

It has also been said that he was called Dhu al-Qarnayn for his strength; this is why a ram with horns is known to be stronger and more powerful. It has also been said that he was called so because he had two marks placed on his head like horns, like a crown of kings. The truth is that the Qur'an does not explain it, but what is closest to the Qur'an is that its meaning is the one who possessed the east and the west, and this fits perfectly, since the Prophet (ﷺ) said of the sun: "It rises between the two horns of Satan" [Reported by Muslim (832/294) from the hadith of Amr ibn Abasa al-Sulami].

﴿Say: I will recite to you from it a mention﴾. I think we took it up to? 

* The student: ﴿Then he followed a way﴾ (...).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verses 89–91:

﴿Then he followed a way (sabab)﴾ [Al-Kahf: 89, 90]. Subhan Allah! He first headed west, reaching the furthest point of the inhabited land that he could reach, then he returned to the east. Generally, a kingdom extends from east to west or from west to east, while north and south [are less significant]. * The student: ﴿Then he followed a way﴾ (...).
Shaykh: Yes. ﴿Then he followed a way﴾ means: he set out and took a means by which he could reach his aim.

﴿Until, when he reached between the two barriers﴾. The two barriers (al-saddayn) are two great mountains that stand between the eastern side of East Asia and the western side. They are two great mountains, but between them there is a passage through which people can pass. He reached between them, between the two barriers.

﴿He found beside them a people who could hardly understand any speech﴾. "Beside them" means: neither between them nor behind them. It has been said that they are the Turks (Turkiyya).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 94:

﴿They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn"﴾. In this verse there are two readings (qira'at): ﴿لَا يَكَادُونَ يُفْقِهُون قَوْلًا﴾ (*la yakadūna yufqihūna qawlan*) and ﴿لا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا﴾ (*la yakadūna yafqahūna qawlan*). The difference between them is clear. *Yafqahūna* (with the verb in the form that means "they understand") refers to the people themselves, while *yufqihūna* (with the causative form, meaning "they make others understand") refers to others. That is, they (the people of Yajuj and Majuj) do not understand the language of people, and people do not understand their language. This is the benefit of the two readings. Both readings are sound, and each carries a meaning different from the other. Taken together, they tell us that these people do not understand the language of people, and people do not understand their language: ﴿They hardly understand any speech﴾.

Here a problem arises. How can it say ﴿they hardly understand any speech﴾ and then report that they addressed Dhul-Qarnayn with clear and eloquent speech: ﴿They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn"﴾?

The answer to this is very easy. Allah the Exalted gave him a great kingdom, and he had translators through whom he could make known what he wanted and understand what others wanted. It may also be that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, inspired him with the language of all the peoples he ruled. The point is that they addressed Dhul-Qarnayn with clear speech.

﴿They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn"﴾: they addressed him by his title, as a sign of honor. ﴿Indeed, Yajuj and Majuj are corrupters in the land, so may we pay you a tribute on condition that you set up a barrier between us and them?﴾ and so on to the end of the verse.

﴿Yajuj and Majuj﴾: these are two tribes from the children of Adam, as this has been authentically reported from the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when he told the Companions that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say to Adam on the Day of Resurrection, "O Adam!" and he will say, "At Your service and at Your pleasure." Allah will say, "Bring forth from your progeny a contingent for the Fire." He will say, "O Lord, what is the contingent for the Fire?" He will say, "Out of every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine." This was grievous to the Companions, and they said, "O Messenger of Allah, which of us will be that one?" He said, "Rejoice, for you are among two peoples who never accompany anything without outnumbering it: Yajuj and Majuj."[[Reported by al-Tirmidhi (3169) from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Husayn.]]

From this we know the error of those who say that they are not in the form of human beings, that some of them are extremely short and some extremely tall, that some have an ear they spread out as a mat and an ear they wrap themselves in, and similar things. All of this is from the fabrications of the Children of Israel, and it is not permissible to believe it.

Rather, it is said that they are from the children of Adam, but they may differ as people differ according to their environments. For example, today you find that the people of the equatorial regions have an environment different from that of the northern peoples; each has its own environment. Those of the east today differ from the people of the center of the earth, and this may indeed be a difference. But that they should differ in a glaring way, as is mentioned, is not correct.

﴿Corrupters in the land﴾: How do they corrupt? Corruption in the land encompasses everything that is not righteous and not good. They corrupt it through killing, plundering, deviation, polytheism, and everything else. The point is that they need someone to protect them from these people.

﴿So may we pay you a tribute on condition that you set up a barrier between us and them﴾: that is, a barrier that prevents them from reaching us. They offered him something to give him, and this was an ill-considered judgment. But they feared that he might say "no," and that afterward they would be unable to do anything. Otherwise, how could they say to this king, who conquered the eastern and western parts of the earth, ﴿Shall we pay you a tribute on condition that you set up a barrier between us and them?﴾ This would only be said to someone who is unable to act. Rather, they said it out of fear that he would reject their request, and they wanted to establish the proof against him: that they had wished to give him something by which he would protect them from these people.

He replied: "What my Lord has established me in is better" (ma makkanni fihi rabbi khayr). Here "ma" is a subject (mubtada'), and "khayr" is its predicate (khabar al-mubtada'). The meaning is: what my Lord has established me in, of power, wealth, servants and everything else, is better than what? Better than this tribute you are offering me. This is like the statement of Sulayman, peace be upon him, concerning the gift of the Queen of Sheba, when he said: "Will you provide me with wealth? But what Allah has given me is better than what He has given you" (An-Naml 36). This is an acknowledgment by a person of the blessings of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, which make him need no one.

"He said: What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength" (fa-a'inuni biquwwah): with physical strength, not with money, because he already possessed a great deal of wealth.

"I will set up a barrier between you and them" (aj'al baynakum wa baynahum radman): that is, a barrier greater than what they asked for. They asked for a barrier (saddan), but he said "radman," meaning something stronger than a saddan.

Then he commanded them, "Bring me blocks of iron," and they gathered it for him. "Zubar" here means pieces of iron, so they gathered the iron and made it level with the mountains. This shows the great strength they had at that time, meaning that loads of iron were gathered until they equaled the towering great mountains.

﴿Until, when he had made it level between the two cliffs﴾, meaning the two sides of the mountains, ﴿he said, "Blow," ﴾, meaning: blow upon this iron. It is not meant with your mouths, because that is impossible; rather, blow with the machines and equipment they had, for Allah had given him a great kingdom, so they blew.

﴿Until, when he had made it a fire, he said, "Bring me molten copper that I may pour over it."﴾ It is well known that iron, when kindled in fire, becomes like fire; the piece becomes like a glowing ember, indeed even fiercer than an ember. Then he asked that they bring qitr, which he would pour over it. Qitr is melted copper, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We caused a fountain of molten copper to flow for him﴾ [Saba 12], meaning: copper, which Allah the Exalted caused to flow for Solomon, instead of being a hard ore that needs to be extracted with picks and then smelted in fire. No, Allah caused a fountain of qitr to flow for him as if it were water, glory be to Allah. This Dhul-Qarnayn said: ﴿Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper﴾, so they poured the molten copper over it, and the copper intermingled with the blocks of iron, so it became strong.

He says: ﴿So they were not able to scale it, nor could they make a hole in it.﴾ The two forms ﴿مَا اسْطَاعُوا﴾ and ﴿وَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا﴾ have the same meaning. It was mentioned earlier, in the story of Musa with al-Khidr, in the forms ﴿مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ﴾ and ﴿مَا لَمْ تَسْطِعْ﴾. ﴿فَمَا اسْطَاعُوا أَنْ يَظْهَرُوهُ﴾ means: they could not climb over it. Why? Because it is high, and because its surface is apparently smooth, so they are unable to climb it. ﴿وَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا لَهُ نَقْبًا﴾: here the tā' does not appear in the first verb, but it does appear in the second. An increase in the form indicates an increase in meaning. Which is harder: to climb the mountain, or to pierce this iron? The second is harder, and for this reason He said: ﴿وَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا لَهُ نَقْبًا﴾, because it is iron held together with copper. So they were unable to scale it, given its height and its apparent smoothness, and they were unable to make a hole in it, given its hardness and strength. Thus it became an impregnable barrier, and God sufficed the believers against the evil of these corrupters, Gog and Magog.

"Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 98:

﴿He said: "This is a mercy from my Lord."﴾ Who says this? Dhul-Qarnayn says it. Observe how the righteous servants of Allah do not attribute what they accomplish to themselves, but attribute it to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to His bounty. This is why, when an ant spoke when Sulayman came with his armies upon the valley of the ants, ﴿a small ant said﴾ [an-Naml 18], she stood up as an eloquent orator: ﴿"O ants, enter your dwellings, lest Sulayman and his soldiers crush you while they do not perceive."﴾ (18) ﴿So he smiled, laughing at her speech, and said, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness with which You are pleased, and admit me by Your mercy into the ranks of Your righteous servants."﴾ [an-Naml 18-19]. This was also Dhul-Qarnayn, may Allah have mercy on him, who said: ﴿"This is a mercy from my Lord"﴾, and it was not by my own power or strength, but it was a mercy from Him and a mercy toward those who asked him for a barrier, that this impregnable rampart came into being.

﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level; and ever is the promise of my Lord true.﴾ ﴿When the promise of my Lord comes﴾ means: by the emergence of these corrupters. ﴿He will make it level﴾, i.e., He will make this barrier dakk, meaning completely collapsed and leveled with the ground. And it is authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today an opening has been made in Ya'juj and Ma'juj like this," and he gestured with his index and middle fingers. [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3346) and Muslim (2880/1), from the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh.] That is, a small amount; but where the crack has appeared, it will inevitably widen.

He says: ﴿So when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and ever is the promise of my Lord true.﴾ So what is this promise? The promise is that Allah, glorified and exalted, will bring them out at the end of time, after the emergence and killing of the Dajjal. Allah will bring them out in a great multitude like locusts or more, to the extent that they will pass by the Lake of Tiberias and drink its water; the last of them will pass and say, "There was once water in this place one day." Then 'Isa, upon whom be peace, and those believers with him, will be besieged in Mount Tur, and hardship will befall them, and they will beseech Allah, exalted is He, to destroy these people. So Allah will send upon them a worm in their necks, and they will all die as a single man dies. In one night, despite their multitude, they will be dead as one man, until the earth stinks from their odor. Then Allah will send rains that carry them into the sea, or He will send birds that carry them to the sea, and Allah is over all things capable.

We believe in these matters as the Prophet ﷺ informed us, but as for how this state comes about, that is a matter for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿And ever is the promise of my Lord true﴾ means: the promise of Allah, exalted is He, regarding their emergence is true; it is true and must come to pass. Everything Allah has promised will certainly occur, because failure to fulfill a promise arises either from incapacity or from falsehood, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is free of both: of incapacity and of falsehood. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, does not break His appointed promise, owing to the perfection of His power and the perfection of His truthfulness. ﴿And ever is the promise of my Lord true﴾."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 99:

﴿And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another.﴾ ﴿We will leave some of them that day﴾. The exegetes whose statements I have seen say: ﴿that day﴾ means: when they come out, some of them will surge over others. Then they differed regarding the meaning of "surging over one another": does it mean that they surge along with the people, or that they push against one another when they come out of the barrier? If any of the scholars says that ﴿We will leave some of them that day surging over one another﴾ means that, after the barrier, they themselves surge over one another, then this is closer to the context of the verse. But what I have seen is that "they surge over one another" means: when they come out.

﴿We will leave some of them that day﴾ ﴿that day﴾ means: the day on which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wills their coming out.

﴿And they will surge over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering.﴾ ﴿The Horn will be blown﴾: the one who blows is Israfil (Israfil), one of the noble angels. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to open the night prayer with this supplication: "O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You judge between Your servants concerning that in which they differ. Guide me, by Your permission, to the truth in what they differ about, for You guide whom You will to a straight path."[[Recorded by Muslim (770/200) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] These three noble angels each is entrusted with that in which there is life: Jibril with that in which there is life of hearts, Mika'il with that in which there is life of plants, which is rain, and the third, Israfil, with that in which there is life of people at resurrection. He will blow into the Horn twice. The first blast is one of terror and swooning. We cannot now grasp the greatness of this blast, a blast that terrifies all creation and then makes them swoon; all of them will die except whomever Allah wills, because of the intensity of this blast and the severity of its impact. Now, if someone fired a cannon outside the mosque, what would happen? Would you be frightened or not? You would be frightened. Some years ago, on a Friday, the electricity cut off in the main mosque while people were waiting for the prayer, and there was a tremendous sound; they told us that the whole mosque was terrified and came out. Yes, this blast into the Horn is far more intense than anything we can imagine, for people will be terrified, indeed those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified, and then they will swoon. Allahu akbar! It is a tremendous matter; whatever a person imagines, his skin shivers at its greatness and its horror. So the Horn is blown.

The second blast: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then it will be blown again, and behold, they will be standing, looking on.﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. La ilaha illa Allah! At the second blast, people will rise from their graves alive, looking to see what has happened; for Allah sends down a great rain upon the bodies in the graves, and they grow within the earth until the bodies are complete. Then the blast of resurrection is blown into the Horn, and they stand up looking: ﴿and behold, they will be standing, looking on.﴾

﴿And the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them in a gathering﴾: (We will gather) whom? The creatures. ﴿A gathering﴾ means: a great gathering. This gathering includes mankind, jinn, angels, wild beasts and all creeping things. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies on its two wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected anything in the Book. Then to their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ [Al-An'am 38]. All creatures, even the angels of the heavens, as Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿And your Lord will come, and the angels, rank upon rank.﴾ [Al-Fajr 22]. What a tremendous scene! Allahu akbar.

He says: ﴿Then We will gather them in a comprehensive gathering. And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, exposed.﴾ [Al-Kahf 18:99–100] "O Allah, protect us from it!" "We will present it to them so that it is before them." ﴿Exposed (ʿarḍan)﴾ means: a tremendous exposure. That is why it is indefinite (nakkara); meaning, an exposure so great that hearts will fall away from it. And Allah's (Exalted and Majestic is He) telling us of this, do not think that these are merely historical stories. The purpose of it is that a person should put right what is between him and Allah, that he should fear this Day, that he should prepare for it, and that he should picture himself as if it were beneath his feet, as the Companion (al-Ṣiddīq) (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

Every man wakes up among his family,
while death is nearer to him than the strap of his sandal.

So picture this, and picture that there is nothing between you and it except that this soul leaves the body, and at that point everything ends.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 101:

﴿And We shall present Hell that Day to the disbelievers, plainly displayed, (100) those whose eyes were under a covering from My remembrance, and who were unable to hear.﴾ [al-Kahf: 100, 101] These disbelievers, their eyes were under a covering from the remembrance of Allah; they do not look at the remembrance of Allah. Allah the Most High has mentioned earlier in the same surah that there are coverings (akinnah) upon their hearts, so now the hearts, the sights and the hearing are all closed.

﴿وَكَانُوا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا﴾ Is the meaning "they are not willing," like the words of Allah the Most High: ﴿Can your Lord send down to us a table from the heaven?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 112], meaning "is He willing?" Or does the meaning mean that they are unable to hear the hearing of acceptance (sam' al-ijabah), and not the hearing of perception (sam' al-idrak)? This allows both, it allows both meanings, and both are true. ﴿And they were unable to hear.﴾

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 102:

﴿Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me?﴾ Meaning: Do those who disbelieve suppose that they can take My servants as protectors besides Me? Who are His servants? Everything is His servant: "There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant" [Maryam 93]. Who is it that is taken as a protector besides Allah, meaning: who is worshipped besides Allah?

The angels have been worshipped, the messengers have been worshipped, the sun has been worshipped, the moon has been worshipped, trees have been worshipped, stones have been worshipped, cows have been worshipped. We ask Allah for well-being; Satan comes to the son of Adam from every direction.

﴿That they take My servants as protectors besides Me﴾ meaning: as lords, whom they call upon and seek help from, forgetting the guardianship of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Meaning: do those who did this think that they will be given victory?

The answer: No, they will not be helped. Whoever thinks this is deranged in his mind. Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a hospitality (nuzul) for the disbelievers﴾. Meaning: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has readied the Fire as a ﴿nuzul﴾ for the disbelievers. The meaning of nuzul (hospitality) is what the host of a house provides to a guest; this is the nuzul. It may also mean a dwelling place (manzil), and both are correct. They will dwell in it, and they will be given it as though it were a hospitality, and what an evil hospitality it is. ﴿Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a hospitality for the disbelievers﴾.

Ibn 'Uthaymin's Commentary (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 18, verse 103:

﴿Say, "Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?"﴾ Meaning: Say, O Muhammad, to the whole community: ﴿Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds?﴾

The answer: Yes, we want to be informed about the greatest losers in deeds, so that we may avoid the deeds of those people and be among the successful. Allah the Exalted has made clear in Surah al-'Asr that every human being is in loss, except those who possess four qualities: ﴿Except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [al-'Asr 103:3].

The commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 104:

Here He says: ﴿Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good work.﴾ ﴿Whose effort is lost﴾ means: it is wasted and rendered void in the life of this world, yet they think that they are doing good work. Thus the truth is veiled from them—we seek refuge in Allah—and they suppose, while they are upon falsehood, that falsehood is the truth. This is common. For example, the Jews think they are upon the truth, the Christians think they are upon the truth, and the communists think they are upon the truth. Every one of them thinks that he is upon the truth; for this reason they remain upon what they are upon. And among them are those who know that they are not upon the truth, but—we seek refuge in Allah—because of their arrogance and self-exaltation, they persist in what they are upon.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 105:

﴿And they think that they are doing good work. (104) Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him, so their deeds have become worthless﴾ [al-Kahf: 104, 105] ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord﴾: are these the cosmic (kawniyyah) signs or the legislative (shar'iyyah) signs?

* The students: (...).

* The Shaykh: Apparently both, but those who denied the Messenger ﷺ denied the legislative signs and did not deny the cosmic signs. The evidence is that Allah, exalted is He, informed that when they are asked, "Who created the heavens and the earth?", they say, "Allah, Mighty and Majestic." None of them claims that there is a creator alongside Allah. But they denied the legislative signs: they denied the Messenger and denied what he brought, so they are included in the verse.

﴿And [in] meeting Him﴾, that is: they denied the meeting with Allah. And when does the meeting with Allah take place? It takes place on the Day of Resurrection. These people denied the Day of Resurrection, argued, were shown the signs, but persisted. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Does not man see that We created him from a sperm-drop, and then he is an open adversary? (77) And he presents for Us an example﴾ [Ya-Sin: 77, 78], denying Us regarding it, and said: ﴿Who will give life to bones while they are decayed?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 78], a challenge. Who will give them life? ﴿Decayed﴾: there is no life in them and nothing. He was answered: ﴿Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79]. Who produced them the first time? Allah. Allah will give them life, and repetition is easier than initiation, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him﴾ [ar-Rum: 27]. This is the evidence. So the proof of the possibility of resurrection and giving life to bones that are decayed is that Allah initiated them. When Zakariyya was given the glad tidings of a son, when he had reached extreme old age and his wife was barren, Allah said: ﴿He said, "So it will be. Your Lord says, 'It is easy for Me, and I had already created you before, when you were nothing.'"﴾ [Maryam: 9]. So He who created you before when you were nothing is able to grant you a child. Thus ﴿He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79] is the evidence.

﴿And He is Knowing of all creation﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79]. If He is Knowing of all creation, then it will not be difficult for Him to create what He wills. Who can prevent Him if He is knowing of all creation? No one can prevent Him. ﴿He who made for you from the green tree fire﴾ [Ya-Sin: 80]: a green tree from which fire comes out! Is this how it is with you?!

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: You do not know it?! The tree among you, the green tree, is struck with a flint and then sparks fire, and the Arabs knew this. So He who brings out this fire, which is hot and dry, from a moist, cold branch, meaning two things that are utterly opposite, is able to create a human being or to recreate these bones when they are decayed. How many proofs is this?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿He who produced them the first time, and He is Knowing of all creation (79). He who made for you from the green tree fire﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79, 80], then He confirmed this fire by His saying: ﴿and then you ignite from it﴾.

The fourth proof: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. The answer: ﴿Yes.﴾

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57]. So He who created the heavens and the earth in their greatness and magnitude is able to restore a part, which is nothing in comparison with the earth. What are you, O son of Adam, in comparison with the earth? Nothing. You were created from it; you are a part of it, a small part of it. So He who was able to create the heavens and the earth is able to create their likes.

﴿Yes﴾: Allah, exalted is He, said, answering Himself: ﴿Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. This is the fifth proof. ﴿Al-Khallaq﴾ is an intensive form; if you wish, make it a description, meaning that He is characterized by creating eternally and forever. It is an emphasis of His earlier saying: ﴿And He is the Creator, the Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81].

The sixth proof: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. He needs no workers, no builders, and no one. ﴿Be, and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It will be but one shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Ya-Sin: 53]: one word. ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. The seventh proof?

* A student: (...).

* The Shaykh: ﴿So exalted is He in whose hand is the realm of all things﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83]. ﴿All things﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83]. So in His hand is His dominion, exalted is He; He disposes as He wills. So we ask Him, exalted is He, to guide us to His straight path.

﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 83]. This is the eighth proof. It is a proof because, were it not for our return to Allah, exalted is He, our existence would be purposeless, and this contradicts wisdom. Consider the context of these eight proofs in this brief statement; despite that, they deny the meeting with Allah. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in meeting Him﴾.

In His saying ﴿in the signs of their Lord﴾ is a binding obligation upon them to believe in the signs, because His being their Lord, exalted is He, requires that they obey Him and believe in Him. But whoever has the word of punishment justly due against him will not believe.

﴿So their deeds have become worthless﴾: "become worthless" means they are nullified and they gain nothing from them. Even if the disbeliever does good, improves the roads, builds hostels, and gives charity to the poor, that does not benefit him. If Allah wills to reward him, He hastens his reward in this world; but in the Hereafter he has no share, we seek refuge in Allah. We ask Allah for protection and well-being, because his deeds have become worthless.

But does a deed become void merely by apostasy, or is a condition required? A condition is required, namely that he dies in his apostasy. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever of you reverts from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever, those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless﴾ [al-Baqarah: 217]. As for one who apostatizes and then Allah grants him the favor of returning to Islam, his good deeds prior to apostasy are restored to him.

﴿So We will not assign for them on the Day of Resurrection any weight﴾ [al-Kahf: 105], meaning: they have no value with Us and no weight, and this is a metaphor for the loss of their rank with Allah, exalted is He. It has been said that the meaning is "We will not weigh them," because weighing is only needed to determine which of the good or bad deeds outweigh, and the disbeliever has no deeds to be weighed. But the correct view is that deeds are all weighed. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿As for one whose scales are heavy (6), he will be in a pleasant life (7). But as for one whose scales are light (8), his refuge will be an abyss (9). And what can make you know what it is? (10) A fierce fire﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 6-11]. The weighing is established to show the proof against them. This matter has a difference of opinion; we will continue if we are able to mention the difference, and otherwise the books are in front of you.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 106:

﴿That is their recompense: Hell, because they disbelieved﴾ [al-Kahf: 106]. He means: that mentioned above, that no weight will be set up for them, and that their deeds will be rendered void.

﴿That is their recompense: Hell﴾: "Jahannam" is one of the names of the Fire. ﴿because they disbelieved﴾: the "ba" (ب) here indicates causation (lil-sababiyyah), and "ma" is a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah), so the sentence is to be read as "because of their disbelief."

﴿And they took My signs and My messengers in mockery﴾: His words ﴿and they took﴾ (wa-ittakhadhu) are coordinated with "kafaru" (they disbelieved), meaning: "because they disbelieved and took." So they, may God protect us, disbelieved, and their disbelief extended to others. They began to mock the signs and mock the messengers, and they did not confine themselves to disbelieving in God.

﴿And they took My signs and My messengers in mockery﴾: that is, a target of ridicule, at which they scoff. For this reason God, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in mockery﴾ [al-Anbiya': 36], and they say: ﴿Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger?﴾ [al-Furqan: 41]. The interrogative here (al-istifham) clearly expresses contempt: "Is this the messenger?" ﴿Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger? He had almost led us astray from our gods, had we not been steadfast in them﴾ [al-Furqan: 41-42]. We seek refuge with God: they boast that they stood firm for their gods and defended them.

Here, Mighty and Majestic, He says: ﴿And they took My signs and My messengers in mockery﴾.

Then he mentioned the reward of those who believed and did righteous deeds (may Allah make me and you among them). He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them will be the Gardens of Firdaws as a lodging﴾ [Al-Kahf 107]. In place of Hell being a lodging for the disbelievers, the Gardens of Firdaws become a lodging for the believers. But this is on two conditions: faith and righteous deeds. Faith has its seat in the heart, and righteous deeds have their seat in the limbs, though it may also refer to deeds of the heart such as reliance upon Allah (tawakkul), fear (khawf), turning in repentance (inabah), love (mahabbah), and the like.

The righteous deeds (al-salihat) are those that are sincerely for Allah and in conformity with the Sharia (shari'ah) of Allah. A deed cannot be righteous except with these two: sincerity to Allah, and conformity to the Sharia of Allah. So whoever associates others with Allah, his deed is not righteous, and whoever innovates, his deed is not righteous, and it is rejected upon him—neither the first, who was not sincere, nor the second, who did not follow. The evidence for this is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted, in the Hadith Qudsi: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in need of partners. Whoever does a deed in which he associates another with Me, I abandon him and his association." [Narrated by Muslim (2985/46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever does a deed that is not in accordance with our affair, it is rejected." [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697) and Muslim (1718/18) from the hadith of 'A'ishah.] That is, it is rejected upon him. Thus the righteous deed is that which combines two attributes: sincerity to Allah, and following the Sharia of Allah—pay attention—or the Messenger of Allah? The Sharia of Allah is better, unless by following the Messenger of Allah is meant the category (jins) rather than Muhammad (ﷺ), in which case yes; because believers from the people of Musa and the people of 'Isa are included in this. So: sincerity to Allah and conformity to the Sharia of Allah.

﴿Were for them the Gardens of Firdaws as a lodging﴾. ﴿Were for them﴾: Is the meaning of the "being" here a past existence, or is the intent to affirm that it is a lodging for them? Like His saying: ﴿And Allah was ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [An-Nisa 96]. We say: both are true. It was in Allah's knowledge a lodging for them, and it is a lodging for them in a definite sense; for "kana" (was) may be stripped of the meaning of time and intend affirmation.

﴿Were for them the Gardens of Firdaws as a lodging﴾. ﴿Gardens of Firdaws﴾: Is this an idafah of the described to its description, or is it because Firdaws is the highest of the gardens and the other gardens are beneath it? The apparent meaning is the second; because not all believers who do righteous deeds are all in Firdaws; rather they are in the gardens of Firdaws, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said about Firdaws: "It is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic," [Narrated by al-Bukhari (2790) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.] "the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise" means that Paradise is like a dome. And in it there is also a fourth attribute: "from it the rivers of Paradise gush forth."

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 108:

﴿كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ الْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلًا (١٠٧) خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ [الكهف: ١٠٧، ١٠٨] ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ means: forever, or not? Forever. There is no dispute about this among the Ahl as-Sunnah.

﴿لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا﴾ [al-Kahf 108] means: they do not seek ﴿عَنْهَا﴾ (away from it), i.e., in exchange for it, ﴿حِوَلًا﴾, i.e., a change (taḥawwul). Why? Because each one of them is content with the blessings he has, and each one does not see that anyone is more complete than him, and this is part of the completeness of the bliss. For example, if you were to stay in a lofty palace containing everything that delights the soul, but you saw that so-and-so's palace was greater than it, would your joy be complete? Whoever desires this world does not have complete joy, because he sees that others are better than him. But in Paradise—although people are in ranks—the lowest of them (and there is no lowest-ranked person among them) sees that no one is more blessed than him. This is the opposite of the people of the Fire, where each one of them thinks that no one is more severe than him, and that he is the most severe of them.

﴿لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا﴾ means: if it were said to one of them, "Would you like us to place you in a place other than your place?", he would say, "No." This is one of Allah's blessings upon a person: that he be content with what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given him, that he be at peace, and not be anxious. ﴿لا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 109:

﴿Say﴾ meaning: O Muhammad, ﴿if the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted﴾ [al-Kahf 109]. Glory be to Allah the Mighty. ﴿If the sea were ink﴾ meaning: ink with which the words of Allah are written.

﴿The sea would be exhausted﴾ before the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are exhausted, because He is the one who governs all affairs, and by the word "Be!" (kun) His speech never runs out. Rather, in another verse: ﴿And if whatever trees on earth were pens and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, were ink, the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman 27], meaning: even if they were pens, ﴿and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, [were ink], the words of Allah would not be exhausted﴾ [Luqman 27]. The sea would be exhausted and the pens would break, while the word of Allah remains, exalted is He.

Here He says: ﴿for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as a supplement﴾, meaning: an addition. Indeed the words of Allah do not run out. In this there is a clear text affirming the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿words﴾. The words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are both cosmic (kawniyyah) and legislative (shar'iyyah). The legislative are what He revealed to His messengers, and the cosmic are what His decree has determined: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin 82]. Everything is by His will. So He says to everything, "Be," and it is. Among His legislative words is what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to those other than messengers, like the words He revealed to Adam. Adam, peace be upon him, was a prophet but not a messenger, and Allah commanded him and forbade him. Are commands and prohibitions cosmic words or legislative words? They are legislative words.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 18, verse 110:

﴿And if We were to bring the like of it as additional help (109). Say: "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your god is but one God."﴾ [al-Kahf 109, 110] Meaning: Announce to the assembly that you are not an angel, and that you are of the human species.

﴿I am only a human being like you﴾: The mention of likeness is to establish humanity, meaning that he is a human being who does not go beyond humanity. For this reason, the Prophet (ﷺ) would become angry as people become angry, did he not? He (ﷺ) would fall ill as people fall ill, he would feel hunger as people feel hunger, he would feel thirst as people feel thirst, he would guard against heat as people guard against it, he would guard against the arrows of battle as people guard against them, and he would forget as people forget. All of human nature is established for the Messenger (ﷺ), and he had a shadow as people have shadows.

As for the one who claims that the Messenger (ﷺ) was luminous and had no shadow, this is undoubtedly a lie. The Messenger (ﷺ), like other humans, had a shadow, and he himself would seek shade. Had the Messenger (ﷺ) had no shadow, this would have been transmitted by mass transmission (mutawatir), because it is one of the signs of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

So the Messenger (ﷺ) is a human being like people. Can the Messenger (ﷺ) bring benefit or harm to people? No, as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to say: ﴿Say: "I do not possess for you any harm or any right guidance."﴾ [al-Jinn 21]. It is strange that there are still groups of people who cling to the Messenger (ﷺ) more than they cling to Allah — we seek refuge in Allah — when the Messenger is mentioned their skins shiver, but when Allah is mentioned it is as if He were not mentioned. Some of them prefer to swear by the Messenger rather than swear by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and some of them consider visiting the grave of the Messenger (ﷺ) better than visiting the Ka'bah. I have witnessed people who were prevented from going to Madinah in the days of Hajj because the time of Hajj was near, since when the time of Hajj approaches they are prevented from going to Madinah so that they do not miss the Hajj. He weeps, saying: "I was prevented from the lights, and I was prevented from such and such," and enumerates what I have now forgotten. Fine, you have come for what? He says: "I came to see the lights," as if he had come only to visit Madinah, and forgot that he had come for Hajj, to perform one of the obligations of Hajj. The cause of that is ignorance, because the scholars do not explain to the common people; otherwise the layman has a surging emotion, and if he were told the truth he would return to it.

He says: ﴿it is revealed to me﴾. This is the distinction of the Messenger (ﷺ), that it is revealed to him, and no one else is revealed to except his brethren among the messengers. He says: ﴿it is revealed to me that your god is but one God﴾. ﴿That your god is but one God﴾: this sentence is a restriction (hasr), as if he said: "There is no god for you except One." From where have we derived the restriction? From (innama), because the word (innama) is one of the particles of restriction. You say: "Innama Zayd is standing," meaning he has no attribute other than standing. And you say: "Innama al-'ilm bi-l-ta'allum" (knowledge is only by learning), meaning there is no path to knowledge except by learning. ﴿That your god is but one God; so whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾, meaning: hopes and expects to meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and believes in that, ﴿let him do righteous deeds﴾, meaning: a simple, easy call. Do you wish to meet your Lord while your heart is full of hope? If that is the case, ﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾. Every sensible person who hopes to meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and the meeting with Allah is not far off. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah, then indeed the term of Allah is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-'Ankabut 5]. Some scholars said that His saying: ﴿indeed the term of Allah is coming﴾ [al-'Ankabut 5] has the meaning of their saying: "Everything that is coming is near." ﴿So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾.

If someone says: Have you not established that righteous deeds must include sincerity (ikhlas) and following the Sunnah (mutaba'ah)? We say: Yes, but since sincerity is of great importance, it was singled out after being included in His saying: ﴿let him do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾. Reflect on His saying: ﴿in the worship of his Lord﴾, so that it becomes clear to you that He, the Majestic and Exalted, is worthy that none be associated with Him, because He is the Lord, the Creator, the Owner, the Governor of all affairs.

We say with our hearts and tongues: Our Lord is Allah, and we ask Allah, the Exalted, for steadfastness, so that we enter into the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who say: "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Garden which you were promised."﴾ [Fussilat 30].

In any case, praise be to Allah who enabled us to complete this surah. In truth, our shaykh 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'di (may Allah have mercy on him) has in this very surah abundant and great benefits that you will not find in any other book. He mentioned great benefits in the story of Musa and al-Khidr, which the student of knowledge should review, because they are extremely beneficial.
